title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第十九: 高允 高祐 盧曹
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 19: Gao Yun, Gao Yu, Lu Cao
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第十九: 高允 高祐 盧曹 Volume 31 Biographies 19: Gao Yun, Gao Yu, Lu Cao

sentences.zh: 高允 高祐 盧曹

translations.literal: Gao Yun, Gao You, Lu Cao
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun, Gao You, and Lu Cao

sentences.zh: 列傳第十九

translations.literal: Biographies 19
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 19

sentences.zh: 高允從祖弟祐祐曾孫德正祐從子乾昂季式

translations.literal: Gao Yun's second cousin once removed You; You's great-grandson Dezheng; You's grandnephews Qian, Ang, and Jishi
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun; his second cousin once removed Gao You; You's great-grandson Dezheng; and You's grandnephews Qian, Ang, and Jishi

sentences.zh: 高允，字伯恭，勃海蓚人，漢太傅裒之後也。

translations.literal: Gao Yun, styled Bogong, was a native of Liaoxian in Bohai and a descendant of Gao Yuan, Grand Tutor of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun, courtesy name Bogong, came from Liaoxian in Bohai and traced his line to Gao Yuan, Grand Tutor of Han.

sentences.zh: 曾祖慶，慕容垂司空。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qing served Murong Chui as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qing had been Minister of Works under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 祖父泰，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tai was Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tai had held the post of Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 父韜，少以英朗知名，同郡封懿雅相推敬。

translations.literal: His father Tao was famed in youth for brilliance and openness; Feng Yi of the same commandery greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao won early renown for brilliance and candor, and Feng Yi of the same commandery held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 亦仕慕容垂，為太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: He also served Murong Chui as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Tao likewise served Murong Chui as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 道武平中山，以為丞相參軍，早卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, he was made a staff officer to the Chancellor and died young.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu conquered Zhongshan, Tao was appointed a staff officer to the Chancellor but died while still young.

sentences.zh: 允少孤夙成，有奇度，清河崔宏見而異之，歎曰：「高子黃中內潤，文明外照，必為一代偉器，但吾恐不見耳。

translations.literal: Yun was orphaned early yet matured quickly and had an extraordinary capacity; Cui Hong of Qinghe saw him and was struck with wonder, sighing: "Master Gao is golden at the core and lustrous without—surely he will be a great vessel of his age, though I fear I shall not live to see it."
translations.idiomatic: Yun lost his parents young yet showed precocious judgment and unusual breadth of mind. Cui Hong of Qinghe met him and marveled, saying, "Master Gao has gold within and light without—he is bound to become a pillar of his generation, though I doubt I shall live to see it."

sentences.zh: 」年十餘歲，祖父泰喪，還本郡。

translations.literal: In his teens, when his grandfather Tai died, he returned to his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his teens he went home to his commandery for his grandfather Tai's funeral.

sentences.zh: 允推財與二弟而為沙門，名法淨，未久而罷。

translations.literal: Yun turned over the family property to his two younger brothers and became a monk under the name Fajing, but before long he left the order.
translations.idiomatic: Yun gave the estate to his two younger brothers, took monastic vows as Fajing, and soon afterward returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 性好文學，擔笈負書，千里就業。

translations.literal: He loved literature by nature and carried books in a satchel a thousand li to pursue his studies.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved letters and traveled a thousand li with books on his back to study.

sentences.zh: 博通經史、天文、術數，尤好《春秋公羊》。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics and histories, astronomy, and numerology, and was especially fond of the Gongyang Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He gained a thorough command of the classics and histories, astronomy, and numerology, above all the Gongyang Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 曾作《塞上公詩》，有混欣戚、遺得喪之致。

translations.literal: He once wrote "The Hermit on the Frontier," which blended joy and sorrow and transcended gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed "The Lord on the Frontier," a poem that mingled joy and grief and left behind both gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 神蒨三年，太武舅陽平王杜超行征南大將軍，鎮鄴，以允為從事中郎，年四十餘矣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenqi, the emperor's maternal uncle the Prince of Yangping, Du Chao, served as General Who Pacifies the South and garrisoned Ye; he appointed Yun Attendant-in-Ordinary—Yun was then over forty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenqi, Emperor Taiwu's uncle by marriage, the Prince of Yangping Du Chao, marched south as generalissimo and encamped at Ye, taking Yun as Attendant-in-Ordinary; Yun was already past forty.

sentences.zh: 超以方春而諸州囚不決，表允與中郎呂熙等分詣諸州，共評獄事。

translations.literal: Because it was spring yet prisoners in the provinces still had no verdicts, Chao memorialized that Yun, with Palace Gentleman Lü Xi and others, should go to the various provinces jointly to review cases.
translations.idiomatic: It was spring, yet prisoners in the provinces still awaited judgment, so Chao sent Yun with Palace Gentleman Lü Xi and others to tour the provinces and adjudicate cases together.

sentences.zh: 熙等皆以貪穢得罪，唯允以清平獲賞。

translations.literal: Xi and the others were all punished for greed and corruption; only Yun was rewarded for fairness and rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and the rest were all convicted of graft, while Yun alone was commended for clean and even-handed conduct.

sentences.zh: 府解，還家教授，受業者千餘人。

translations.literal: When his office ended, he returned home to teach; more than a thousand students came to him.
translations.idiomatic: After his term he went home to instruct disciples, and more than a thousand students followed him.

sentences.zh: 四年，與盧玄等俱被征，拜中書博士，遷侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned with Lu Xuan and others, appointed Academic Language of the Secretariat, and promoted to Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was called up with Lu Xuan and others, made Academic Language of the Secretariat, and later promoted to Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 與太原張偉並以本官領衛大將軍樂安王範徒事中郎。

translations.literal: With Zhang Wei of Taiyuan he held the same office as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Collected Corps Lieutenant General, the Prince of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Wei of Taiyuan both served in their original posts as attendants to the Prince of Le'an, who held the rank of Collected Corps Lieutenant General.

sentences.zh: 范，太武寵弟，西鎮長安，允甚有匡益，秦人稱之。

translations.literal: Fan was a favored younger brother of Emperor Taiwu and held the western garrison at Chang'an; Yun greatly aided and corrected him, and the people of Qin praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was a cherished younger brother of Emperor Taiwu and commanded the west from Chang'an; Yun gave him much sound counsel, and the people of Qin praised Yun.

sentences.zh: 尋被征還。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 樂平王丕西討上邽，復以本官參丕軍事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Le'ping, Pi, campaigned west against Shanggui; Yun again served on Pi's staff in his original office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Le'ping Pi marched west against Shanggui, Yun again joined his headquarters in the same capacity.

sentences.zh: 以謀平涼州之勳，賜爵汶陽子。

translations.literal: For merit in the plan to pacify Liang Province, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in the pacification of Liang Province he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 後奉詔領著作郎，與司徒崔浩述成國記。

translations.literal: Later he received an edict to head the office of Compiler and, with Minister of Works Cui Hao, completed the National Chronicle.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict made him head Compiler, and with Minister of Works Cui Hao he finished the National Chronicle.

sentences.zh: 時浩集諸術士，考校漢元以來，日月薄蝕，五星行度，並譏前史之失，別為魏曆以示允。

translations.literal: At that time Hao gathered technologists to examine solar and lunar eclipses and the courses of the five planets since the Han Yuan reign period, found fault with the former histories, and drew up a Wei calendar to show Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then assembled experts to check eclipses and the motions of the five planets from the Yuan reign of Han onward, criticized the old histories, and prepared a Wei calendar to present to Yun.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「善言遠者，必先驗於近。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Those who speak well of the distant must first test it against the near."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Anyone who speaks confidently of remote times must first verify his claims against what is near at hand."

sentences.zh: 且漢元年冬十月，五星聚于東井，此乃曆術之淺事。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the tenth month of winter of the first year of Han, the five planets gathered in the Well—this is elementary calendar lore.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the gathering of the five planets in the Well in the tenth month of the first year of Han is a matter every calendarist knows.

sentences.zh: 今譏漢史而不覺此謬，恐後之譏今，猶今之譏古。

translations.literal: Now you rebuke Han history without seeing this error—perhaps later men will rebuke us as we today rebuke the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: You fault the Han historians yet miss this mistake—later ages may fault us just as we fault them today."

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「所謬云何？

translations.literal: Hao said: "What is the error?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked, "What mistake do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」允曰：「案《星傳》，金、水二星，常附日而行，冬十月，日旦在尾、箕，昏沒于申南，而東井方出於寅北，二星何因背日而行？

translations.literal: Yun said: "According to the Canon of Stars, Venus and Mercury habitually follow the sun. In the tenth month of winter, at dawn the sun is in the Tail and Basket; at dusk it sets south of Shen, while the Well has just risen north of Yin—how could the two planets travel against the sun?
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "The Canon of Stars tells us that Venus and Mercury normally keep with the sun. In the tenth month, at dawn the sun stands in the Tail and Basket; at dusk it sets south of Shen, while the Well is only rising north of Yin—how could two planets run counter to the sun?"

sentences.zh: 是史官欲神其事，不復推之於理。

translations.literal: The historians wished to make the affair miraculous and no longer weighed it by reason."
translations.idiomatic: The clerks wanted to magnify the omen and stopped reasoning from the pattern of the heavens."

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「欲為變者，何所不可？

translations.literal: Hao said: "When one wishes to bring about a change, what may not be done? You alone do not doubt the gathering of three stars yet find it strange that two came."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "If heaven means to show a portent, what is impossible? You do not question three stars gathering, yet you balk at two appearing."

sentences.zh: 君獨不疑三星之聚，而怪二星之來。

translations.literal: Yun said: "This cannot be argued in empty words; it should be examined further."
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "That will not do in bare disputation—we must look into it again."

sentences.zh: 」允曰：「此不可以空言爭，宜更審之。

translations.literal: At the time all present were astonished; only You Ya, Junior Tutor of the Eastern Palace, said: "Master Gao is skilled in calendrical reckoning; his words will not be empty."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present was startled; only You Ya, Junior Tutor of the Eastern Palace, said, "Master Gao excels at calendrical science—he will not speak idly."

sentences.zh: 」時坐者咸怪，唯東宮少傅遊雅曰：「高君長於曆，當不虛言也。

translations.literal: More than a year later Hao said to Yun: "What we argued before I did not take to heart; on examining it again, it is indeed as you said.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Hao told Yun, "Our earlier dispute I had not really weighed; when I looked into it again, it was exactly as you said.

sentences.zh: 」後歲餘，浩謂允曰：「先所論者，本不經心，及更考究，果如君語。

translations.literal: It was the third month, not the tenth, when they gathered in the Well."
translations.idiomatic: The planets met in the Well in the third month, not the tenth."

sentences.zh: 以前三月聚于東井，非十月也。

translations.literal: He also told Ya: "Gao Yun's art is like Yang Yuan's archery."
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Ya, "Gao Yun's skill is like Yang Yuan's bowmanship."

sentences.zh: 」又謂雅曰：「高允之術，陽源之射也。

translations.literal: He also told Ya, "Gao Yun's art is Yang Yuan's archery."
translations.idiomatic: He also told You Ya, "Gao Yun's mastery is like Yang Yuan's skill with the bow."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃嘆服。

translations.literal: The assembly then sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At that the whole assembly sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 允雖明于歷數，初不推步有所論說。

translations.literal: Although Yun was clear in calendrical reckoning, at first he never undertook prognostication or offered any discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Though Gao Yun was masterful in calendrical science, he at first never performed calculations or offered opinions on such matters.

sentences.zh: 惟遊雅數以災異問允。

translations.literal: Only You Ya repeatedly questioned Yun about portents and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Only You Ya kept pressing Yun with questions about omens and calamities.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「昔人有言，知之甚難。

translations.literal: Yun said, "In antiquity someone said that to know is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Men of old remarked that knowing is hard indeed.

sentences.zh: 既知，復恐漏泄，不如不知也。

translations.literal: Once one knows, one again fears leakage; it is better not to know.
translations.idiomatic: Once you know, you fear letting it slip—better not to know at all.

sentences.zh: 天下妙理至多，何遽問此。

translations.literal: Subtle principles under Heaven are exceedingly many—why hurry to ask this?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's subtle truths are endless—why fix on this?"

sentences.zh: 」雅乃止。

translations.literal: Ya then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya said no more.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官為秦王翰傅。

translations.literal: Soon, in his existing office, he became tutor to Prince Han of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made tutor to Prince Han of Qin while retaining his present post.

sentences.zh: 後敕以經授景穆，甚見禮待。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to impart the classics to Jingmu and was greatly honored and well treated.
translations.idiomatic: Later the throne ordered him to teach the classics to Crown Prince Jingmu, who treated him with the highest respect.

sentences.zh: 又詔允與侍郎公孫質、李靈、胡方回共定律令。

translations.literal: The throne also ordered Yun, together with Gentlemen-in-Attendance Gongsun Zhi, Li Ling, and Hu Fanghui, jointly to establish laws and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also charged Yun, together with Gentlemen of the Palace Gongsun Zhi, Li Ling, and Hu Fanghui, to draft laws and regulations.

sentences.zh: 太武引允與論刑政，言甚稱旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu drew Yun to discuss criminal administration; his words greatly matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu summoned Yun to discuss punishments and governance, and Yun's counsel pleased him deeply.

sentences.zh: 因問允「萬機何者為先」。

translations.literal: He then asked Yun, "Among the myriad affairs of state, which comes first?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Yun, "Of all the business of empire, what should come first?"

sentences.zh: 時多禁封良田，又京師遊食眾。

translations.literal: At the time many fertile fields were under prohibition and sealed off, and there were many idlers eating without labor in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time fertile lands were widely sealed from cultivation, and the capital swarmed with idle dependents.

sentences.zh: 允因曰：「臣少也賤，所知唯田，請言農事。

translations.literal: Yun therefore said, "Your servant was lowly in youth; what he knows is only agriculture—permit me to speak of farming affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yun answered, "I was born to humble station and know only the fields. May I speak of agriculture?

sentences.zh: 古人云：方一里則為田三頃七十畝，方百里則田三萬七千頃。

translations.literal: The ancients said: within a square li there are three hundred seventy mu of fields; within a square hundred li there are thirty-seven thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that a square li holds three hundred seventy mu of cropland, and a square hundred li holds thirty-seven thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 若勸之，則畝益三升；

translations.literal: If one encourages farming, then per mu there is an increase of three sheng;
translations.idiomatic: If the state encourages farming, each mu yields three sheng more;

sentences.zh: 不勸，則畝損三升。

translations.literal: if one does not encourage it, then per mu there is a decrease of three sheng.
translations.idiomatic: if it does not, each mu loses three sheng.

sentences.zh: 方百里損益之率，為粟二百二十二萬斛，況以天下之廣乎？

translations.literal: For a square hundred li, the rate of gain or loss is two million two hundred twenty thousand hu of grain—how much more when one reckons the breadth of all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Across a square hundred li, the swing amounts to two million two hundred twenty thousand hu of grain—what then for the whole realm?

sentences.zh: 若公私有儲，雖遇饑年，復何憂乎？

translations.literal: If public and private stores exist, though a famine year comes, what worry is there?
translations.idiomatic: If both the state and the people keep grain in store, even in famine there is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」帝善之，遂除田禁，悉以授百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; he thereupon lifted the field prohibition and granted all to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved. He abolished the ban on cultivation and opened all such lands to the people.

sentences.zh: 初，崔浩薦冀、定、相、幽、并五州士數十人，各起家為郡守。

translations.literal: Initially Cui Hao recommended several tens of scholars from the five provinces Ji, Ding, Xiang, You, and Bing; each began his career as a prefectural administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cui Hao had recommended several dozen men of learning from Ji, Ding, Xiang, You, and Bing; each had taken his first office as a prefectural chief.

sentences.zh: 景穆謂誥曰：「先召之人，亦州郡選也，在職已久，勤勞未答。

translations.literal: Jingmu said to Hao, "Those summoned before were also provincial selections; they have served long in office, and their labor has gone unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jingmu told Hao, "The men you called up earlier were provincial appointees too. They have served a long while without reward for their diligence.

sentences.zh: 今可先補前召，外任郡縣；

translations.literal: Now one may first fill the posts of the previous summons with external appointments to commanderies and counties;
translations.idiomatic: Fill the earlier cohort first with county and commandery posts abroad;

sentences.zh: 以新召者代為郎吏。

translations.literal: let those newly summoned replace them as clerks in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and let the new men take their places as secretarial clerks."

sentences.zh: 又守令宰人，宜使更事者。

translations.literal: Moreover prefects, magistrates, and local heads should be men who have already served and gained experience.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and local chiefs, too, ought to be men with prior experience."

sentences.zh: 」浩固爭而遣之。

translations.literal: Hao obstinately contended and dispatched them anyway.
translations.idiomatic: Hao stubbornly objected and sent the new appointees out all the same.

sentences.zh: 允聞之，謂東宮博士管恬曰：「崔其不免乎！

translations.literal: When Yun heard of it, he told the Eastern Palace academician Guan Tian, "Will Cui not be ruined?
translations.idiomatic: When Yun heard this, he told the Eastern Palace academician Guan Tian, "Surely Cui cannot escape ruin.

sentences.zh: 苟逞其非而校勝於上，何以能濟？

translations.literal: If one indulges one's error and measures victory against one's superiors, how can one succeed?
translations.idiomatic: When a man insists on his own way and tries to best his betters, how can he endure?"

sentences.zh: 遼東公翟黑子有寵于太武，奉使并州，受布千疋。

translations.literal: Duke Liaodong Zhai Heizi had favor with Emperor Taiwu; on a mission to Bingzhou he accepted a thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Liaodong Zhai Heizi enjoyed Emperor Taiwu's favor. On a mission to Bing Province he had accepted a thousand bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 事發，黑子問允：「主上問我，首乎？

translations.literal: When the matter broke, Heizi asked Yun, "When the sovereign questions me, shall I confess first?
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, Heizi asked Yun, "When the emperor questions me, should I confess at once?

sentences.zh: 諱乎？

translations.literal: Or shall I conceal it?"
translations.idiomatic: Or should I hide it?"

sentences.zh: 」允曰：「公幃幄寵臣，答詔宜實。

translations.literal: Yun said, "You, sir, are a favored intimate within the curtains of state; in answering the edict you should be truthful.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "You are a trusted confidant at the inner court. When you reply to the throne, speak the truth."

sentences.zh: 」中書侍郎崔鑒、公孫質等咸言宜諱之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the Secretariat Cui Jian, Gongsun Zhi, and others all said he should conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Gentleman Cui Jian, Gongsun Zhi, and the rest all urged him to lie.

sentences.zh: 黑子以鑒等為親己，怒而絕允，而不以實對，終獲罪戮。

translations.literal: Heizi, taking Jian and the others as on his side, grew angry, broke with Yun, and did not answer truthfully; in the end he suffered punishment and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Heizi took Jian and the others for friends, turned on Yun in anger, and lied to the emperor. In the end he was punished and put to death.

sentences.zh: 時著作令史閔湛、郤舣性巧佞，為崔浩信待。

translations.literal: At the time Recording Official Min Zhan and Xi Yi were clever and flatterers; they were trusted and favored by Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the recording clerks Min Zhan and Xi Yi were clever flatterers in whom Cui Hao placed great trust.

sentences.zh: 見浩所注《詩》、《書》、《論語》及《易》，遂上疏言馬、鄭、王、賈不如浩之精微，請收藏境內諸書，班浩所注。

translations.literal: Seeing Hao's commentaries on the Classic of Poetry, the Documents, the Analects, and the Changes, they submitted a memorial saying that Ma Rong, Zheng Xuan, Wang Bi, and Jia Kui were not as subtle as Hao; they requested that all books within the realm be collected and Hao's commentaries circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Having seen Hao's commentaries on the Poetry, Documents, Analects, and Changes, they memorialized that the work of Ma, Zheng, Wang, and Jia could not match Hao's refinement, and asked that every book in the realm be gathered and Hao's versions made the standard.

sentences.zh: 並求敕浩注《禮》、《傳》。

translations.literal: They also requested an edict that Hao annotate the Records of Ritual and the Zuozhuan.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked that Hao be commanded to annotate the Ritual Canon and the Zuozhuan.

sentences.zh: 浩亦表薦湛有著述才。

translations.literal: Hao also submitted a memorial recommending that Zhan had talent for authorship.
translations.idiomatic: Hao in turn recommended Zhan as a man of literary talent.

sentences.zh: 湛等又勸浩刊所撰國史于石，以彰直筆。

translations.literal: Zhan and the others also urged Hao to carve the national history he had compiled on stone, to manifest the straight brush.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and the others also pressed Hao to have the dynastic history he had compiled cut into stone, to display the historian's honest pen.

sentences.zh: 允聞之，謂著作郎宗欽曰：「閔湛所營分寸之間，恐為崔門萬世之禍，吾徒無類矣。

translations.literal: When Yun heard of it, he told the Authoring Gentleman Zong Qin, "In the inches that Min Zhan manages, I fear there will be calamity for the Cui house for ten thousand generations; our sort will perish without survivors.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun heard of this, he told the Authoring Gentleman Zong Qin, "In the petty schemes Min Zhan is hatching I see disaster for the House of Cui for generations—none of us may escape.

sentences.zh: 」未幾而難作。

translations.literal: Before long calamity broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the trouble erupted.

sentences.zh: 初，浩之被收，允直中書省。

translations.literal: Initially, when Hao was taken into custody, Yun was directly at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was first arrested, Yun was on duty in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景穆使召允，留宿宮內。

translations.literal: Jingmu sent to summon Yun and kept him lodging within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jingmu sent for Yun and had him stay overnight in the palace.

sentences.zh: 翌日，命驂乘至宮門，謂曰：「入當見至尊，吾自導卿，脫至尊有問，但依吾說。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered him to ride in the carriage beside him to the palace gate, and said to him, "On entering you will see the sovereign; I myself will guide you. If the sovereign should question you, follow what I say.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he had Yun ride beside him to the palace gate and said, "When you enter and face the sovereign I will guide you. If he questions you, say only what I tell you.

sentences.zh: 」既入見，景穆言允小心慎密，且微賤，制由於浩，請赦之。

translations.literal: Once they had entered and been received, Jingmu said that Yun was careful and discreet, and moreover of humble rank; his work had been dictated by Hao—he requested clemency.
translations.idiomatic: After they entered, Jingmu told the emperor that Yun was cautious and lowly in station, that Hao had dictated his part in the work, and asked that he be spared.

sentences.zh: 帝召允謂曰：「國書皆浩作不？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yun and said to him, "Were the national annals entirely Hao's work?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Yun forward and asked, "Was the entire national history Hao's doing?

sentences.zh: 」允曰：「《太祖記》，前著作郎鄧彥海所撰；

translations.literal: Yun said, "The Annals of the Founding Emperor was composed by the former Authoring Gentleman Deng Yanhai;
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "The Annals of the Founding Emperor was the work of the former Authoring Gentleman Deng Yanhai;

sentences.zh: 《先帝記》及《今記》，臣與浩同作，然而臣多於浩。

translations.literal: The Annals of the Late Emperor and the Present Annals, your servant and Hao composed together—yet your servant contributed more than Hao.
translations.idiomatic: the Annals of the Late Emperor and the Present Annals were written by Hao and myself together—and I wrote more than Hao."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒曰：「此甚于浩，安有生路？

translations.literal: The emperor grew greatly enraged and said, "This is worse than Hao—where is there a path to life?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage. "This is worse than Hao! What hope of life is there for you?

sentences.zh: 」景穆曰：「天威嚴重，允迷亂失次耳。

translations.literal: Jingmu said, "Imperial majesty is grave; Yun was confused and lost his order of words.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmu said, "Your Majesty's awe is overwhelming. Yun spoke out of confusion.

sentences.zh: 臣向問，皆云浩作。

translations.literal: When I questioned him earlier, he all said Hao did it."
translations.idiomatic: When I questioned him before, he said Hao had written it all."

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「如東宮言不？

translations.literal: The emperor asked, "Is it as the Eastern Palace said?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Is it as the Crown Prince says?

sentences.zh: 」允曰：「臣罪應滅族，不敢虛妄。

translations.literal: Yun said, "Your servant's crime deserves extermination of the clan; I dare not speak falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "I deserve death for my whole clan and dare not lie.

sentences.zh: 殿下以臣侍講日久，哀臣乞命耳。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince has attended to me as a lecturer for many days and pitied me, begging for my life, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince, who has had me as his teacher for many years, pitied me and pleaded for my life—that is all.

sentences.zh: 實不問臣，不敢迷亂。

translations.literal: Had he truly not questioned me, I would not have spoken in confusion."
translations.idiomatic: If he had not truly questioned me, I would not have spoken at random."

sentences.zh: 」帝謂景穆曰：「直哉！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Jingmu, "How straight!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Jingmu, "What integrity!

sentences.zh: 此亦人情所難，而能臨死不移。

translations.literal: This too is what human feeling finds difficult, yet he could, facing death, not waver.
translations.idiomatic: Even facing death, he would not bend—such steadfastness is rare among men.

sentences.zh: 且對君以實，貞臣也，寧失一有罪，宜宥之。

translations.literal: Moreover, to answer one's lord with truth is the mark of a loyal minister; better to lose one guilty man than punish him—he should be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: A subject who speaks truth to his sovereign is a loyal minister. Better to spare one guilty man than punish such honesty—he should be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 」允竟得免。

translations.literal: Yun in the end was spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Yun was spared.

sentences.zh: 於是召浩前，使人詰，惶惑不能對。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hao was summoned forward; messengers were sent to question him, but he was fearful and confused and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was then brought forward and questioned, but in panic and confusion he could not answer.

sentences.zh: 允事事申明，皆有條理。

translations.literal: Yun explained every matter clearly; each had proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Yun answered every question with clarity and in perfect order.

sentences.zh: 時帝怒甚，敕允為詔，自浩以下，僮吏以上，一百二十八人皆夷五族。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's wrath was extreme. He ordered Yun to draft an edict: from Hao downward, including household servants and clerks, one hundred twenty-eight persons all were to have five generations of their kin exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's fury was at its height. He ordered Yun to draft an edict sentencing all one hundred twenty-eight persons—from Hao on down to his household servants and clerks—to execution of their entire clans to the fifth degree.

sentences.zh: 允持疑不為，頻詔催切，允乞更一見，然後為詔。

translations.literal: Yun held back in doubt and would not draft it. Edicts repeatedly came urging him; Yun begged to see the emperor once more, and only then would he draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yun hesitated and refused. The emperor sent repeated urgent summons; Yun asked to see him once more before he would draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 詔引前，允曰：「浩之所坐，若更有餘釁，非臣敢知。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him forward. Yun said: "As for the crime Hao stands convicted of, if there are further offenses beyond this, your servant does not dare to know.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned before the emperor, Yun said, "If Hao is guilty of further offenses beyond what is known, I cannot say.

sentences.zh: 直以犯觸，罪不至死。

translations.literal: It is simply because he gave offense; the crime does not reach death.
translations.idiomatic: He merely gave offense; the offense does not merit death.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，命介士執允。

translations.literal: " The emperor grew angry and ordered armed guards to seize Yun.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flew into a rage and ordered armored guards to seize Yun.

sentences.zh: 景穆拜請，帝曰：「無此人忿朕，當有數千口死矣！

translations.literal: Jingmu bowed and pleaded. The emperor said: "Were it not for this man defying me, several thousand people would be dead by now!
translations.idiomatic: Jingmu prostrated himself and begged for mercy. The emperor said, "Had this man not defied me, several thousand souls would already be dead!

sentences.zh: 」浩竟族滅，餘皆身死。

translations.literal: " In the end Hao's clan was utterly destroyed; the rest all died by execution alone.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao's clan was exterminated to the last, while the others were put to death individually.

sentences.zh: 宗欽臨刑歎曰：「高允其殆聖乎！」

translations.literal: Zong Qin, facing execution, sighed and said: "Is Gao Yun not perhaps a sage!"
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of his execution, Zong Qin sighed, "Gao Yun is nearly a sage!"

sentences.zh: 景穆後讓允，以不同己所導之言而令帝怒。

translations.literal: Later Jingmu reproached Yun, because he had not followed the words Jingmu had guided him to speak and had angered the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jingmu took Yun to task for refusing to follow his coached testimony and provoking the emperor's wrath.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「夫史籍，帝王之實錄，將來之炯誡，今之所以觀往，後之所以知今。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Historical records are the true chronicle of emperors, bright admonition for generations to come—by them the present looks upon the past, and posterity shall know the present.
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "History is the true record of emperors, a bright warning to future ages. By it we study the past today, and by it posterity will understand our own time.

sentences.zh: 是以言行舉動，莫不備載，故人君慎焉。

translations.literal: Therefore words, deeds, and every act are all fully recorded—hence rulers must be careful.
translations.idiomatic: Every word and deed is recorded in full; that is why a ruler must watch his conduct.

sentences.zh: 然浩世受殊遇，榮曜當時，私欲沒其公廉，愛憎蔽其直理，此浩之責也。

translations.literal: Yet Hao generation after generation received special favor and glory in his own time; private desire drowned his public integrity, and love and hate blinded his straight judgment—this is Hao's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hao had enjoyed exceptional favor generation after generation and basked in glory. Private desire drowned his integrity, and personal likes and dislikes clouded his judgment—that is Hao's fault.

sentences.zh: 至於書朝廷起動之跡，言國家得失之事，此為史之本體，未為多違。

translations.literal: As for recording the court's movements and actions and speaking of the state's gains and losses—this is the essential substance of history, and has not greatly strayed.
translations.idiomatic: But to record the court's doings and speak frankly of the state's successes and failures—that is the very essence of history, and it is no great transgression.

sentences.zh: 然臣與浩實同其事，死生義無獨殊。

translations.literal: Yet your servant and Hao truly shared the same undertaking; in the matter of life and death there is no reason I alone should be treated differently.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hao and I shared the same work. There is no reason I alone should be spared while he faces death.

sentences.zh: 誠荷殿下再造之慈，違心苟免，非臣之意。

translations.literal: I truly bear the Crown Prince's grace of giving me new life, but to go against my heart and seek escape by pretense is not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply grateful to Your Highness for saving my life, but to lie to save myself goes against everything I stand for.

sentences.zh: 」景穆動容稱歎。

translations.literal: " Jingmu's expression changed and he praised him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingmu was visibly moved and praised him.

sentences.zh: 允後與人言曰：「我不奉東宮導旨者，恐負翟黑子也。」

translations.literal: Later Yun spoke to others, saying: "The reason I did not follow the Eastern Palace's guided words is that I feared failing Zhai Heizi."
translations.idiomatic: Later Yun told others, "I refused the Crown Prince's coached testimony because I could not betray Zhai Heizi."

sentences.zh: 景穆季年，頗親近左右，營立田園，以收其利。

translations.literal: In Jingmu's later years, he grew quite close to his attendants and established private estates and gardens to reap profit from them.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Jingmu kept close company with his personal attendants, establishing private estates and gardens for profit.

sentences.zh: 允諫曰：「殿下，國之儲貳，四海屬心，言行舉動，萬方所則。

translations.literal: Yun remonstrated, saying: "Your Highness is the heir presumptive of the state; all within the four seas look to you—your words, deeds, and every act are the model for all regions.
translations.idiomatic: Yun admonished him: "Your Highness is the heir to the throne; the whole realm watches you. Your every word and deed sets the example for ten thousand realms.

sentences.zh: 而營立私田，畜養雞犬，乃至販酤市厘，與人爭利，議聲流布，不可追掩。

translations.literal: Yet you establish private fields, raise chickens and dogs, and even sell wine and trade in market tolls, competing with others for profit—talk spreads and cannot be recalled or covered up.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have established private fields, keep chickens and dogs, and even sell wine and haggle over market fees, competing with common folk for profit. The talk has spread far and wide and cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，殿下之天下，富有四海，何求而不獲何欲而弗從？

translations.literal: The realm under Heaven is Your Highness's realm; possessing all within the four seas, what could you seek and not obtain, what desire and not have granted?
translations.idiomatic: The empire is yours, Your Highness—you possess all within the four seas. What could you want that you cannot have?

sentences.zh: 而與販夫販婦競此尺寸？

translations.literal: Yet you compete for these petty sums with peddling men and peddling women?
translations.idiomatic: Why compete over pennies with street peddlers?

sentences.zh: 願殿下少察過言，斥出佞邪，所在田園，分給貧下。

translations.literal: I hope Your Highness will give a little heed to my excessive words, drive out flatterers and the wicked, and distribute all your estates and gardens among the poor.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to consider my blunt words, dismiss the flatterers and the corrupt, and divide your estates among the poor.

sentences.zh: 如此，則休聲日至，謗議可除。

translations.literal: If you do this, then praise will arrive day by day, and slander can be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Do so, and your good name will grow daily while the scandal fades away.

sentences.zh: 」景穆不納。

translations.literal: " Jingmu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingmu paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 景穆之崩也，允久不進見，後見，升階歔欷，悲不能止。

translations.literal: When Jingmu died, Yun for a long time did not appear at court. When he later had an audience and ascended the steps, he sobbed and sighed, grieving without cease.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingmu's death, Yun stayed away from court for a long time. When he finally came before the emperor and climbed the steps, he wept uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 帝流淚，命允使出。

translations.literal: The emperor shed tears and ordered Yun to go out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and ordered Yun to leave.

sentences.zh: 左右莫知其故，相謂曰：「允無何悲泣，令至尊哀傷，何也？

translations.literal: Those on either side did not know the reason and said to one another: "Why is Yun weeping so suddenly and making the sovereign sorrowful?
translations.idiomatic: The attendants, not knowing why, whispered among themselves: "Why is Yun weeping for no apparent reason and grieving the emperor?

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，召而謂曰：「汝不知高允悲乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor heard this, summoned them, and said: "Do you not know why Gao Yun grieves?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor overheard and summoned them. "Do you not understand Gao Yun's grief?" he said.

sentences.zh: 崔浩誅時，允亦應死。

translations.literal: When Cui Hao was executed, Yun too ought to have died.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hao was put to death, Yun should have died with him.

sentences.zh: 東宮苦請，是以得免。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace pleaded bitterly, and on that account he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince pleaded desperately on his behalf, and so he was spared.

sentences.zh: 今無東宮，允見朕悲耳。

translations.literal: Now there is no Eastern Palace; Yun grieves when he sees me, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Crown Prince is gone—when Yun sees me, he remembers that grief.

sentences.zh: 」先是，敕允集天文災異，使事類相從，約而可觀。

translations.literal: " Before this, an edict had ordered Yun to compile astronomical portents and calamities, arranging them by category so they would be concise and readable.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, the emperor had ordered Yun to compile records of celestial portents and omens, grouping them by category in a concise and readable form.

sentences.zh: 允依《洪範傳》、《天文志》，撮其事要，略其文辭，凡為八篇。

translations.literal: Yun followed the Hong Fan Zhuan and the Tianwen Zhi, extracting the essentials and abbreviating the wording—in all, eight chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on the Commentary on the Hong Fan and the Astronomical Treatise, Yun distilled the essentials and trimmed the prose, producing eight chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而善之，曰：「高允之明災異，亦豈減崔浩乎？

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved, saying: "Gao Yun's understanding of omens—is it not also no less than Cui Hao's?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the work and praised it. "Gao Yun's mastery of portents—is it any less than Cui Hao's?" he said.

sentences.zh: 」及文成即位，允頗有謀焉，司徒陸麗等皆受重賞，允既不蒙褒異，又終身不言。

translations.literal: When Wencheng ascended the throne, Yun had contributed substantially to the undertaking; Minister over the Masses Lu Li and others all received heavy rewards, but Yun neither received praise nor distinction, and to the end of his life he never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, Yun had played a significant role in the succession. Lu Li, Minister over the Masses, and others received rich rewards, but Yun received no honors and never spoke of his own contribution.

sentences.zh: 其忠而不伐，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His loyalty without boasting was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his loyalty without self-promotion.

sentences.zh: 給事中郭善明，性多機巧，欲逞其能，勸文成大起宮室。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Guo Shanming was by nature full of ingenious schemes and wished to display his talents; he urged Wencheng to undertake grand palace construction on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shanming, Attendant-in-Ordinary, was clever and ambitious. Wishing to show off his abilities, he urged Emperor Wencheng to launch massive palace construction.

sentences.zh: 允諫曰：「臣聞太祖道武皇帝既定天下，始建都邑。

translations.literal: Yun remonstrated, saying: "Your servant has heard that when Emperor Daowu the Founding Ancestor had settled the realm, he only then established the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yun remonstrated: "I have heard that when Emperor Daowu, the Founding Ancestor, had pacified the realm, he began building the capital.

sentences.zh: 其所營立，必因農隙。

translations.literal: What he constructed was always done during breaks in the farming season.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he built was done only in the slack seasons of farming.

sentences.zh: 今建國已久，宮室已備，永安前殿，足以朝會萬國；

translations.literal: Now the state has long been established and the palaces are already complete—the Yong'an Front Hall is sufficient for receiving tribute from ten thousand states;
translations.idiomatic: The state has stood for many years now, and the palaces are already sufficient. The Yong'an Front Hall is ample for audiences with envoys from every land;

sentences.zh: 西堂溫室，足以安禦聖躬；

translations.literal: the Western Hall and heated chambers are sufficient to shelter the sacred person of the sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: the Western Hall and its heated chambers are sufficient to shelter the sacred person;

sentences.zh: 紫樓臨望，可以周視遠近。

translations.literal: the Purple Tower overlooking the view can survey near and far all around.
translations.idiomatic: and the Purple Tower, rising above the capital, affords a view in every direction.

sentences.zh: 若廣修壯麗為異觀者，宜漸致之，不可倉卒。

translations.literal: If one wishes to build broadly, magnificently, and splendidly as extraordinary sights, it should be done gradually and not in haste.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to raise grand and splendid edifices as marvels, it should be done gradually—not in haste.

sentences.zh: 計斫材軍士及諸雜役須二萬，丁夫充作，老小供餉，合四萬人，半年可訖。

translations.literal: Calculating lumber-cutters, soldiers, and all miscellaneous laborers requires twenty thousand; adult males assigned to construction, elders and children supplying provisions—in all forty thousand men, and it could be finished in half a year.
translations.idiomatic: I estimate that felling timber, soldiers, and assorted laborers would require twenty thousand men; with corvée workers and those supplying provisions for the young and old, the total would reach forty thousand—and even then the work would take half a year.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：'一夫不耕，或受其饑，一婦不織，或受其寒。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: 'If one man does not plow, someone may suffer hunger; if one woman does not weave, someone may suffer cold.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'If one man does not plow, someone may go hungry; if one woman does not weave, someone may go cold.

sentences.zh: '況數萬之眾，其所損費，亦已多矣！

translations.literal: ' How much more when tens of thousands are involved—the loss and expense would also be great indeed!
translations.idiomatic: ' How much greater still would be the loss when tens of thousands are taken from the fields!"

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 允以文成纂承平之業，而風俗仍舊，婚娶喪葬，不依古式，乃諫曰：

translations.literal: Yun, seeing that Wencheng had inherited a realm at peace yet customs remained as before—marriage and burial not following ancient forms—thereupon remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Emperor Wencheng had inherited a realm at peace yet customs remained unchanged—weddings and funerals observing none of the ancient rites—Yun submitted a remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 前朝之世，屢發明詔，禁諸婚娶，不得作樂。

translations.literal: In the previous reign, enlightened edicts were repeatedly issued forbidding music at all weddings.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign, edicts were repeatedly issued forbidding music at weddings.

sentences.zh: 及葬送之日，歌謠鼓舞，殺牲燒葬，一切禁絕。

translations.literal: On the day of burial and the funeral procession, singing, dancing, beating drums, killing livestock, and cremation were all entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: At funerals, singing, dancing, drum-beating, slaughter of livestock, and cremation were all strictly banned.

sentences.zh: 雖條旨久班，而不革變，將由居上者未能悛改，為下者習以成俗，教化陵遲，一至於此。

translations.literal: Although the regulations had long been promulgated, there was no reform—presumably because those above could not repent and change, while those below had grown accustomed until it became custom; instruction and transformation had declined, reaching this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though these laws were long on the books, nothing had changed—because those above would not amend their ways and those below had made custom of disobedience. Moral instruction had fallen so low as to come to this.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云'爾之教矣，人胥效矣。

translations.literal: The Book of Songs says, 'When you teach, the people all imitate.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says, 'You have taught—and the people have followed your example.

sentences.zh: '人君舉動，不可不慎。

translations.literal: ' A ruler's words and actions must not be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: ' A sovereign's conduct must never be careless.

sentences.zh: 《禮》云：嫁女之家，三日不息火；

translations.literal: The Rites say: In the house of one giving a daughter in marriage, the fire is not extinguished for three days;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites prescribe: in the household giving a daughter in marriage, the hearth-fire must burn for three days;

sentences.zh: 娶妻之家，三日不舉樂。

translations.literal: in the house of one taking a wife, no music is played for three days.
translations.idiomatic: in the household receiving a bride, no music is played for three days.

sentences.zh: 今諸王納室，皆樂部給伎以為嬉戲，而獨禁細人不得作樂，此一異也。

translations.literal: Now when the princes take wives, the Music Bureau provides performers for amusement, yet common folk alone are forbidden music—this is the first inconsistency.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today when princes take wives, the Music Bureau supplies performers for their entertainment, while commoners alone are forbidden music. This is the first inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 古之婚者，皆采德義之門，妙簡貞閑之女，先之以媒娉，繼之以禮物，集僚友以重其別，親禦輪以崇其敬。

translations.literal: In ancient marriages, one chose families of virtue and righteousness and carefully selected chaste and modest daughters; first came the matchmaker's visit, then the ritual gifts; colleagues were gathered to honor the separation, and the groom personally held the carriage wheel to show reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times marriages were arranged with families of virtue, selecting daughters of chastity and modesty; first the matchmaker's visit, then ritual gifts; kinsmen were gathered to honor the parting, and the groom himself held the carriage wheel in respect.

sentences.zh: 今諸王十五便賜妻別居。

translations.literal: Now at fifteen the princes are granted wives and live apart.
translations.idiomatic: Today princes are given wives at fifteen and set up in separate households.

sentences.zh: 然所配者，或長少差舛，或罪入掖庭，而以作合宗王，妃嬪籓懿，失禮之甚，無復此過。

translations.literal: Yet those paired with them were sometimes mismatched in age, sometimes criminal women from the inner palace—and to make them consorts of royal princes and imperial consorts of the frontier lords was an extreme breach of ritual; there is no worse offense than this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those paired with them are sometimes grossly mismatched in age, sometimes women condemned to the inner palace—and to wed them to royal princes as imperial consorts is a grievous breach of ritual without parallel.

sentences.zh: 今皇子娶妻，多出宮掖，令天下小人，必依禮限，此二異也。

translations.literal: Now when imperial princes take wives, most come from within the palace precincts, while common folk are commanded to observe ritual limits—this is the second inconsistency.
translations.idiomatic: Today imperial princes take wives chiefly from the inner palace, while ordinary folk are commanded to follow ritual propriety. This is the second inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 凡萬物之生，靡不有死，然葬者藏也，死者不可再見，故深藏之。

translations.literal: All things that live none but die; yet burial means concealment—the dead cannot be seen again, and so they are deeply hidden.
translations.idiomatic: All living things must die; burial means concealment—the dead cannot be seen again, and so they should be laid deep in the earth.

sentences.zh: 昔堯葬谷林，農不易畝；

translations.literal: Formerly Yao was buried in Gulin, and farmers did not change their furrows;
translations.idiomatic: When Yao was buried in the Forest Valley, no farmer had to shift his furrows;

sentences.zh: 舜葬蒼梧，市不改肆。

translations.literal: Shun was buried in Cangwu, and the market did not change its stalls.
translations.idiomatic: when Shun was buried in Cangwu, no shopkeeper had to move his stall.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇作為地市，下錮三泉，死不旋踵，屍焚墓掘。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang made an underground market city and sealed it beneath the Three Springs; before death had even turned, his corpse was burned and his tomb excavated.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang built an underground palace and sealed it beneath three rivers—and before he was cold in his grave, his body was burned and his tomb looted.

sentences.zh: 由此推之，堯舜之儉，始皇之奢，是非可見。

translations.literal: From this one may infer—Yao and Shun's frugality, the First Emperor's extravagance; right and wrong are plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: From this the contrast is plain: Yao and Shun's frugality against the First Emperor's extravagance.

sentences.zh: 今國家營葬，費損巨億，一旦焚之，以為灰燼。

translations.literal: Now when the state arranges burials, costs run to hundreds of millions, and in an instant they are cremated to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Today state burials cost hundreds of millions—and then the corpses are cremated to ash in an instant.

sentences.zh: 上為之而不輟，而禁下人之必止，此三異也。

translations.literal: Those above do this without ceasing, yet demand that common people below must stop—this is the third inconsistency.
translations.idiomatic: The court practices cremation without restraint, yet forbids the common people from doing the same. This is the third inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 古者，祭必立屍，序其昭穆；

translations.literal: In antiquity, at sacrifice one always set up a corpse-figure and arranged the senior and junior lines;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity sacrifices required a corpse-figure representing the dead, arranged in proper ancestral order;

sentences.zh: 使亡者有馮，致食饗之禮。

translations.literal: so that the departed had someone to rely upon and the rite of offering food and feasting could be performed.
translations.idiomatic: so the departed might have one to rely on and the rites of offering food could be performed.

sentences.zh: 今已葬之魂，人直求貌類者，事之如父母，宴好如夫妻，損敗風化，黷亂情禮，莫此之甚。

translations.literal: Now for those already buried, people simply seek someone resembling their appearance and serve them as parents, feasting and coupling as husband and wife—damaging custom and debasing ritual sentiment; nothing is more extreme than this.
translations.idiomatic: Today, for the already buried, people seek look-alikes and treat them as parents, even sharing marital intimacy with them—debasing morality and corrupting ritual propriety. Nothing exceeds this in depravity.

sentences.zh: 上未禁之，下不改絕，此四異也。

translations.literal: Those above have not forbidden it; those below have not ceased the practice—this is the fourth inconsistency.
translations.idiomatic: The court has not forbidden it, and the people have not abandoned the practice. This is the fourth inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 夫大饗者，所以定禮儀，訓萬國，故聖王重之。

translations.literal: Grand feasts serve to fix ritual and instruct ten thousand states; therefore sage kings held them in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Grand royal feasts establish ritual and instruct the realm; sage kings therefore held them in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 至乃爵盈而不飲，肴乾而不食，樂非雅聲則不奏，物非正色則不列。

translations.literal: To the point that when goblets were full one did not drink, when dishes were dry one did not eat; if music was not correct ceremonial sound it was not performed; if objects were not the proper colors they were not displayed.
translations.idiomatic: At such feasts, goblets might stand full yet remain untouched, dishes dried yet untouched; no music was played unless it was proper ceremonial music, and no offerings displayed unless they were ritually correct.

sentences.zh: 今之大會，內外相混，酒醉喧嘵，罔有儀式，又俳優鄙褻，污辱視聽。

translations.literal: Today's great assemblies mix inner and outer circles; drunk and shouting loudly, there is no ceremony at all; moreover actors and jesters are vulgar and indecent, fouling what is seen and heard.
translations.idiomatic: Today's great assemblies mix courtiers and commoners alike—men drunk and shouting without a trace of ceremony, while vulgar comedians pollute what eyes and ears must endure.

sentences.zh: 朝廷積習以為美，而責風俗之清純，此五異也。

translations.literal: The court has accumulated such custom and taken it for beauty, yet demands purity of popular custom—this is the fifth inconsistency.
translations.idiomatic: The court treats such coarseness as refinement, yet demands moral purity from the people. This is the fifth inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 今陛下當百王之末，踵晉亂之弊，而不矯然厘改，以厲頹俗，臣恐天下蒼生，永不聞見禮教矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty stands at the end of a hundred kings, following the evils of Jin's disorder, yet does not sharply reform and rectify to sharpen a declining custom—I fear the people under Heaven will never hear or see ritual teaching again.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty stands at the end of a long line of kings, inheriting the disorder left by Jin, yet does not sternly reform customs to revive a failing morality. I fear the people of this realm may never again know the teaching of ritual.

sentences.zh: 允如此非一，帝從容聽之。

translations.literal: Yun's remonstrances of this kind were not once alone; the emperor listened at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yun offered such remonstrances more than once, and the emperor always listened patiently.

sentences.zh: 或有觸迕，帝所不忍聞者，命左右扶出。

translations.literal: If something touched against or offended what the emperor could not bear to hear, he ordered attendants to support Yun out.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun touched on something the emperor could not bear to hear, he would have attendants escort him out.

sentences.zh: 事有不便，允輒求見，帝知允意，逆屏左右以待之。

translations.literal: When there was something inconvenient, Yun would immediately request an audience; the emperor, knowing Yun's intent, in advance dismissed attendants and waited for him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever something troubled the state, Yun would request an audience. Knowing his purpose, the emperor would dismiss his attendants in advance and wait for him.

sentences.zh: 禮敬甚重，晨入暮出，或積日居中，朝臣莫知所論。

translations.literal: The courtesy shown him was very great; he entered in the morning and left at evening, sometimes remaining inside for days on end—court ministers did not know what was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: He was honored with the utmost respect—entering at dawn and leaving at dusk, sometimes remaining within for days on end, while the courtiers knew nothing of what was said.

sentences.zh: 或有上事陳得失者，帝省而謂群臣曰：「君父一也，父有是非，子何為不作書于人中諫之，使人知惡，而於家內隱處也？

translations.literal: When someone submitted a memorial stating gains and losses, the emperor read it and said to the assembled ministers: "Sovereign and father are one—when a father has right and wrong, why should a son not remonstrate in writing among people so that others know the fault, but instead hide it within the family?
translations.idiomatic: When someone submitted a memorial listing the state's strengths and failings, the emperor reviewed it and said to his ministers, "The sovereign and the father are one. When a father errs, why does a son not write openly to correct him before others, so that the wrong may be known—instead of hiding his remonstrance within the family?

sentences.zh: 豈不以父親，恐惡彰於外也。

translations.literal: Is it not because of affection for the father, fearing that the fault would be displayed outward?
translations.idiomatic: Does he not do so out of filial concern—fearing to expose his father's faults to the world?

sentences.zh: 今國家善惡，不能面陳，而上表顯諫，以此，豈不彰君之短，明己之美。

translations.literal: Now the state's good and ill cannot be stated face to face, yet one submits a memorial for open remonstrance—in this way, does one not display the lord's shortcomings while making one's own merit plain?
translations.idiomatic: Today ministers cannot speak face to face of the state's right and wrong, yet submit memorials for all to see—does this not expose the sovereign's faults while proclaiming one's own virtue?

sentences.zh: 至如高允者，真忠臣矣。

translations.literal: As for one like Gao Yun—he is a true loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: As for Gao Yun—there is a true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 朕有是非，恆正言而論，至朕所不忍聞者，皆侃侃論說，無所避就。

translations.literal: When I have right and wrong, he always speaks straight and discusses it; even what I cannot bear to hear—he all discusses openly and at ease, with nothing avoided or shunned.
translations.idiomatic: When I err, he speaks plainly. Even on matters I least wish to hear, he argues forthrightly, never flinching.

sentences.zh: 朕聞其過，而天下不知其諫，豈不忠乎。

translations.literal: I hear my faults, yet the realm does not know he remonstrated—is this not loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: I alone hear his corrections, while the realm never knows he challenged me—is that not the mark of a loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 汝等在左右，不曾聞一正言，但伺朕喜以求官。

translations.literal: You who attend at my side have never once heard a straight word from you—you only watch my pleasure to seek office.
translations.idiomatic: You attend me daily yet never speak an honest word—you only watch my mood to win promotion.

sentences.zh: 汝等以弓刀侍朕，待立勞耳，皆至公、王，此人執筆匡我，不過著作郎。

translations.literal: You attend me with bow and blade, standing by in mere attendance, yet all reach ranks of duke and prince; this man holds the brush to set me right, yet rises no higher than Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: You guard me with bow and blade, mere attendants in waiting—yet you have all risen to dukes and princes. This man corrects me with his brush and holds no rank higher than Compiler.

sentences.zh: 汝等不亦愧乎！

translations.literal: Are you not ashamed!
translations.idiomatic: Are you not ashamed?"

sentences.zh: 」於是拜允中書令，著作如故。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yun was appointed Central Secretariat Director, retaining his Compiler post as before.
translations.idiomatic: " At this he appointed Yun Director of the Central Secretariat, while retaining his post as Compiler.

sentences.zh: 司徒陸麗曰：「高允雖蒙寵待，而家貧布衣，妻子不立。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Lu Li said: "Though Gao Yun enjoys favor and preferment, his household is poor in plain cloth; wife and children have no settled livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Li, Minister over the Masses, said, "Though Gao Yun enjoys Your Majesty's favor, his home is humble—he and his family wear plain cloth and have scarcely a livelihood."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒曰：「何不先言？

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily: "Why did you not speak of this earlier?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "Why did you not tell me this before?

sentences.zh: 今見朕用之，方言其貧！

translations.literal: Now that you see I am employing him, you only now speak of his poverty!
translations.idiomatic: You wait until I appoint him, and only then mention his poverty!"

sentences.zh: 」是日，幸允第，唯草屋數間，布被溫袍，廚中鹽菜而已。

translations.literal: That day the emperor visited Yun's residence—only a few thatched cottages, cotton quilt and padded robe, and in the kitchen nothing but salt and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: That very day the emperor visited Yun's home and found only a few thatched cottages, cotton bedding and a padded robe, and in the kitchen nothing but salt and pickled vegetables.

sentences.zh: 帝歎息曰：「古人之清貧，豈有此乎！

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "The frugal poverty of the ancients—could it have reached this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed. "Even the austere poverty of the ancients—was it ever like this?

sentences.zh: 」即賜帛五百疋，粟千斛，拜長子忱為長樂太守。

translations.literal: " Immediately he bestowed five hundred bolts of silk and a thousand bushels of grain, and appointed his eldest son Chen as Administrator of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately granted five hundred bolts of silk and a thousand bushels of grain, and appointed Yun's eldest son Chen Administrator of Changle.

sentences.zh: 允頻表固讓，帝不許。

translations.literal: Yun repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yun repeatedly memorialized to decline, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 初與允同征遊雅等，多至通官，封侯，及允部下吏百數十人，亦至刺史、二千石；

translations.literal: At first those who went on campaign with Yun, such as You Ya and others, mostly reached high office and were enfeoffed as marquises; as for the hundred-odd clerks under Yun's command, many also reached the rank of Regional Inspector or the two-thousand-bushel salary grade;
translations.idiomatic: Those who had served alongside Yun in the early years—You Ya and others—mostly rose to high office and were enfeoffed as marquises; of the hundred-odd clerks who had served under him, many became Regional Inspectors or administrators at the two-thousand-bushel rank;

sentences.zh: 而允為郎二十七年不徙官。

translations.literal: Yet Yun served as Gentleman for twenty-seven years without transfer of office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yun remained a Gentleman for twenty-seven years without ever changing posts.

sentences.zh: 時百官無祿，允恆使諸子樵采自給。

translations.literal: At the time all officials received no salary; Yun constantly had his sons gather firewood to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In those days officials received no stipends, and Yun regularly sent his sons out to cut wood and forage for the household.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書竇瑾坐事誅，瑾子遵亡在山澤，遵母焦沒入縣官。

translations.literal: Initially, Attendant-in-Chief Dou Jin was executed for an offense; Jin's son Zun fled to the mountains and marshes, and Zun's mother Jiao was seized as government property.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Attendant-in-Chief Dou Jin had been executed for a crime. His son Zun fled into the wilds, and Zun's mother Jiao was confiscated by the government.

sentences.zh: 後焦以老得免，瑾之親故，莫有恤者。

translations.literal: Later Jiao was released on account of old age, but none of Jin's kin or friends showed her any care.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiao was freed because of her age, yet none of Jin's relatives or old associates offered her any help.

sentences.zh: 允湣焦年老，保護在家，積六年，遵始蒙赦。

translations.literal: Yun pitied Jiao in her old age and kept her sheltered in his home; after six years Zun finally received an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yun took pity on the aged Jiao and sheltered her in his household. Six years passed before Zun at last received a pardon.

sentences.zh: 其篤行如此。

translations.literal: His steadfast conduct was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his moral constancy.

sentences.zh: 轉太常卿，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Ceremonies while retaining his original office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Minister of Ceremonies while keeping his former post as well.

sentences.zh: 允上《代都賦》，因以夫諷，亦《二京》之流也。

translations.literal: Yun submitted "Rhapsody on the Capital of Dai," using it thereby to remonstrate—in the same tradition as the "Two Capitals" rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: Yun presented his "Rhapsody on the Capital of Dai," turning it to admonition in the manner of the "Two Capitals" rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 時中書博士索敞與侍郎傅默、梁祚論名字貴賤，著議紛紜。

translations.literal: At the time Imperial Library Erudite Suo Chang and Attendants-in-Ordinary Fu Mo and Liang Zuo debated the noble and base qualities of personal names, producing arguments in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Suo Chang, Erudite of the Secretariat, and Attendants-in-Ordinary Fu Mo and Liang Zuo argued over whether names were high or low in rank, and their written opinions were wildly at odds.

sentences.zh: 允遂著《名字論》以釋其惑，甚有典證。

translations.literal: Yun then wrote "Discourse on Personal Names" to resolve their confusion, with much classical evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Yun thereupon composed "Discourse on Personal Names" to clear up their doubts, drawing on abundant canonical proof.

sentences.zh: 復以本官領秘書監，解太常卿，進爵梁城侯。

translations.literal: Again with his original office he concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat; he was relieved of Grand Minister of Ceremonies and advanced in rank to Marquis of Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He again held his original post while also serving as Director of the Secretariat, resigned as Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and was ennobled as Marquis of Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 初，允與遊雅及太原張偉同業相友。

translations.literal: Initially Yun studied alongside You Ya and Zhang Wei of Taiyuan and became their friend.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years Yun studied with You Ya and Zhang Wei of Taiyuan and formed a close friendship with them.

sentences.zh: 雅嘗論允曰：「夫喜怒者，有生所不能無也。

translations.literal: Ya once remarked on Yun: "Joy and anger are what no living person can be without.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya once said of Yun: "Joy and anger are feelings no living man can wholly escape.

sentences.zh: 而前史載卓公寬中，文饒洪量，褊心者或之弗信。

translations.literal: Yet former histories record Zhuo Gong's broad tolerance and Wenrao's vast forbearance; narrow-minded men may fail to believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the old histories tell us of Zhuo Gong's magnanimity and Wenrao's great breadth of spirit, and the small-souled may refuse to credit it.

sentences.zh: 余與高子游處四十餘年，未見是非慍喜之色，不亦信哉。

translations.literal: I have kept company with Master Gao for more than forty years and never seen the colors of approval, disapproval, anger, or delight on his face—is this not believable?
translations.idiomatic: I have kept company with Master Gao for more than forty years without once seeing approval, disapproval, anger, or pleasure cross his face—is that not proof enough?

sentences.zh: 高子內文明而外柔弱，其言呐呐不能出口，余常呼為'文子'。

translations.literal: Master Gao is enlightened within yet outwardly yielding; his speech is halting and hard to get out—I often call him 'Wenzi.'
translations.idiomatic: Master Gao is luminous within yet gentle without; his words come slowly and with difficulty, and I often call him 'Master Wen.'

sentences.zh: 崔公謂餘云：'高生豐才博學，一代佳士，所乏者矯矯風節耳。

translations.literal: Minister Cui said to me: 'Master Gao has abundant talent and broad learning—a fine gentleman of his generation; what he lacks is only a stiff, upright bearing.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister Cui once told me, 'Master Gao is richly gifted and widely learned—a true gentleman of the age. All he lacks is that hard, unyielding moral spine.'

sentences.zh: '餘亦然之。

translations.literal: I agreed with this too.
translations.idiomatic: I agreed with him then, as I do now.

sentences.zh: 司徒之譴，起於纖微，及於詔責，崔公聲嘶股戰，不能一言。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor's reprimand began from something slight and reached the point of imperial censure; Minister Cui's voice went hoarse and his legs trembled—he could not speak a word.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Tutor's rebuke arose from a trifle and swelled into an imperial denunciation, Minister Cui's voice broke, his legs shook, and he could not utter a single word.

sentences.zh: 宗欽以下，伏地流汗，都無人色。

translations.literal: From Zong Qin downward, all prostrated themselves streaming sweat, utterly without human color.
translations.idiomatic: From Zong Qin on down, men fell prostrate and drenched themselves in sweat until their faces lost all color.

sentences.zh: 高子敷陳事理，申釋是非，辭義清辯，音韻高亮。

translations.literal: Master Gao laid out the principles of the matter, clarified right and wrong; his words were lucid and sharp, his tone clear and resounding.
translations.idiomatic: Master Gao set out the facts of the case, explained what was right and wrong, and spoke with such clarity and force that every phrase rang clear.

sentences.zh: 明主為之動容，聽者無不稱善。

translations.literal: The enlightened sovereign was moved by it; none who heard failed to praise it.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened ruler was visibly moved, and everyone who heard him praised what he had said.

sentences.zh: 仁及寮友，保茲元吉，向之所謂矯矯者，更在斯乎！

translations.literal: His kindness reached his colleagues and preserved this great good fortune—the so-called stiff uprightness was rather in this, was it not!
translations.idiomatic: His kindness extended to his colleagues and preserved their safety—and the stiff uprightness we had spoken of was found here, was it not!

sentences.zh: 宗愛之任勢也，威振四海，嘗召百司於都坐，王公以下，望庭畢拜，高子獨升階長揖。

translations.literal: When Zong Ai wielded power, his authority shook the four seas; he once summoned the hundred offices to the main hall, and from kings and dukes downward all bowed upon seeing the courtyard—Master Gao alone ascended the steps and made a long bow with hands clasped.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Ai held power his authority filled the realm. Once he summoned every office to the imperial hall; kings and dukes and all below bowed the moment they saw the courtyard, but Master Gao alone climbed the steps and gave a formal bow with clasped hands.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，汲長孺可臥見衛青，何抗禮之有！

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, Ji Changru could meet Wei Qing while reclining—what was there in refusing full obeisance!
translations.idiomatic: Seen in that light, Ji Changru could receive Wei Qing while lying at ease—what offense was there in withholding a full prostration!

sentences.zh: 向之所謂風節者，得不謂此乎！

translations.literal: The bearing and integrity spoken of earlier—can it be called anything but this!
translations.idiomatic: The moral bearing we had meant earlier—could it have been anything but this!

sentences.zh: 知人故不易，人亦不易知。

translations.literal: Knowing men is therefore not easy; men too are not easily known.
translations.idiomatic: To know others is hard; and others are not easily known in return.

sentences.zh: 吾既失之於心內，崔亦漏之於形外。

translations.literal: I already missed it within my heart, and Cui also let it slip in outward appearance.
translations.idiomatic: I had failed to see it in my own heart, and Cui had missed it in what showed on the surface.

sentences.zh: 鐘期止聽于伯牙，夷吾見明于鮑叔，良有以也。

translations.literal: Zhong Ziqi listened only to Bo Ya; Guan Zhong's insight was seen by Bao Shuya—there is truly reason in this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ziqi would listen to no one but Bo Ya; Guan Zhong's worth was recognized by Bao Shuya—and there is good reason for such things.

sentences.zh: 」其為人物所推如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed by others.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which others held him.

sentences.zh: 文成重允，常不名之，恆呼為「令公」。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng held Yun in high regard, often not calling him by name, always addressing him as "Lord Ling."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng valued Yun so highly that he seldom used his personal name, always calling him "Lord Ling" instead.

sentences.zh: 令公之號，播於四遠矣。

translations.literal: The title "Lord Ling" spread to the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: The name "Lord Ling" was known in every quarter of the realm.

sentences.zh: 文成崩，獻文居諒闇，乙弗渾專擅朝命，謀危社稷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, Emperor Xiaowen observed mourning seclusion; Yifu Hun monopolized court commands and plotted to endanger the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wencheng's death, Emperor Xiaowen withdrew into mourning seclusion while Yifu Hun seized control of court orders and plotted against the state.

sentences.zh: 文明太后誅之，引允禁中，參決大政。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming executed him, summoned Yun within the inner palace, and had him participate in deciding great affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming had him executed, brought Yun into the inner palace, and had him take part in deciding major affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 又詔允曰：「朕稽之舊典，欲置學官于郡國。

translations.literal: She also issued an edict to Yun: "I have examined the old regulations and wish to establish academic officers in the commanderies and principalities.
translations.idiomatic: She also issued an edict to Yun: "I have looked into the ancient statutes and wish to place school officers in the commanderies and principalities.

sentences.zh: 卿儒宗元老，宜與中秘二省，參議以聞。

translations.literal: You are a patriarch of Confucian learning and an elder statesman—you should deliberate with the two bureaus of the Central Secretariat and report your findings."
translations.idiomatic: You are the senior patriarch of the Confucian tradition. You should consult with the two secretariat bureaus and submit your recommendations."

sentences.zh: 」允表：請制大郡立博士二人、助教四人、學生一百人；

translations.literal: Yun memorialized: requesting that large commanderies establish two Erudites, four Assistant Instructors, and one hundred students;
translations.idiomatic: Yun memorialized as follows: large commanderies should appoint two Erudites, four Assistant Instructors, and one hundred students;

sentences.zh: 次郡立博士二人、助教二人、學生八十人；

translations.literal: secondary commanderies two Erudites, two Assistant Instructors, and eighty students;
translations.idiomatic: secondary commanderies two Erudites, two Assistant Instructors, and eighty students;

sentences.zh: 中郡立博士一人、助教二人、學生六十人；

translations.literal: medium commanderies one Erudite, two Assistant Instructors, and sixty students;
translations.idiomatic: medium commanderies one Erudite, two Assistant Instructors, and sixty students;

sentences.zh: 下郡立博士一人、助教一人、學生四十人。

translations.literal: small commanderies one Erudite, one Assistant Instructor, and forty students.
translations.idiomatic: small commanderies one Erudite, one Assistant Instructor, and forty students.

sentences.zh: 其博士取博關經典，履行忠清，堪為人師者，年限四十以上。

translations.literal: Erudites should be chosen from those broadly versed in the classics, upright and loyal in conduct, fit to be others' teachers, aged forty or above.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites were to be men broadly learned in the classics, loyal and pure in conduct, fit to serve as teachers, and at least forty years of age.

sentences.zh: 助教亦與博士同，年限三十以上。

translations.literal: Assistant Instructors likewise same as Erudites, aged thirty or above.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Instructors were to meet the same standards as Erudites and be at least thirty years old.

sentences.zh: 若道業夙成，才任教授，不拘年齒。

translations.literal: If the Way is early perfected and talent suffices for instruction, age limits need not apply.
translations.idiomatic: If a man had already mastered the Way and his talent qualified him to teach, the age limits did not apply.

sentences.zh: 學生取郡中清望，人行修謹，堪循名教者，先盡高門，次及中等。

translations.literal: Students should be taken from the commandery's families of clear reputation, persons careful in conduct who can follow the teachings of names—first from eminent houses, then from middling ones.
translations.idiomatic: Students were to be drawn from families of good standing in the commandery—men of careful conduct who could live by the rites—first from the highest houses, then from those of middling rank.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，郡國立學，自此始也。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; commandery and principality schools began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan, and schools in the commanderies and principalities date from that time.

sentences.zh: 後允以老疾，頻上表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Later Yun, owing to age and illness, repeatedly submitted memorials requesting to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Later, afflicted by age and illness, Yun repeatedly memorialized asking to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 詔不許。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused each request.

sentences.zh: 於是乃著《告老詩》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote "Poem on Requesting Retirement."
translations.idiomatic: He then composed his "Poem on Requesting Retirement."

sentences.zh: 又以昔歲同征，零落將盡，感逝懷人，作《征士頌》。

translations.literal: Also, because those who had campaigned with him in former years were nearly all gone, moved by the passing of time and thinking of those men, he composed "Eulogy for the Campaign Scholars."
translations.idiomatic: And because the companions of his early campaigns were nearly all gone, grieving for the dead and remembering the living, he wrote the "Eulogy for the Campaign Scholars."

sentences.zh: 蓋止于應命，其有命而不至，則闕焉。

translations.literal: It included only those who answered the call; those summoned who did not come are omitted.
translations.idiomatic: It included only those who answered the imperial summons; anyone summoned who failed to appear is left out.

sentences.zh: 其著《頌》者：中書侍郎、固安侯范陽盧玄子真，郡功曹史博陵崔綽茂祖，河內太守、下樂侯廣甯燕崇玄略，上党太守、高邑侯廣甯常陟公山，征南大將軍從事中郎勃海高毗子翼，征南大將軍從事中郎勃海李金道賜，河西太守、饒陽子博陵許堪祖根，中書郎、新豐侯京兆杜銓士衡，征西大將軍從事中郎京兆韋閬友規，京兆太守趙郡李詵令孫，太常博士、钜鹿公趙郡李靈武符，中書郎中、即丘子趙郡李遐仲熙，營州刺史、建安公太原張偉仲業，輔國大將軍從事中郎范陽祖邁，征東大將軍從事中郎范陽祖侃士倫，東郡太守、蒲陰子中山劉策，濮陽太守、真定子常山許琛，行司隸校尉、中都侯西河宋宣道茂，中書郎燕郡劉遐彥鑒，中書郎、武恆子河間邢穎宗敬，滄水太守、浮陽侯勃海高濟叔仁，太平太守、原平子雁門李熙士元，秘書監、梁郡公廣平游雅伯度，廷尉正、安平子博陵崔建興祖，廣平太守、列人侯西河宋愔，州主簿長樂潘符，郡功曹長樂杜熙，征東大將軍從事中郎中山張綱，中書郎上谷張誕叔術，秘書郎雁門王道雅，秘書郎雁門閔弼，衛大將軍從事中郎中山郎苗，大司馬從事中郎上谷侯辯，陳郡太守、高邑子趙郡呂季才，合三十四人。

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: The text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy runs thus:

sentences.zh: 紫氣幹天，群雄亂夏，王龔徂征，戎車屢駕。

translations.literal: Purple vapors reach the sky; myriad heroes disorder Xia; King Gong went on campaign; war chariots were repeatedly dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Purple omens filled the heavens; rival warlords threw the realm into chaos; the king set out on campaign, and chariots rolled forth again and again.
