sentences.zh: 掃蕩遊氛，克剪妖霸，四海從風，八垠漸化。

translations.literal: Sweeping away wandering miasmas, conquering and cutting down demonic overlords, the four seas follow the wind, the eight borders gradually transform.
translations.idiomatic: Wandering turmoil was swept away, usurping tyrants were cut down, the four seas turned with the wind, and the eight directions were slowly transformed.

sentences.zh: 政教無外，即寧且壹，偃武櫜兵，唯文是恤。

translations.literal: Government and teaching know no outer bounds; peace and unity are restored; arms are laid aside and troops stowed away; only culture is cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Rule and teaching extended without limit; the realm settled into peace; weapons were sheathed and armies disbanded; only learning was tended.

sentences.zh: 帝乃虛求，搜賢采逸，岩隱投竿，異人並出。

translations.literal: The emperor then sought in earnest, gathering the worthy and collecting the reclusive; men hidden in cliffs cast aside their rods, and extraordinary men appeared together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then searched in earnest for talent, gathering the worthy and drawing out recluses; hermits left their cliffs and put down their fishing poles, and remarkable men came forth together.

sentences.zh: 亹亹盧生，量遠思純，鑽道據德，遊藝依仁；

translations.literal: Assiduous Master Lu, far-reaching in measure and pure in thought, drilled into the Way and rooted himself in virtue, roaming through the arts and relying on humaneness;
translations.idiomatic: Diligent Master Lu, broad in vision and pure in mind, drilled into the Way, rooted himself in virtue, and moved through the arts with humaneness as his guide;

sentences.zh: 旌弓既招，釋褐投巾，攝齋升堂，嘉謀日陳；

translations.literal: Once the bow of honor was offered, he doffed common cloth and took office; adjusting his robes he entered the hall, and good counsel was daily set forth;
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial summons came, he put aside plain dress and entered service; straightening his robes he took his place in court, and sound counsel was offered day after day;

sentences.zh: 自東徂南，躍馬馳輸，僭馮影附，劉以和親。

translations.literal: From east to south he leaped on horses and raced chariots; the usurper Feng attached like a shadow, and Liu was won by marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: From the east to the south he rode hard and drove fast; the rebel Feng clung like a shadow, and Liu was brought over through marriage ties.

sentences.zh: 茂祖煢單，夙離不造，克己勉躬，聿隆家道；

translations.literal: Maozu stood alone, long parted from family nurture; restraining himself and striving in person, he thereby raised his house;
translations.idiomatic: Maozu was solitary, bereft since youth of family guidance; by disciplining himself and laboring in earnest he lifted up his household;

sentences.zh: 敦心《六經》，游思文藻，終辭寵命，以之自保。

translations.literal: Devoting his heart to the Six Classics, roaming in literary refinement, he finally declined favored appointment and thereby preserved himself.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his heart to the Six Classics and wandered among the refinements of letters, yet in the end refused preferment and so preserved his integrity.

sentences.zh: 燕、常篤信，百行靡遺，仕不苟進，任理棲遲；

translations.literal: Yan and Chang were deeply faithful; in a hundred conduct they left nothing undone; they did not seek office rashly, but accepted duty and dwelt at ease;
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Chang were steadfast in faith; in conduct of every kind they left nothing wanting; they did not rush into office, but accepted duty and waited their time;

sentences.zh: 居沖守約，好讓善推，思賢樂古，如渴如饑。

translations.literal: Dwelling in humility they kept to simplicity; they loved yielding and excelled at deferring; they thirsted for the worthy and delighted in antiquity, like hunger, like thirst.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in modesty and held to simplicity; they loved to yield and knew how to step back; they longed for the worthy and rejoiced in antiquity, hungry as for food, thirsty as for drink.

sentences.zh: 子翼致遠，道賜悟深，相期以義，和若瑟琴；

translations.literal: Ziyi looked far ahead; Daoci was deep in understanding; they pledged themselves to one another in righteousness and harmonized like lute and zither;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi looked to what lay far ahead; Daoci saw deeply into things; they bound themselves to one another in righteousness and lived in harmony like lute and zither;

sentences.zh: 並參幕府，俱發德音，優遊卒歲，聊以寄心。

translations.literal: Together they served in the staff offices, together they gave forth virtuous words; at ease they passed the year, merely to set their hearts at rest.
translations.idiomatic: Both served in military staffs, both gave voice to virtue; they passed the years at ease, finding in that enough for their hearts.

sentences.zh: 祖根運會，克光厥猷，仰緣朝恩，俯因德友；

translations.literal: Zugen met the turning of fortune and was able to brighten his plans; looking up he relied on court favor, looking down he drew on the friendship of the virtuous;
translations.idiomatic: Zugen met the tide of fortune and made his designs shine; he rose on imperial grace and stood on the friendship of good men;

sentences.zh: 功雖後建，爵實先受，班同舊臣，位並群後。

translations.literal: Though his merit came later, his rank was received earlier; his stipend matched old ministers, his place stood among the foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Though his achievements came later, his ennoblement came sooner; his honors matched those of veteran ministers, his rank stood with the highest.

sentences.zh: 士衡孤立，內省靡疚，言不崇華，交不遺舊；

translations.literal: Shiheng stood alone; inwardly he found no fault; his words did not pursue ornament, his friendships did not abandon the old;
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng stood apart; looking within, he found no cause for shame; his speech did not chase finery, and in friendship he did not cast off old ties;

sentences.zh: 以產則貧，論道則富，所謂伊人，實邦之秀。

translations.literal: Judged by possessions he was poor; judged by the Way he was rich—such a man as this was truly the finest of the state.
translations.idiomatic: By worldly goods he was poor; by the Way he was rich—the man of whom this is said was truly the glory of the realm.

sentences.zh: 卓矣友規，稟茲淑量，存彼大方，擯此細讓；

translations.literal: Outstanding was Yougui, endowed with this fine measure; he kept to that great breadth and put aside this petty yielding;
translations.idiomatic: Yougui stood above the rest, bearing this noble breadth; he held to the larger way and set aside small concessions;

sentences.zh: 神與理冥，形隨流浪，雖屈王侯，莫廢其尚。

translations.literal: His spirit joined with principle in darkness; his form followed the drifting current; though he bowed to kings and marquises, he never abandoned his ideals.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit moved in accord with principle; his body went where the current carried it; though he served among lords, he never abandoned what he upheld.

sentences.zh: 趙實名區，世多奇士，山嶽所鍾，挺生三李；

translations.literal: Zhao was truly a famed region; generation after generation produced extraordinary men; what mountains and rivers enfolded gave birth to three Lis;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was a land of renown, producing strange and brilliant men generation after generation; what the hills and rivers nurtured brought forth three Lis;

sentences.zh: 矯矯清風，抑抑容止，初九而潛，望雲而起。

translations.literal: Upright was their clear wind; restrained their bearing and stopping; at first hidden like the ninth hexagram, they rose at sight of the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and upright was their moral wind; measured and restrained their bearing; hidden at first like the ninth line, they rose when the clouds appeared.

sentences.zh: 詵尹西都，靈惟作傅，載訓皇宮，載理雲霧；

translations.literal: Shen served as director of the western capital; Ling alone served as tutor; he instructed the imperial palace and ordered the cloudy mists of state;
translations.idiomatic: Shen governed the western capital; Ling alone became tutor to the heir; one trained the palace, one put the drifting affairs of state in order;

sentences.zh: 熙雖中夭，跡階郎署，餘塵可挹，終亦顯著。

translations.literal: Though Xi died in mid-course, his trace climbed the secretariat offices; what dust he left can still be gathered—he too in the end became illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Xi died before his time, yet his path had already reached the secretariat; the traces he left can still be taken up—in the end he too won distinction.

sentences.zh: 仲業深長，雅性清到，憲章古式，綢繆典誥；

translations.literal: Zhongye was deep and long-lasting; by nature refined and clear; he took ancient models as his law and wove close the canonical edicts;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongye was deep and enduring, clear and refined by nature; he made antiquity his standard and gave careful form to the court's edicts;

sentences.zh: 時逢嶮艱，常一其操，納眾以仁，訓下以孝；

translations.literal: When the times turned perilous he kept one constant conduct; he received the multitude with humaneness and instructed subordinates with filial duty;
translations.idiomatic: In hard and dangerous times he held to one unchanging course; he gathered men through humaneness and taught those below him through filial example;

sentences.zh: 化洽龍川，人歸其教。

translations.literal: His transforming influence reached Longchuan; the people returned to his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching permeated Longchuan, and the people came back to his rule.

sentences.zh: 邁則英賢，侃亦稱選，聞達邦家，名行素顯；

translations.literal: Mai was a hero and worthy man; Kan too was a chosen talent; known and eminent in the state, their names and conduct had long been clear;
translations.idiomatic: Mai was a man of heroic worth; Kan too was a chosen talent; famed in the realm, their names and conduct had long stood clear;

sentences.zh: 志在兼濟，豈伊獨善，繩匠弗顧，功不獲展。

translations.literal: Their aim was to benefit all together; how could they be content with private good alone? The master craftsman paid them no heed, and their merit could not be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Their aim was to help the world together—how could they be satisfied with private good alone? The master craftsman did not look their way, and their achievements went unrealized.

sentences.zh: 劉、許履忠，竭力致躬，出則騁說，入獻其功；

translations.literal: Liu and Xu walked in loyalty; they exerted their strength and gave their persons; going forth they expounded persuasions, entering they presented their achievements;
translations.idiomatic: Liu and Xu lived by loyalty, giving their strength and their very selves; abroad they argued their case, at court they offered up their accomplishments;

sentences.zh: 輶軒一舉，橈燕下崇，名彰魏世，享業亦隆。

translations.literal: Once the diplomatic carriage set out, Yan bowed and submitted to Chong; their names shone in the Wei age, and the fortunes they enjoyed were likewise great.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy's carriage went forth once, Yan was bent and brought low before Chong; their fame blazed in the Wei age, and the estates they enjoyed were great as well.

sentences.zh: 道茂夙成，弱冠播名，與朋以信，行物以誠；

translations.literal: Daomao was early perfected; at weak cap his name spread abroad; with friends he was trustworthy, in dealings with things he was sincere;
translations.idiomatic: Daomao matured early; while still young his name rang out; with friends he was faithful, in every action he was sincere;

sentences.zh: 怡怡昆弟，穆穆家庭，發響九皋，翰飛紫冥。

translations.literal: Harmonious were the brothers; reverent was the household; his voice rose from the nine marshes, his brush flew to the purple heights.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers lived in harmony; the household was grave and orderly; his reputation sounded from the distant marshes, his writing soared to the highest court.

sentences.zh: 頻煩省闥，亦司于京，刑以之中，政以之平。

translations.literal: Again and again he served in the inner offices, and also held office in the capital; in punishment he hit the mean, in government he brought peace.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly in the inner offices and also governed in the capital; in law he struck the proper balance, in administration he brought order.

sentences.zh: 猗歟彥鑒，思參文雅，率性任真，器成非假；

translations.literal: Ah, Yanjian! He thought to join the refinements of culture; following his nature he was true to himself; his vessel was fully formed, not borrowed from others;
translations.idiomatic: How fine was Yanjian, aspiring to the elegance of letters; true to his nature and free of artifice, his talent was his own and not borrowed;

sentences.zh: 靡矜于高，莫恥於下，乃謝硃門，歸跡林野。

translations.literal: He did not pride himself on height, nor was he shamed by lowliness; he then declined the vermilion gates and returned his steps to woods and fields.
translations.idiomatic: He did not boast of high station, nor was he ashamed of humble place; he left the crimson gates and went back to the forests and fields.

sentences.zh: 宗敬延譽，號為四俊，華藻雲飛，金聲夙振；

translations.literal: Zongjing spread his reputation and was called one of the Four Outstanding Men; his literary ornament soared like clouds, his golden voice rang early;
translations.idiomatic: Zongjing won wide praise and was numbered among the Four Outstanding Men; his literary grace rose like clouds, his golden voice sounded early;

sentences.zh: 中遇沈痾，賦詩以訊，忠顯於辭，理出於韻。

translations.literal: Midway he fell into grave illness; he composed a poem to inquire after himself; loyalty showed in his words, principle issued from his rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: In midlife he was struck by grave illness; he wrote a poem to question his fate; loyalty showed in what he wrote, and right principle rose from the cadence.

sentences.zh: 高滄朗達，默識該通，領新悟異，發自心胸；

translations.literal: Langda was clear and penetrating; silently he knew and comprehended all; leading what was new, discerning what was strange, he issued it from his own breast;
translations.idiomatic: Langda was bright and far-reaching; he understood without being told; grasping what was new and discerning what was strange, he brought it forth from his own heart;

sentences.zh: 質侔和璧，文照雕龍，燿姿天邑，衣錦舊邦。

translations.literal: In substance he matched the harmonizing jade; in writing he illuminated the carved dragon; his splendor adorned the capital, and he returned to his old commandery in brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In quality he matched the jade of harmony; in letters he shone like the carved dragon; his brilliance filled the capital, and he went home to his native commandery clothed in glory.

sentences.zh: 士元先覺，介焉不惑，振袂來庭，始賓王國；

translations.literal: Shiyuan was first to awaken; upright and unwavering; shaking out his sleeves he came to court and first became a guest of the royal domain;
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan saw early and stood firm, never in doubt; brushing his sleeves he came to court and was among the first to serve the kingdom as a guest;

sentences.zh: 蹈方履正，好是繩墨，淑人君子，其儀不忒。

translations.literal: Treading the square and walking the straight, he loved the measuring line; a good man and a gentleman—his bearing was without error.
translations.idiomatic: He walked the square path and kept to the straight line; a virtuous man and a true gentleman, his conduct never missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 孔稱游、夏，漢美卿、雲，越哉伯度，出類逾群；

translations.literal: Confucius praised You and Xia; Han honored Qing and Yun; how surpassing was Baidu, rising above his kind and beyond the crowd;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised Ziyou and Zixia; Han glorified Gongqing and Ziyun; how far above the rest was Baidu, exceeding his peers and standing beyond the crowd;

sentences.zh: 司言秘閣，作牧河、汾，移風易俗，理亂解紛。

translations.literal: He spoke for the secretariat and served as governor on the He and Fen; he shifted the winds and changed custom, ordering chaos and unraveling strife.
translations.idiomatic: He held speech for the secretariat and governed along the He and Fen; he changed custom and shifted the winds, putting disorder in order and undoing conflict.

sentences.zh: 融彼滯義，渙此潛文，儒道以析，九流以分。

translations.literal: He melted stagnant meanings and dispersed hidden texts; the Confucian Way was thereby analyzed, the Nine Currents thereby divided.
translations.idiomatic: He dissolved meanings that had stagnated and spread texts that had lain hidden; the Confucian Way was clarified through him, the Nine Schools were sorted through him.

sentences.zh: 崔、宋二賢，誕性英偉，擢穎閭閻，聞名象魏；

translations.literal: The two worthies Cui and Song were born with heroic greatness; they pulled forth their brilliance from village lanes and made their names known at the Elephant Gate;
translations.idiomatic: The two worthies Cui and Song were born heroic and grand; they drew forth their talent from common lanes and made their names heard at the court gate;

sentences.zh: 謇謇儀形，邈邈風氣，達而不矜，素而能貴。

translations.literal: Stern and upright was their bearing; remote and lofty their moral air; accomplished yet not proud, plain yet able to be honored.
translations.idiomatic: Stern was their deportment, lofty their moral bearing; eminent yet never arrogant, simple yet truly worthy of honor.

sentences.zh: 潘符標尚，杜熙好和，清不潔流，渾不同波；

translations.literal: Pan Fu set the standard; Du Xi loved harmony; clear yet not fouled by the stream, muddy yet not of the same wave;
translations.idiomatic: Pan Fu held to his ideals; Du Xi loved concord; one was clear yet not stained by the current, the other turbid yet not swept along by the same tide;

sentences.zh: 絕悕龍津，止分常科，幽而逾顯，損而逾多。

translations.literal: They cut off longing for the dragon ford and stopped at the ordinary grade; hidden yet more manifest, diminished yet more abundant.
translations.idiomatic: They cut off desire for the ford of dragons and rested in ordinary rank; in obscurity they shone the more, in self-denial they gained the more.

sentences.zh: 張綱柔謙，叔術正直，道雅洽聞，弼為兼識；

translations.literal: Zhang Gang was gentle and modest; Shushu was upright; Daoya was widely learned; Biwei had comprehensive knowledge;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang was soft-spoken and humble; Shushu stood straight; Daoya was learned in all he heard; Biwei united many fields of knowledge;

sentences.zh: 拔萃衡門，俱漸鴻翼，發憤忘攵食，豈要鬥食。

translations.literal: Rising above the common gate, together they gradually spread great wings; striving in ardor they forgot to eat—how could they settle for a menial bowl of rice?
translations.idiomatic: Chosen from humble doorways, together they slowly gained the wings of great birds; burning with resolve they forgot their meals—how could they be content with a petty livelihood?

sentences.zh: 率禮從仁，罔愆於式，失不系心，得不形色。

translations.literal: Leading through ritual and following benevolence, they never erred against the norm; loss did not bind their hearts, gain did not show on their faces.
translations.idiomatic: They led by ritual and walked in benevolence, never missing the standard; defeat did not cling to their hearts, success did not alter their bearing.

sentences.zh: 郎苗始舉，用均已試，智是周身，言足為志；

translations.literal: Langmiao was first recommended; his employment was tested by fairness; wisdom filled his whole person; his words fully expressed his will;
translations.idiomatic: Langmiao was first raised up; his use was weighed and tried; intelligence filled his person; his speech was enough to declare his aim;

sentences.zh: 性協于時，情敏於事，與今而同，與古而異。

translations.literal: His nature harmonized with the age; his feeling was keen in affairs; with the present he agreed, from antiquity he differed.
translations.idiomatic: His character accorded with the times; his mind was quick in action; he matched the present yet stood apart from the past.

sentences.zh: 物以利移，人以酒昏，侯生潔己，唯義是敦 ；

translations.literal: Things shift with profit; people are dulled by wine; Hou Sheng kept himself pure and held only to righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Goods move men through gain; wine muddles men through drink; Hou Sheng kept himself undefiled and honored only righteousness;

sentences.zh: 日縱醇醪，逾敬逾溫，其在私室，如涉公門。

translations.literal: Though daily indulging in fine wine, he became more reverent and more gentle; in his private chambers he was as if treading the public hall.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day he poured out rich wine, yet grew more respectful and more mild; even in his private rooms he was as one entering the public gate.

sentences.zh: 季才之性，柔而執競，屆彼南秦，申威致命；

translations.literal: Jicai's nature was gentle yet firm in competition; arriving in Southern Qin, he displayed authority and gave his life on mission;
translations.idiomatic: Jicai by nature was soft yet held to rivalry; when he reached Southern Qin he asserted power and laid down his life on imperial command;

sentences.zh: 誘之以權，矯之以正，帝道用光，邊王內慶。

translations.literal: Enticed by power yet corrected by righteousness, the imperial Way was thereby brightened, border kings inwardly rejoiced;
translations.idiomatic: Led by authority yet straightened by right principle, the imperial Way shone forth and frontier lords rejoiced within;

sentences.zh: 群賢遭世，顯名有代。

translations.literal: Worthies met their age and won fame in their generation.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled worthies met their times and made their names shine in their own age.

sentences.zh: 志竭其忠，才盡其概。

translations.literal: Their wills exhausted their loyalty; their talents exhausted their breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Their intent spent itself in loyalty; their gifts spent themselves in full measure.

sentences.zh: 體襲硃裳，腰紉雙佩，榮曜當時，風高千載；

translations.literal: Their bodies wore vermilion robes; at their waists hung double pendants; glory shone in their age, their moral wind lofty for a thousand years;
translations.idiomatic: They wore crimson robes on their persons and double pendants at their belts; honor blazed in their day, their fame high for a thousand years;

sentences.zh: 君臣相遇，理實難階。

translations.literal: Lord and minister meeting—such a thing is hard to achieve in principle and in reality.
translations.idiomatic: When lord and minister truly meet, reason and fact alike are hard to bring together.

sentences.zh: 昔因朝命，與之克諧，披衿散想，解帶舒懷。

translations.literal: Once by court command we harmonized together; we opened our robes and released our thoughts, loosened our belts and eased our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, by the court's order, we found accord together; we opened our collars and let our thoughts go free, loosened our belts and eased our hearts.

sentences.zh: 此昕猶昨，存亡奄乖，靜言思之，衷心九摧。

translations.literal: That dawn is still like yesterday, yet life and death suddenly parted; in silence I think of it and my innermost heart is nine times crushed.
translations.idiomatic: That morning is still as yesterday, yet life and death were suddenly torn apart; in quiet I think on it and my inmost heart is broken nine times over.

sentences.zh: 揮毫頌德，潛爾增哀。

translations.literal: Wielding the brush to praise virtue only deepens my hidden grief.
translations.idiomatic: To lift the brush and hymn their virtue only adds to my hidden sorrow.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，詔允兼太常至兗州祭孔子廟。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era, an edict ordered Yun, while also serving as Grand Minister of Ceremonies, to go to Yan Province to sacrifice at Confucius's temple.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangxing, an edict appointed Yun, concurrently Grand Minister of Ceremonies, to go to Yan Province and offer sacrifice at the temple of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 謂允曰：「此簡德而行，勿有辭也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yun: "This selects you for your virtue—go, and do not decline."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Yun, "This mission chooses you for your moral worth—go, and do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 」後允從獻文北伐，大捷而還，至武川鎮，上《北伐頌》，帝覽而善之。

translations.literal: Later Yun followed Emperor Xianwen on the northern campaign, returned after a great victory, and at Wuchuan garrison submitted the "Ode to the Northern Expedition"; the emperor read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yun accompanied Emperor Xianwen on the northern expedition and returned in great triumph; at Wuchuan garrison he submitted the "Ode to the Northern Expedition," and the emperor read it with approval.

sentences.zh: 帝時有不豫，以孝文沖幼，欲立京兆王子推，集諸大臣，以次召問。

translations.literal: The emperor was then indisposed; because Emperor Xiaowen was young, he wished to establish Prince Tui of Jingzhao and summoned the great ministers in turn to question them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then unwell; because Emperor Xiaowen was still young, he wished to set up Prince Tui of Jingzhao as heir and summoned the chief ministers one by one to ask their views.

sentences.zh: 允進跪上前，涕泣曰：「臣不敢多言以勞神聽。

translations.literal: Yun stepped forward, knelt before the emperor, and with tears said: "Your servant dares not speak at length and weary Your Majesty's ears."
translations.idiomatic: Yun came forward, knelt before the throne, and weeping said, "Your servant dares not say much and burden Your Majesty's hearing."

sentences.zh: 願陛下上思宗廟托附之重，追念周公抱成王之事。

translations.literal: "May Your Majesty think above on the weight of the ancestral temple's trust and recall how the Duke of Zhou held the young King Cheng."
translations.idiomatic: "May Your Majesty look upward to the heavy trust of the ancestral temple and remember how the Duke of Zhou held the infant King Cheng in his arms."

sentences.zh: 」帝於是傳位於孝文，賜允帛百疋，以標忠亮。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon transferred the throne to Emperor Xiaowen and rewarded Yun with a hundred bolts of silk to mark his loyal candor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then passed the throne to Emperor Xiaowen and granted Yun a hundred bolts of silk to honor his loyal forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 又遷中書監，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was also transferred to Director of the Secretariat and given the additional title of Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Director of the Secretariat with the additional rank of Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 雖久典史事，然不能專勤屬述。

translations.literal: Although he long managed the affairs of historiography, he could not devote himself entirely to compiling and writing.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had long overseen the work of the historians, he could not give himself wholly to drafting and editing.

sentences.zh: 時與校書郎劉模有所緝綴，大較依續崔浩故事，准《春秋》之體而時有刊正。

translations.literal: At the time he did some editing and collation with Collator Liu Mo, broadly following Cui Hao's precedent, conforming to the Spring and Autumn Annals in form while making corrections here and there.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he joined Collator Liu Mo in some editorial work, broadly continuing Cui Hao's model, following the form of the Spring and Autumn Annals while revising where needed.

sentences.zh: 自文成迄于獻文，軍國書檄，多允作也。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wencheng through Emperor Xianwen, most military and state proclamations were written by Yun.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wencheng down to Emperor Xianwen, most military and state dispatches were composed by Yun.

sentences.zh: 末乃薦高閭以自代。

translations.literal: In the end he recommended Gao Lu to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he recommended Gao Lu to take his place.

sentences.zh: 以定議之勳，進爵咸陽公。

translations.literal: For his merit in fixing the succession, he was advanced to Duke of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in settling the succession, he was ennobled as Duke of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 尋授懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Governor of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was made Governor of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 允秋月巡境，問人疾苦。

translations.literal: In autumn Yun toured the circuit, inquiring after the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn month Yun made a circuit of inspection, asking after the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 至邵縣，見邵公廟廢毀不立，乃歎曰：「邵公之德，闕而不祀，為善者何望！

translations.literal: Reaching Shao County, he saw that Duke Shao's temple had fallen into ruin and was not maintained; he sighed: "Duke Shao's virtue goes unhonored—what hope remains for those who do good!"
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Shao County and saw Duke Shao's shrine ruined and left unrepaired, he sighed and said, "Duke Shao's virtue is neglected and unhonored—what can those who do good still hope for?"

sentences.zh: 」乃表修葺之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to have it repaired.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting that it be restored.

sentences.zh: 允于時年將九十矣，勸人學業，風化頗行。

translations.literal: Yun was then nearly ninety years old; he urged people in learning, and moral reform flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was then close to ninety; he encouraged men in their studies, and moral influence spread widely.

sentences.zh: 然儒者優遊，不以斷決為事。

translations.literal: Yet as a Confucian scholar he was easygoing and did not make judicial decision his main work.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as a Confucian he moved at an easy pace and did not take judgment and decision as his chief task.

sentences.zh: 後正光中，中書舍人河內常景追思允，率郡中故老，為允立祠于野王之南，樹碑紀德焉。

translations.literal: Later, in the Zhengguang era, Palace Attendant Chang Jing of Henei, recalling Yun, led the elders of the commandery to erect a shrine to Yun south of Yewang and set up a stele recording his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the Zhengguang era, Palace Attendant Chang Jing of Henei, remembering Yun, led the old men of the commandery to build a shrine to Yun south of Yewang and raise a stele to record his virtue.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，又以老乞還鄉，章十餘上，卒不聽許，遂以疾告歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he again begged to return home on account of age; he submitted more than ten memorials, but in the end permission was not granted, so he pleaded illness and went home.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 2 he again asked to retire home because of old age; he sent up more than ten memorials, but at last was not allowed, so he reported illness and returned.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔以安車征允，敕州郡發遣。

translations.literal: That same year an edict summoned Yun in a comfort carriage and ordered the provinces and commanderies to send him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict summoned Yun in a comfort carriage and instructed the provinces and commanderies to escort him forth.

sentences.zh: 至都，復拜鎮軍大將軍，領中秘書事。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he was again appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and put in charge of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was again made General Who Pacifies the Army and placed in charge of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 固辭，不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined firmly, but permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 扶引就內，改定皇誥；

translations.literal: Supported and led inside, he revised and fixed the Imperial Edict;
translations.idiomatic: Helped in and led within, he revised and settled the Imperial Edict;

sentences.zh: 又被敕，論集往世酒之敗德，以為《酒訓》。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to compile and discuss how wine had ruined virtue in past ages, producing the "Admonition on Wine."
translations.idiomatic: He was also commanded to gather and discuss how wine had destroyed virtue in former ages, and from this he made the "Admonition on Wine."

sentences.zh: 孝文覽而悅之，常置左右，詔允乘車上殿，朝賀不拜。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen read it and was pleased; he always kept it at hand and ordered that Yun might enter the hall in a carriage and need not bow at court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen read it with delight, kept it constantly at his side, and ordered that Yun might ride in a carriage to the hall and need not bow at court felicitations.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔允議定律令。

translations.literal: The following year an edict had Yun take part in deliberating on statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict had Yun join in deliberating on laws and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 雖年漸期頤，而志識無損，猶心存舊職，披考史書。

translations.literal: Though his years approached one hundred, his mind and knowledge were unimpaired; he still kept his old duties in heart and pored over historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Though his years drew near a full century, his will and understanding were undiminished; he still held his former office in mind and examined historical writings.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「允年涉危境，而家貧養薄，可令樂部絲竹十人，五日一詣允，以娛其志。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Yun's years have entered perilous ground, yet his household is poor and his sustenance thin; let ten musicians of the Music Bureau visit Yun every five days to lift his spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "Yun's years have entered dangerous ground, yet his home is poor and his support meager; let ten musicians of the Music Bureau visit Yun every five days to delight his heart."

sentences.zh: 」特賜允蜀牛一頭、四望蜀車一乘、素几杖各一、蜀刀一口。

translations.literal: He was specially granted one Shu ox, one four-canopied Shu carriage, one plain armrest staff each, and one Shu knife.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted one Shu ox, one four-canopied Shu carriage, one plain armrest and one plain staff, and one Shu knife.

sentences.zh: 又賜珍味，每春秋致之。

translations.literal: Delicacies were also granted and sent every spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Fine foods were also granted and delivered each spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 尋詔朝晡給禦膳，朔望致牛酒，衣服綿絹，每月送給。

translations.literal: Soon an edict provided imperial meals morning and evening, beef and wine on the first and fifteenth of the month, clothing of cotton and silk sent monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict provided imperial fare morning and evening, beef and wine on the new and full moon, and cotton and silk garments sent every month.

sentences.zh: 允皆分之親故。

translations.literal: Yun shared all of it among relatives and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Yun divided all of it among kin and old friends.

sentences.zh: 是時貴臣之門，並羅列顯官，而允子弟，皆無官爵，其廉退若此。

translations.literal: At that time the gates of great ministers all bristled with high offices, yet none of Yun's sons and younger kinsmen held rank or title—such was his modest restraint.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the households of great ministers were lined with eminent posts, yet none of Yun's sons or younger relatives held rank or title—such was his modest withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Secretariat and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of the Secretariat and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時延入，備几杖，詢以政事。

translations.literal: From time to time he was summoned in; armrests and staff were provided and he was consulted on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he was invited in; armrest and staff were prepared and he was questioned on affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 十年，加光祿大夫，金章紫綬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was given the additional rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 朝之大議，皆諮訪焉。

translations.literal: On major deliberations at court all consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: On great matters debated at court, all sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，有事西郊，詔御馬車迎允就郊所板殿觀矚。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month, when there were rites at the Western Suburb, an edict sent the imperial carriage to bring Yun to the plank hall at the suburban site to observe.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the fourth month, when rites were held at the Western Suburb, an edict sent the imperial carriage to bring Yun to the plank hall at the suburban altar to watch.

sentences.zh: 馬忽驚奔，車覆，傷眉三處。

translations.literal: The horse suddenly bolted in fright, the carriage overturned, and he was injured in three places on his brow.
translations.idiomatic: The horse suddenly panicked and ran; the carriage overturned and he was wounded in three places on his brow.

sentences.zh: 孝文、文明太后遣醫藥護療，存問相望。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming sent physicians and medicines for his care; messages of concern followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming sent doctors and medicine to treat him, and inquiries of concern came in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 司駕將處重坐，允啟陳無恙，乞免其罪。

translations.literal: The Master of Carriages was about to impose heavy punishment; Yun memorialized that he was unharmed and begged that the driver's offense be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Carriages was about to impose severe punishment; Yun memorialized that he was unhurt and asked that the driver's crime be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 先是，命中黃門蘇興壽扶侍允，曾雪中遇犬驚倒，扶者大懼，允慰勉之，不令聞徹。

translations.literal: Earlier, the palace had ordered Inner Gate Attendant Su Xingshou to support Yun; once in snow he was startled by a dog and fell, and the attendant was greatly terrified—Yun comforted and encouraged him and would not let the matter be reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had ordered Inner Gate Attendant Su Xingshou to support Yun; once in the snow he was startled by a dog and fell, and the attendant was greatly afraid—Yun comforted him and would not allow the matter to be reported.

sentences.zh: 興壽稱共允接事三年，不嚐見其忿色。

translations.literal: Xingshou said that in three years of serving Yun together, he had never once seen him show anger.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshou said that in three years of attending Yun together, he had never once seen anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 恂恂善誘，誨人不倦，晝夜手常執書，吟詠尋覽。

translations.literal: Mild and good at guiding others, never weary in instruction, day and night his hand always held a book as he recited and read.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and skilled at guiding others, never weary in teaching, day and night his hand always held a book as he chanted and read.

sentences.zh: 篤親念故，虛己存納，雖處貴重，志同貧素。

translations.literal: Devoted to kin and mindful of old ties, empty of self and receptive to others—even in high station his heart was like that of the poor and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in affection for kin and mindful of old friends, empty of self and open to others—though he stood in high honor, his heart was like that of the poor and plain.

sentences.zh: 性好音樂，每至伶人弦歌鼓舞，常擊節稱善。

translations.literal: He loved music by nature; whenever performers sang to string and drum, he would beat time and praise them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music by nature; whenever musicians played strings and sang and dancers performed, he would beat time and praise them.

sentences.zh: 又雅信佛道，時設齋講，好生惡殺。

translations.literal: He also deeply revered the Buddhist Way, often held vegetarian feasts and lectures, loved life and hated killing.
translations.idiomatic: He also deeply honored the Buddhist Way, often set out vegetarian feasts and lectures, loved life and abhorred killing.

sentences.zh: 魏初法嚴，朝士多見杖罰。

translations.literal: In early Wei the law was severe and many court officials suffered beating.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wei the law was strict and many court officials were beaten.

sentences.zh: 允曆事五帝，出入三省五十餘年，初無譴咎。

translations.literal: Yun served through five emperors, going in and out of the Three Departments for more than fifty years, and from the first never met reproach or punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yun served five emperors, entering and leaving the Three Departments for more than fifty years, and from the beginning never met censure or punishment.

sentences.zh: 始真君中，以獄訟留滯，始令中書以經義斷諸疑事。

translations.literal: Beginning in the Zhenjun era, because lawsuits were delayed, it was first ordered that the Secretariat decide doubtful cases by classical principles.
translations.idiomatic: Starting in the Zhenjun era, because court cases were backlogged, it was first ordered that the Secretariat decide doubtful matters by classical principle.

sentences.zh: 允據律評刑，三十餘載，內外稱平。

translations.literal: Yun judged punishments according to the statutes for more than thirty years, and within and without the court he was called fair.
translations.idiomatic: Yun assessed punishments according to the statutes for more than thirty years, and inside and outside the court he was called even-handed.

sentences.zh: 允以獄者人命所系，常歎曰：「皋陶至德也，其後英、蓼先亡；

translations.literal: Because imprisonment concerns men's lives, Yun often sighed and said: "Gao Yao was of the highest virtue, yet afterward Ying and Liao perished first;
translations.idiomatic: Because prisons bind up men's lives, Yun often sighed and said, "Gao Yao was of the utmost virtue, yet afterward Ying and Liao perished first;

sentences.zh: 劉、項之際，英布黥而王。

translations.literal: At the time of Liu and Xiang, Ying Bu was tattooed yet became king.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Liu and Xiang, Ying Bu was branded yet became king.

sentences.zh: 經世雖久，猶有刑之餘釁。

translations.literal: Though the world has lasted long, there remain the after-stains of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Though generations have passed, the lingering taint of punishment still remains.

sentences.zh: 況凡人能無咎乎？

translations.literal: How much less can ordinary men be without fault?
translations.idiomatic: How much less can common men be free of blame?

sentences.zh: 」性簡至，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: His nature was plain and direct; he did not associate lightly.
translations.idiomatic: His character was simple and upright; he did not make friends lightly.

sentences.zh: 獻文之平青、齊，徙其族望於代。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianwen pacified Qing and Qi, he relocated their clan elites to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen conquered Qing and Qi, he moved their leading clans to Dai.

sentences.zh: 時諸士人，流移遠至，率皆饑寒。

translations.literal: At the time many scholars, driven far in displacement, were almost all hungry and cold.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many scholars, displaced from afar, were almost all starving and freezing.

sentences.zh: 徙人之中，多允姻媾，皆徒步造門。

translations.literal: Among the displaced were many connected to Yun by marriage; all came to his gate on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Among the relocated were many linked to Yun by marriage, and all came to his door on foot.

sentences.zh: 允散財竭產，以相贍振，慰問周至，無不感其仁厚。

translations.literal: Yun spent his wealth and exhausted his estate to support and relieve them; his inquiries were thorough, and none failed to be moved by his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Yun scattered his wealth and emptied his property to feed and succor them; his inquiries were thorough, and none failed to feel his kindness and depth.

sentences.zh: 又隨其才能，表奏申用。

translations.literal: He also, according to their abilities, memorialized to have them employed.
translations.idiomatic: He also, according to each man's talent, memorialized to have them put to use.

sentences.zh: 時議者皆以新附致異，允謂取材任能，無宜抑屈。

translations.literal: At the time critics held that newly attached men should be treated differently; Yun said talent should be selected and ability employed—there was no reason to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time critics said the newly submitted should be treated as outsiders; Yun said one should choose material and assign ability—there was no call to hold them down.

sentences.zh: 先是，允被召在方山作頌，志氣猶不多損，談說舊事，了無所遺。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yun was summoned to compose an ode at Fangshan, his spirit was still not much diminished; he spoke of old events and left nothing out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yun was summoned to Fangshan to compose an ode, his vigor was still little diminished; he spoke of old affairs and forgot nothing.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月卒，年九十八。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year he died, aged ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year he died at the age of ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 初，允每謂人曰：「吾在中書時有陰德，濟救人命，若陽報不差，吾壽應享百年矣。

translations.literal: Initially Yun often told people: "When I was in the Secretariat I accumulated hidden virtue and saved men's lives; if the public reward is not mistaken, my span ought to reach a hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: From the first Yun often told people, "When I served in the Secretariat I built up hidden virtue and saved men's lives; if open reward does not err, my years should reach a full century."

sentences.zh: 」先卒旬外，微有不適，猶不寢臥，呼醫請藥，出入行止，吟詠如常。

translations.literal: More than ten days before he died he felt slight discomfort, yet still did not take to bed; he called physicians and asked for medicine, going in and out and moving about, reciting as usual.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days before his death he felt slight illness, yet still did not lie down; he summoned doctors and asked for medicine, coming and going and moving about, chanting as always.

sentences.zh: 孝文、文明太后聞而遣醫李修往脈視之，告以無恙。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming heard, they sent Physician Li Xiu to feel his pulse and reported that he was well.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming heard of it, they sent Physician Li Xiu to examine his pulse and were told he was unharmed.

sentences.zh: 修入，密陳允榮衛有異，懼其不久。

translations.literal: When Xiu entered he secretly stated that Yun's pulse and protective qi were strange and feared he would not last long.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu went in he secretly reported that Yun's pulse and protective qi were abnormal and feared he would not long survive.

sentences.zh: 於是遣使備賜禦膳珍羞，自酒米至於鹽醢，百有餘品，皆盡時味。

translations.literal: Thereupon emissaries were sent with full provision of imperial delicacies—from wine and grain to salt and pickles, more than a hundred kinds, all at the peak of season.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon messengers were sent bearing a full grant of imperial delicacies—from wine and grain to salt and pickles, more than a hundred kinds, all at the height of season.

sentences.zh: 及床帳衣服，茵被几杖，羅列於庭。

translations.literal: Bed curtains and clothing, mats and coverings, armrests and staffs were arrayed in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Beds and curtains, clothing, mats and covers, armrests and staffs were lined up in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 王官往還，慰問相屬。

translations.literal: Court officers came and went; messages of sympathy followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Palace officers went back and forth, and inquiries of concern came in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 允喜形於色，語人曰：「天恩以我篤老，大有所齎，得以贍客矣。

translations.literal: Yun showed pleasure on his face and told people: "Heaven's grace, seeing my great age, has sent abundant gifts—I can now provide for my guests."
translations.idiomatic: Yun showed joy in his face and told people, "Heaven's favor, seeing my great age, has sent rich gifts—I can now entertain my guests."

sentences.zh: 」表謝而已，不有他慮。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial of thanks and nothing more; he had no other thought.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial of thanks and nothing else; he had no other concern.

sentences.zh: 如是數日，夜中卒，家人莫覺。

translations.literal: After several days like this, he died in the middle of the night; his household did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: After several days in this way, he died in the middle of the night, and his family did not know.

sentences.zh: 詔給絹一千疋、布二千疋、綿五百斤、錦五十疋、雜彩百疋、穀千斛，以周喪用。

translations.literal: An edict granted a thousand bolts of silk, two thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of cotton, fifty bolts of brocade, a hundred bolts of mixed colored silk, and a thousand hu of grain for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted a thousand bolts of silk, two thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of cotton, fifty bolts of brocade, a hundred bolts of mixed colored silk, and a thousand hu of grain to cover the funeral costs.

sentences.zh: 魏初以來，存亡蒙齎者莫及，朝廷榮之。

translations.literal: Since the founding of Wei, none had received such gifts in life or death; the court honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Wei, none honored in life or death had received such gifts; the court gloried in it.

sentences.zh: 將葬，贈侍中、司空公、冀州刺史，將軍、公如故。

translations.literal: When he was about to be buried, he was posthumously given the offices of Palace Attendant, Duke of Works, and Governor of Ji Province; his generalship and dukedom remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to be buried, he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, Duke of Works, and Governor of Ji Province; his generalship and ducal title remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文，賜命服一襲。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wen, and one set of court robes was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Wen, and one set of court robes was granted.

sentences.zh: 允所制詩賦詠頌箴論表贊誄、《左氏釋》、《公羊釋》、《毛詩拾遺》、《雜解》、《議何鄭膏肓事》凡百餘篇，別有集，行於世。

translations.literal: Yun's compositions—poems, rhapsodies, odes, eulogies, admonitions, treatises, memorials, praises, dirges; "Explication of the Zuo Tradition," "Explication of the Gongyang Tradition," "Recovered Fragments of the Mao Odes," "Miscellaneous Explications," and "Discussion of the Terminal Illness of He and Zheng"—altogether more than a hundred works, were collected separately and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's works—poems, rhapsodies, songs, eulogies, admonitions, treatises, memorials, praises, and dirges; "Explication of the Zuo Tradition," "Explication of the Gongyang Tradition," "Recovered Fragments of the Mao Odes," "Miscellaneous Explications," and "Discussion of the Terminal Illness of He and Zheng"—more than a hundred pieces in all, were gathered in a separate collection and circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 允尤明演算法，為《算術》三卷。

translations.literal: Yun was especially skilled in computational methods and wrote Arithmetic in three fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was especially versed in computational methods and composed Arithmetic in three fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子忱，字士和，位長安太守，為政寬惠，百姓安之。

translations.literal: His son Chen, styled Shihe, held the post of Governor of Chang'an; his governance was generous and kind, and the people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen, styled Shihe, served as Governor of Chang'an; his rule was generous and kind, and the people lived in peace under him.

sentences.zh: 後例降爵為侯，卒，子貴賓襲。

translations.literal: Later, by regulation his rank was reduced to marquis; when he died, his son Guibin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent his title was reduced to marquis; when he died, his son Guibin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 忱弟懷，字士仁，恬淡退靜，位太尉、東陽王丕諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Huai, styled Shiren, was tranquil and retiring; he held the post of Staff Adviser to the Grand Commander, Prince Pi of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother Huai, styled Shiren, was quiet and withdrawn by nature and served as Staff Adviser to the Grand Commander, Prince Pi of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 子綽，字僧裕。

translations.literal: His son Chuo, styled Sengyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chuo, styled Sengyu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，恭敏自立。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was reverent and diligent and stood on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was respectful and attentive and made his own way in the world.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi in height, his waist ten wei in girth.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, with a waist ten wei around.

sentences.zh: 沈雅有度量，博涉經史。

translations.literal: Deeply refined and broad-minded, he ranged widely through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply cultured and magnanimous, he read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 稍遷洛陽令，為政強直，不避豪右，京邑憚之。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Magistrate of Luoyang; his governance was forceful and upright, he did not shrink from the powerful great families, and the capital feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by degrees to Magistrate of Luoyang, where his rule was firm and straight; he never flinched before the great clans, and the capital stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanchang, he served as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yanchang era, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後為御史中尉元匡奏高聰及綽朋附高肇，詔並原罪。

translations.literal: Later the Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang memorialized against Gao Cong and Chuo for banding together with Gao Zhao; an edict pardoned them both.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang accused Gao Cong and Chuo of attaching themselves to Gao Zhao; an edict pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 曆豫、並二州刺史，卒，諡文簡。

translations.literal: He served successively as Inspector of Yu and Bing provinces; when he died, he was posthumously titled Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Inspector of Yu and Bing provinces; when he died, he was given the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 允弟推，字仲讓，早有名譽。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Tui, styled Zhongrang, early gained fame and repute.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother Tui, styled Zhongrang, won renown early in life.

sentences.zh: 太延中，以前後南使不稱，妙簡行人，游雅薦推應選。

translations.literal: In Taiyan, because successive envoys to the south had proved unsatisfactory, the court carefully selected travelers; You Ya recommended Tui as fit for selection.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiyan, successive southern envoys had proved inadequate, so the court carefully chose new emissaries; You Ya recommended Tui for the mission.

sentences.zh: 詔兼散騎常侍使宋，南人稱其才辯。

translations.literal: By edict he was additionally appointed Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and sent as envoy to Song; the southerners praised his talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him concurrently Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and envoy to Song; the southerners praised his wit and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 卒於建業，贈臨邑子，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died at Jianye; posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Linyi, with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Jianye and was posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Linyi, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 推弟燮，字季和，亦有文才。

translations.literal: Tui's younger brother Xie, styled Jihe, also possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Tui's younger brother Xie, styled Jihe, had literary gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 太武每詔征，辭疾不應，恆笑允屈折久官，棲泊京邑，常從容於家。

translations.literal: Each time Emperor Taiwu summoned him by edict, he pleaded illness and did not respond; he always laughed that Yun had bent himself to long service in office and lingered in the capital, while he himself lived at ease at home.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Taiwu summoned him by edict, he pleaded illness and refused to come; he often mocked Yun for bending to long years in office and lingering in the capital, while he himself lived at leisure at home.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，卒。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as Chief Clerk; he died.
translations.idiomatic: The province recruited him as Chief Clerk; he died in that post.

sentences.zh: 孫市賓，永熙中，開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: His grandson Shibin, in Yongxi, served as Attendant-in-Ordinary on the staff of an office-opening general.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shibin, during Yongxi, served as Attendant-in-Ordinary on the staff of a general who had opened an office.

sentences.zh: 始神蒨中，允與從叔濟、族兄毗及同郡李金俱被征。

translations.literal: In the early years of Shenqi, Yun, together with his uncle Ji, his clansman cousin Pi, and Jin Li of the same commandery, were all summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shenqi period, Yun was summoned along with his uncle Ji, his clansman cousin Pi, and Jin Li of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 濟位滄水太守、浮陽子。

translations.literal: Ji held the posts of Governor of Cangshui and Marquis of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji held office as Governor of Cangshui and was ennobled as Marquis of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冀州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously awarded Inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Inspector of Jizhou and given the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子矯襲。

translations.literal: His son Jiao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 矯弟遵，字世禮。

translations.literal: Jiao's younger brother Zun, styled Shili.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's younger brother was Zun, styled Shili.

sentences.zh: 賤出，其兄矯等常欺侮之，及父亡，不令在喪位。

translations.literal: Born of a low-status mother, his elder brothers Jiao and the others often bullied and humiliated him; when their father died, they would not let him take his place in the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a concubine, he was often bullied by his elder brothers Jiao and the rest; when their father died, they refused to let him take his proper place in mourning.

sentences.zh: 遵遂馳赴平城，歸允。

translations.literal: Zun thereupon galloped to Pingcheng and returned to Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zun rode at once to Pingcheng and sought refuge with Yun.

sentences.zh: 允為作計，乃為遵父舉哀，以遵為喪主，京邑無不吊集，朝貴咸識之。

translations.literal: Yun devised a plan for him: he held mourning for Zun's father, made Zun chief mourner, and everyone in the capital came to offer condolences; the court nobles all came to know him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun laid a plan: he arranged mourning for Zun's father, installed Zun as chief mourner, and the whole capital turned out to condole; the great officials of the court all came to know him.

sentences.zh: 徐歸奔止。

translations.literal: Slowly he returned and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he slowly make his way home.

sentences.zh: 免喪後，為營宦路。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, Yun arranged an official career for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, Yun opened the way to office for him.

sentences.zh: 遵感成益之恩，事允如諸父。

translations.literal: Zun felt gratitude for the kindness that had secured his standing, and served Yun as he would his own uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the favor that had established him, Zun treated Yun as he would his own uncles.

sentences.zh: 涉曆文史，頗有筆劄。

translations.literal: He ranged through literature and history and was quite skilled with the brush.
translations.idiomatic: He had read widely in literature and history and wrote with considerable skill.

sentences.zh: 隨都將長廣公侯窮奇等平定三齊。

translations.literal: He followed the capital general the Prince of Changguang, Hou Qiongqi, and others in pacifying the Three Qis.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the capital garrison general, Prince Changguang Hou Qiongqi, and others in the pacification of the Three Qis.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵高昌男，補安定王相。

translations.literal: For his merit he was ennobled as Baron of Gaochang and appointed Chancellor to the Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was ennobled Baron of Gaochang and appointed Chancellor to the Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 撰太和、安昌二殿畫圖。

translations.literal: He compiled illustrated records of the Taihe and Anchang palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled illustrated records of the Taihe and Anchang palace halls.

sentences.zh: 後與中書令高閭增改律令，進中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Later, together with Director of the Secretariat Gao Lu, he revised and amended the statutes and ordinances, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Director of the Secretariat Gao Lu in revising the statutes and ordinances and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 假中書令，詣長安，刊燕宣王廟碑，進爵安昌子。

translations.literal: Acting as Director of the Secretariat, he went to Chang'an to engrave the memorial stele for Prince Xuan of Yan and was advanced to Marquis of Anchang.
translations.idiomatic: Serving temporarily as Director of the Secretariat, he went to Chang'an to cut the memorial stele for Prince Xuan of Yan and was raised to Marquis of Anchang.

sentences.zh: 使濟、兗、徐三州，觀風理訟。

translations.literal: He was sent to Ji, Yan, and Xu provinces to observe local customs and adjudicate lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched to Ji, Yan, and Xu provinces to inspect local customs and settle lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 進中都令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 及新制衣冠，孝文恭薦宗廟，遵形貌莊潔，音氣雄暢，常兼太祝令；

translations.literal: When new robes and caps were instituted and Emperor Xiaowen reverently offered at the ancestral temple, Zun's appearance was dignified and pure, his voice resonant and clear, and he regularly served concurrently as Director of Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: When new ceremonial robes and caps were introduced and Emperor Xiaowen reverently presented offerings at the ancestral temple, Zun's bearing was solemn and clean and his voice strong and clear; he regularly served concurrently as Director of Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 跪贊禮事，為俯仰之節，粗合儀矩，由是帝頗識待之。

translations.literal: kneeling to intone the ritual praises, he set the movements of bowing and rising and roughly conformed to ceremonial rule; because of this the emperor came to know and favor him.
translations.idiomatic: kneeling to recite the ritual praises, he governed the motions of bowing and rising and roughly matched proper ceremony; the emperor took notice and treated him with favor.

sentences.zh: 後與游明根、高閭、李沖等入議律令，親對御坐，時有陳奏。

translations.literal: Later, together with You Minggen, Gao Lu, Li Chong, and others, he entered deliberations on statutes and ordinances, speaking directly before the imperial seat and offering memorials from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined You Minggen, Gao Lu, Li Chong, and others in deliberating on statutes and ordinances, speaking face to face before the throne and submitting proposals as occasion arose.

sentences.zh: 出為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 建節曆本州，宗鄉改觀，而矯等彌妒毀之。

translations.literal: Bearing the staff of authority he passed through his native province, and clansmen and neighbors changed their view of him; yet Jiao and the others only grew more jealous and slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his home province bearing the insignia of office, and kin and neighbors looked on him with new respect; yet Jiao and his faction grew only more envious and spread slander against him.

sentences.zh: 遵性不廉清。

translations.literal: Zun's character was not clean or upright.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was neither clean nor upright in character.

sentences.zh: 在中書時，每假歸山東，必借備騾馬，將從百餘，屯逼人家，不得絲縑滿意，則詬詈不去。

translations.literal: While at the Secretariat, whenever he took leave to return to Shandong he always requisitioned mules and horses and more than a hundred attendants; he quartered them at people's houses, and if he did not obtain silk to his satisfaction he cursed and reviled them and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at the Secretariat, each leave back to Shandong saw him requisition mules and horses and more than a hundred followers; he billeted them on private households, and unless he got silk to his liking he cursed and reviled the hosts and refused to move on.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，縑布千數，郡邑苦之。

translations.literal: Within a month or so, silk and cloth numbered in the thousands; commanderies and districts suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month or two he extorted thousands of bolts of silk and cloth, to the misery of every commandery and district.

sentences.zh: 既蒞方岳，本意未弭，選召僚吏，多所取紅納。

translations.literal: Once he took up a provincial post, his original intent was not stilled; in selecting and summoning subordinate officials, he took many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed as a provincial governor, his old habits did not abate; in choosing subordinates he accepted bribes from many of them.

sentences.zh: 又其妻明氏，家在齊州，母弟舅甥，共相憑屬，爭取貨利。

translations.literal: Moreover his wife was of the Ming clan; her family was in Qi Province, and maternal brothers, younger brothers, and maternal nephews relied on one another to compete for profit.
translations.idiomatic: His wife belonged to the Ming clan of Qi Province; her brothers, maternal kin, and nephews leaned on one another to grab profits.

sentences.zh: 嚴暴，非理殺害甚多。

translations.literal: He was harsh and violent and unlawfully killed a great many people.
translations.idiomatic: He was brutal and violent, and a great many were killed without cause.

sentences.zh: 貪酷之響，帝頗聞之。

translations.literal: Reports of his greed and cruelty reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Word of his greed and cruelty gradually reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及車駕幸鄴，遵自州來朝。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Ye, Zun came from his province to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Ye, Zun came from his province to attend court.

sentences.zh: 會有赦宥，遵臨還州，請辭。

translations.literal: It happened that there was an amnesty; as Zun was about to return to his province, he requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty happened to be proclaimed; on the eve of returning to his province, Zun asked leave to depart.

sentences.zh: 帝於行宮引見誚讓之。

translations.literal: The emperor received him at the traveling palace and rebuked and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him at the traveling palace and rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 遵自陳無負。

translations.literal: Zun declared himself innocent of wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Zun protested that he had done nothing wrong.

sentences.zh: 帝厲聲曰：「若無遷都赦，必無高遵矣！

translations.literal: The emperor said in a harsh voice: "If not for the amnesty tied to the move of the capital, there would be no Gao Zun left!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said sharply: "But for the amnesty tied to the relocation of the capital, Gao Zun would be finished!

sentences.zh: 又卿非唯貪婪，又虐於刑法」。

translations.literal: Moreover you are not only greedy, you are also cruel in the application of punishments."
translations.idiomatic: And you are not merely greedy—you are brutal in your use of the law."

sentences.zh: 謂：「何如濟陰王，猶不免於法。

translations.literal: He said: "What of the Prince of Jiyin—he still could not escape the law.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Consider the Prince of Jiyin—even he could not escape the law.

sentences.zh: 卿何人，而為此行！

translations.literal: Who are you, to behave in this way!
translations.idiomatic: Who are you, to act as you have!

sentences.zh: 自今宜自謹約。

translations.literal: From now on you should restrain yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter you must discipline yourself."

sentences.zh: 」還州，仍不悛革。

translations.literal: " When he returned to his province, he still did not repent and reform.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to his province, he still did not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 齊州人孟僧振至洛訟遵，詔廷尉少卿鄧述窮鞫，皆如所訴。

translations.literal: Meng Zhen of Qi Province came to Luoyang to sue Zun; an edict ordered Vice Director of the Court of Judicature Deng Shu to investigate thoroughly, and everything proved as charged.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhen of Qi Province traveled to Luoyang to bring suit against Zun; an edict ordered Vice Director of the Court of Judicature Deng Shu to investigate to the end, and every charge was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 先，沙門道登過遵。

translations.literal: Earlier, the monk Daodeng had passed through Zun's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the monk Daodeng had passed through Zun's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 遵以道登荷眷于孝文，多奉以貨，深托仗之。

translations.literal: Because Daodeng enjoyed Emperor Xiaowen's favor, Zun lavished goods on him and deeply relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Daodeng enjoyed Emperor Xiaowen's favor, Zun showered him with gifts and leaned on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 道登屢因言次，申啟救遵，帝不省納，遂詔述賜遵死。

translations.literal: Daodeng repeatedly took occasion in conversation to intercede and plead for Zun, but the emperor would not heed it; he then ordered Deng to sentence Zun to death.
translations.idiomatic: Daodeng repeatedly interceded for Zun in conversation, but the emperor would not listen; an edict then ordered Deng to sentence Zun to death.

sentences.zh: 時遵子元榮詣洛訟冤，猶恃道登，不時還赴。

translations.literal: At the time Zun's son Yuanrong had come to Luoyang to plead his father's innocence; still relying on Daodeng, he did not return in time.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zun's son Yuanrong had come to Luoyang to plead his father's case; still counting on Daodeng, he did not return in time.

sentences.zh: 道登知事決，方乃遣之。

translations.literal: When Daodeng knew the matter was decided, only then did he send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Daodeng knew the outcome was sealed did he send him on his way.

sentences.zh: 遵恨其妻，不與訣，別處沐浴，引椒而死。

translations.literal: Zun hated his wife, would not bid her farewell, bathed apart, and drank pepper poison to die.
translations.idiomatic: Zun hated his wife, refused a parting word, bathed apart, and killed himself by drinking pepper poison.

sentences.zh: 元榮學尚有文才，長於几案。

translations.literal: Yuanrong was learned and possessed literary talent, and excelled at desk work.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrong was learned and had literary talent, and excelled at administrative work.

sentences.zh: 位兼尚書右丞，為西道行台，至高平鎮，遇城翻，被害。

translations.literal: He held the concurrent post of Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, served on the Western Route Army Staff, reached Gaoping garrison, encountered a city revolt, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and on the Western Route Army Staff; at Gaoping garrison he was caught in a city revolt and killed.

sentences.zh: 遵弟次文，雖無位宦，而貲產巨萬。

translations.literal: Zun's younger brother Ciwen, though without office or rank, had property worth tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's younger brother Ciwen held no office, yet his wealth ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 遵每責其財，又結憾於遵，吉凶不相往反。

translations.literal: Zun constantly demanded his money, and Ciwen also harbored resentment against Zun; for joys and sorrows they no longer visited one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zun constantly squeezed him for money, and Ciwen came to bear a grudge; they ceased exchanging visits in times of joy or mourning.

sentences.zh: 時論責之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion censured him.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 毗字子翼，鄉邑稱為長者，位征南從事中郎。

translations.literal: Pi, styled Ziyi, was called an elder of virtue in his home district and held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Southern Campaign Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Pi, styled Ziyi, was known in his home district as a man of virtue and served as Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Southern Campaign Staff.

sentences.zh: 初，允所引劉模者，長樂信都人，頗涉經籍。

translations.literal: At the outset, Liu Mo, whom Yun had brought in, was a man of Xindu in Changle and had read widely in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, Liu Mo—whom Yun had recruited—was from Xindu in Changle and had read widely in the classics.

sentences.zh: 允撰修國記，選為校書郎，與其緝著。

translations.literal: When Yun compiled the National History, Mo was selected as Proofreader and collaborated with him in the writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun undertook the National History, Mo was chosen as Proofreader and worked with him on the compilation.

sentences.zh: 常令模帶持管籥，每日同入史閣，接膝對筵，屬述時事。

translations.literal: Yun regularly had Mo carry and hold the archive keys; each day they entered the Historical Archives together, sitting knee to knee across their mats, composing accounts of current events.
translations.idiomatic: Yun regularly had Mo carry the archive keys; each day they entered the Historical Archives together, sitting knee to knee at their desks to set down current affairs.

sentences.zh: 允年已九十，手目稍衰，多遣模執筆而占授裁斷之，如此者五六歲。

translations.literal: Yun was already ninety; his hand and eyes had gradually declined, and he often had Mo take the brush while he dictated and made final judgments—this continued for five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was already ninety; his hand and eyes were failing, and he often had Mo write while he dictated and decided—this went on for five or six years.

sentences.zh: 允所成篇卷，模預有功。

translations.literal: In the completed fascicles Yun produced, Mo had a share in the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Mo contributed substantially to the fascicles Yun completed.

sentences.zh: 太和中，除南潁川太守。

translations.literal: In Taihe, he was appointed Governor of Southern Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he was appointed Governor of Southern Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 王肅之歸闕，路經縣瓠，羈旅窮悴，時人莫識。

translations.literal: When Wang Su returned to court, his route passed through Xiangfu; he was a traveler in destitution and exhaustion, and no one of the time recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su returned to court, he passed through Xiangfu as a destitute traveler in wretched straits, and no one recognized him.

sentences.zh: 模獨經給所須，吊待以禮，肅深感其意。

translations.literal: Mo alone supplied what he needed and received and treated him with courtesy; Su was deeply moved by his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Mo alone supplied his needs and received him with full courtesy; Wang Su was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 及肅臨豫州，模猶在郡，征報復之，由是為新蔡太守。

translations.literal: When Su took up office as Inspector of Yuzhou, Mo was still in the commandery; Su summoned him to repay the favor, and Mo thereby became Governor of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su became Inspector of Yuzhou, Mo was still in the district; Wang summoned him to repay the kindness, and Mo was appointed Governor of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 在二郡積十年，寬猛相濟，頗有聲稱。

translations.literal: Over ten years in the two commanderies, blending leniency and severity, he gained considerable repute.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years across two commanderies he mixed leniency with severity and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 遷陳留太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 時年七十餘矣，而飾老隱年，昧禁自效。

translations.literal: He was then over seventy, yet he feigned old age and concealed his years, violating the prohibition to offer himself for service.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was over seventy, yet he disguised his age and concealed his years, defying the age limit to keep serving.

sentences.zh: 遂家于南潁川，不復歸其舊鄉矣。

translations.literal: He then made his home in Southern Yingchuan and no longer returned to his old native place.
translations.idiomatic: He settled in Southern Yingchuan and never returned to his old home.

sentences.zh: 祐字子集，允之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: You, styled Ziji, was Yun's second cousin once removed.
translations.idiomatic: You, styled Ziji, was Yun's second cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 本名禧，以與咸陽王同名，孝文賜名焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Xi; because it was the same as the Prince of Xianyang's name, Emperor Xiaowen bestowed this name on him.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Xi; because it matched the name of the Prince of Xianyang, Emperor Xiaowen gave him this new name.

sentences.zh: 祖展，慕容寶黃門郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhan was a Palace Attendant under Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhan served Murong Bao as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 道武平中山，徙京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, the family was moved to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, the family was relocated to the capital.

sentences.zh: 卒於三都大官。

translations.literal: He died as Director of the Three Kitchens.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Director of the Three Kitchens.

sentences.zh: 父讜，從太武滅赫連昌，以功賜爵南皮子。

translations.literal: His father Dan followed Emperor Taiwu in destroying Helian Chang and, for his merit, was ennobled as Marquis of Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan followed Emperor Taiwu in the destruction of Helian Chang and, for his service, was ennobled Marquis of Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 與崔浩共參著作，位中書侍郎、給事中、冀青二州中正。

translations.literal: Together with Cui Hao he participated in compiling historical works; he held the posts of Vice Director of the Secretariat, Palace Provisioner, and Rectifier for Ji and Qing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: With Cui Hao he helped compile historical works and held office as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Palace Provisioner, and Rectifier for Ji and Qing provinces.

sentences.zh: 假散騎常侍、蓚縣侯，使高麗。

translations.literal: Acting as Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and Marquis of Liu County, he was sent as envoy to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Acting Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and Marquis of Liu County, he was dispatched as envoy to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冀州刺史，假滄水公，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously made Inspector of Jizhou, provisionally titled Duke of Cangshui, with the posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Inspector of Jizhou and provisionally ennobled Duke of Cangshui, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 祐兄祚襲爵，位東青州刺史。

translations.literal: You's elder brother Zuo inherited the title and held the post of Inspector of Eastern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: You's elder brother Zuo inherited the title and served as Inspector of Eastern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 祐博涉書史，好文字雜說，性通放，不拘小節。

translations.literal: You ranged widely through books and histories, loved miscellaneous writings and exegesis, and by nature was open and free, not bound by small proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: You read widely in books and histories, loved philology and miscellaneous learning, and was by nature expansive and unconstrained by petty rules.

sentences.zh: 自中書學生再遷中書侍郎，賜爵建康子。

translations.literal: From Secretariat student he was promoted twice to Vice Director of the Secretariat and was ennobled as Marquis of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from Secretariat student, he was promoted twice to Vice Director of the Secretariat and ennobled Marquis of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 文成末，兗州東郡吏獲一異獸，送之京師，時無識者，詔以問祐。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign, an official of Dongjun in Yan Province captured a strange beast and sent it to the capital; no one of the time could identify it, and an edict ordered You to be asked.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign, an official of Dongjun in Yan Province caught a strange beast and sent it to the capital; no one could identify it, and the court asked You.

sentences.zh: 祐曰：「此是三吳所出，厥名鯪鯉。

translations.literal: You said: "This is produced in the Three Wu region; its name is lingli.
translations.idiomatic: You said, "This creature comes from the Three Wu region; it is called the lingli.

sentences.zh: 餘域率無，今我獲之，吳、楚之地，其有歸國乎？

translations.literal: Other regions generally do not have it; now that we have obtained it, might the lands of Wu and Chu be coming back to the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Nowhere else has it in any numbers; now that we have caught one, perhaps the lands of Wu and Chu are destined to return to the realm?"

sentences.zh: 」又有人於靈丘得玉印一以獻，詔以示祐。
