translations.literal: Moreover someone at Lingqiu obtained a jade seal and presented it; an edict ordered it shown to You.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone at Lingqiu found a jade seal and presented it; an edict ordered it shown to You.

sentences.zh: 祐曰：「印上有籀書二字，文曰'宋壽'，壽者命也，我獲其命，亦是歸我之征。

translations.literal: You said: "On the seal are two characters in seal script; the text reads 'Song Shou.' Shou means mandate; we have obtained their mandate—this too is a sign that they will return to us.
translations.idiomatic: You said, "The seal bears two characters in seal script reading 'Song Shou.' Shou means mandate; we have gained their mandate—this too is a sign that they will come back to us.

sentences.zh: 」獻文初，宋義陽王昶來奔，薛安都等以五州降附，時謂祐言有驗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xianwen's reign, Liu Chang, Prince of Yiyang of Song, came to surrender; Xue Andu and others submitted five provinces, and people of the time said You's words had been verified.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Xianwen's reign, Liu Chang, Prince of Yiyang of Song, fled north to surrender, and Xue Andu and others brought five provinces over; people of the time said You's prophecy had been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，拜秘書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後與丞李彪等奏曰：「《尚書》者，記言之體；

translations.literal: Later, together with Vice Director Li Biao and others, he memorialized: "The Documents is a form for recording words;
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Vice Director Li Biao and others in a memorial: "The Documents is a form for recording words;

sentences.zh: 《春秋》者，錄事之辭。

translations.literal: the Spring and Autumn Annals is language for recording events.
translations.idiomatic: the Spring and Autumn Annals is language for recording events.

sentences.zh: 尋覽前志，斯皆司勳之實錄也。

translations.literal: On examining earlier chronicles, these are all true records kept by the Director of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: When one looks back at earlier chronicles, these are all true records kept by the Director of Merit.

sentences.zh: 惟聖朝創制上古，開基《長髮》，自始祖以後，至於文成，其間世數久遠，是以史弗能傳。

translations.literal: Our holy dynasty established its institutions in high antiquity and founded its rule with Chang Fa; from the Founding Ancestor down to Emperor Wencheng, the generations in between are remote in time, and so history could not transmit them fully.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty established its institutions in high antiquity and founded its rule with the Chang Fa; from the Founding Ancestor down to Emperor Wencheng, the generations in between are far removed in time, and history could not transmit them fully.

sentences.zh: 臣等疏漏，忝當史職，披覽國記，竊有志焉。

translations.literal: We are deficient and unworthy in our post as historians; in perusing the National Records, we have privately felt the ambition to act.
translations.idiomatic: We are unworthy in our post as historians, yet in reading the National Records we have privately felt the ambition to act.

sentences.zh: 愚謂自王業始基，庶事草創，皇始以降，光宅中土。

translations.literal: We venture to say that from the first laying of the royal enterprise, when all affairs were newly created, and from Huangshi onward, when the realm was illuminated in the Central Land—
translations.idiomatic: We venture to say that from the first laying of the royal enterprise, when all affairs were newly created, and from Huangshi onward, when the realm was established in the Central Land—

sentences.zh: 宜依遷、固大體，令事類相從，紀傳區別，表志殊貫，如此修綴，事可備書。

translations.literal: it would be fitting to follow the great model of Qian and Gu, let events of the same kind follow one another, distinguish annals from biographies, and keep tables and treatises in separate sections; repaired in this way, affairs could be fully written.
translations.idiomatic: it would be fitting to follow the great model of Sima Qian and Ban Gu, group related events together, distinguish annals from biographies, and keep tables and treatises in separate sections; organized in this way, the record could be made complete.

sentences.zh: 著作郎已下，請取有才用者，參造國書。

translations.literal: From Compiler down, we ask that men of talent and ability be selected to participate in compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: From Compiler down, we ask that men of talent and ability be chosen to help compile the National History.

sentences.zh: 如得其人，三年有成矣。

translations.literal: If the right men are obtained, in three years it can be completed.
translations.idiomatic: If the right men are found, the work can be finished in three years.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 孝文嘗問祐：「比水旱不調，何以止災而致豐稔？

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once asked You: "Recently flood and drought have been out of balance—how can disasters be stopped and abundance brought about?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once asked You, "Recently floods and droughts have fallen out of balance—how can disasters be halted and abundance restored?

sentences.zh: 」祐曰：「堯湯之運，不能去陽九之會。

translations.literal: You said: "Even in the reigns of Yao and Tang, the cycle could not escape the yang-nine calamity.
translations.idiomatic: You said, "Even in the age of Yao and Tang, the cycle could not escape the yang-nine calamity.

sentences.zh: 陛下道同前聖，其如小旱何？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's Way matches the earlier sages—what is a minor drought to that?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's Way matches the earlier sages—what is a minor drought beside that?

sentences.zh: 但當旌賢佐政，則災消穰至矣。

translations.literal: You need only honor the worthy and assist governance, and disasters will vanish and abundance will come."
translations.idiomatic: You need only honor the worthy and assist in governance, and disasters will vanish and abundance will follow."

sentences.zh: 」又問止盜之方。

translations.literal: He also asked the method for stopping theft.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked how theft might be stopped.

sentences.zh: 祐曰：「苟訓之有方，寧不易息？

translations.literal: You said: "If instruction has proper method, would it not easily cease?
translations.idiomatic: You said, "If instruction is properly applied, would it not easily cease?

sentences.zh: 當須宰守貞良，則盜賊止矣。

translations.literal: What is needed is that prefects and governors be upright and good, and then bandits and thieves will stop."
translations.idiomatic: What is needed is upright and capable prefects and governors—then bandits and thieves will cease."

sentences.zh: 」祐又上疏云：「今選舉不采職政之優劣，專簡年勞之多少，斯非盡才之謂。

translations.literal: You also submitted a memorial saying: "Today in selection and promotion the quality of performance in office is not taken into account; only years of service are weighed—this is not what is meant by employing talent to the full.
translations.idiomatic: You also submitted a memorial saying, "Today in selection and promotion the quality of performance in office is not taken into account; only years of service are weighed—this is not what is meant by employing talent to the full.

sentences.zh: 宜棄彼朽勞，唯才是舉。

translations.literal: That worn-out seniority should be set aside, and only talent should be raised.
translations.idiomatic: That worn-out seniority should be set aside, and only talent should be promoted.

sentences.zh: 又勳舊之臣，年勤可錄而才非撫人者，則可加以爵賞，不宜委以方任。

translations.literal: Again, for meritorious old ministers whose years of service are worth recording but whose talent is not suited to governing men, titles and rewards may be added, but they should not be entrusted with regional command.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for meritorious old ministers whose years of service are worth recording but whose talent is not suited to governing men, titles and rewards may be granted, but they should not be entrusted with regional command.

sentences.zh: 所謂王者可私人以財，不私人以官者也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by saying that a king may give a man wealth in private, but may not give him office in private."
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by saying that a king may give a man wealth in private, but may not give him office in private."

sentences.zh: 」帝皆善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 加給事中、冀州大中正。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Palace Provisioner and Chief Rectifier of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Palace Provisioner and Chief Rectifier of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 時李彪專統著作，祐為令，時關豫而己。

translations.literal: At the time Li Biao alone controlled compilation; You was Director in name only and was occasionally consulted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Biao alone controlled compilation; You was Director in name only and was occasionally consulted.

sentences.zh: 出為西兗州刺史，假東光侯，鎮滑台。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Western Yan Province, provisionally ennobled as Marquis of Dongguang, and garrisoned Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Western Yan Province, provisionally ennobled Marquis of Dongguang, and stationed at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 子和璧，字僧壽，有學尚，位中書博士，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Hebi, styled Sengshou, was learned and principled, held the post of Doctor of the Secretariat, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hebi, styled Sengshou, was learned and principled, served as Doctor of the Secretariat, and died young.

sentences.zh: 和璧子顥，字門賢，學涉有時譽。

translations.literal: Hebi's son Hao, styled Menxian, was broadly learned and enjoyed repute in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Hebi's son Hao, styled Menxian, was broadly learned and enjoyed repute in his time.

sentences.zh: 襲爵建康子，仕輔國將軍、朝散大夫，贈滄州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Marquis of Jiankang, served as General Who Assists the State and Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and when he died was posthumously made Governor of Cang Province with the posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Marquis of Jiankang, served as General Who Assists the State and Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and when he died was posthumously made Governor of Cang Province and given the posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 子德正襲。

translations.literal: His son Dezheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dezheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 德正幼而敏慧，有風神儀錶。

translations.literal: Dezheng was clever and bright from childhood and had a spirited bearing and dignified appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng was clever and bright from childhood and had a spirited bearing and dignified presence.

sentences.zh: 初為齊文宣儀同開府參軍，尋知管記事，甚相親狎。

translations.literal: At first he served as Army Aide on the staff of Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes for Northern Qi's Emperor Wenxuan; soon he was put in charge of record-keeping and was on very intimate terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Army Aide on the staff of Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes for Northern Qi's Emperor Wenxuan; soon he was put in charge of record-keeping and grew very close to him.

sentences.zh: 累遷相府掾，神武委以腹心。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to staff officer of the chancellor's office, and Gao Huan entrusted him as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to staff officer of the chancellor's office, and Gao Huan entrusted him as a confidant.

sentences.zh: 徙給事黃門侍郎，方雅周慎，動見稱述。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate; upright, refined, thorough, and careful, his conduct was always praised.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate; upright, refined, thorough, and careful, his conduct was always praised.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣業，如晉陽。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng succeeded to the enterprise, he went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded to the enterprise, he went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 文宣在鄴居守，令德正參機密，彌見親重。

translations.literal: Wenxuan remained at Ye to hold the capital; Dezheng was made privy to confidential affairs and was treated with even greater intimacy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan remained at Ye to hold the capital; Dezheng was admitted to confidential affairs and was treated with even greater intimacy and favor.

sentences.zh: 文襄之崩，勳將等以纘戎事重，勸文宣早赴晉陽。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng died, the meritorious generals, considering the weight of continuing the military enterprise, urged Wenxuan to go quickly to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng died, the meritorious generals, considering the weight of continuing the military enterprise, urged Wenxuan to go quickly to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 文宣不決，夜中召楊愔、杜弼、崔季舒及德正等，策始定。

translations.literal: Wenxuan could not decide; in the middle of the night he summoned Yang Yin, Du Bi, Cui Jishu, Dezheng, and others, and only then was the plan settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan could not decide; in the middle of the night he summoned Yang Yin, Du Bi, Cui Jishu, Dezheng, and others, and only then was the plan settled.

sentences.zh: 以愔從，令德正居守。

translations.literal: Yin accompanied him; Dezheng was ordered to remain and hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yin accompanied him; Dezheng was ordered to remain and hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 以為相府司馬，專知門下事。

translations.literal: He was made Chief Administrator of the chancellor's office and given sole charge of gate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chief Administrator of the chancellor's office and given sole charge of gate affairs.

sentences.zh: 德正與文宣舊昵愛，言無不盡。

translations.literal: Dezheng and Wenxuan had long been on affectionate terms, and in speech nothing was held back.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng and Wenxuan had long been on affectionate terms, and in speech nothing was held back.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍徐之才館客宋景業，先為天文圖讖學，又陳山提家客楊子術有所援引，並因德正勸文宣行禪代事。

translations.literal: Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Xu Zhicai's house guest Song Jingye had earlier studied astronomy, charts, and prognostic texts; Chen Shanti's house guest Yang Zishu also had material he cited; all, through Dezheng, urged Wenxuan to carry out the abdication and succession.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Xu Zhicai's house guest Song Jingye had earlier studied astronomy, charts, and prognostic texts; Chen Shanti's house guest Yang Zishu also had material he cited; all, through Dezheng, urged Wenxuan to carry out the abdication and succession.

sentences.zh: 德正又固請。

translations.literal: Dezheng again pressed the request firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng again pressed the request firmly.

sentences.zh: 文宣恐愔不決。

translations.literal: Wenxuan feared Yin would not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan feared Yin would not decide.

sentences.zh: 自請赴鄴與愔言，乃定。

translations.literal: He asked to go himself to Ye to speak with Yin, and then it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to go himself to Ye to speak with Yin, and then it was settled.

sentences.zh: 還，未至而文宣便發晉陽。

translations.literal: On the return, before he arrived Wenxuan had already set out from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the return, before he arrived Wenxuan had already set out from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 至平城都，召諸勳將入，告以禪讓事，諸將莫敢答者。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital at Pingcheng, he summoned the meritorious generals in and told them of the abdication; none of the generals dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital at Pingcheng, he summoned the meritorious generals in and told them of the abdication; none of the generals dared reply.

sentences.zh: 時杜弼為長史，密啟文宣：恐關西因此自稱義兵，挾天子而東向，將何以待？

translations.literal: At the time Du Bi was Chief Administrator; he secretly reported to Wenxuan: "I fear that because of this Guanxi will proclaim itself a righteous army, seize the Son of Heaven, and march east—how will we meet that?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Du Bi was Chief Administrator; he secretly reported to Wenxuan, "I fear that because of this Guanxi will proclaim itself a righteous army, seize the Son of Heaven, and march east—how will we meet that?"

sentences.zh: 之才云：今若先受魏禪，關西自應息心。

translations.literal: Zhicai said: "If we now accept Wei abdication first, Guanxi by itself ought to quiet its heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said, "If we now accept Wei's abdication first, Guanxi by itself ought to quiet its heart.

sentences.zh: 縱欲屈強，止當逐我稱帝。

translations.literal: Even if it wishes to resist by force, at most it will only drive us to declare ourselves emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Even if it wishes to resist by force, at most it will only drive us to declare ourselves emperor."

sentences.zh: 弼無以答。

translations.literal: Bi had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had nothing with which to reply.

sentences.zh: 文宣以眾意未協，又先得太后旨云：「汝父如龍，汝兄如猛獸，皆以帝王之重，不敢妄據，尚以人臣終。

translations.literal: Wenxuan, because the multitude's will was not united, had also earlier received the empress dowager's instruction: "Your father was like a dragon, your elder brother like a fierce beast; both, despite the weight of imperial rank, did not dare seize it rashly and still ended as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan, because the multitude's will was not united, had also earlier received the empress dowager's instruction: "Your father was like a dragon, your elder brother like a fierce beast; both, despite the weight of imperial rank, did not dare seize it rashly and still ended as subjects.

sentences.zh: 何欲行舜禹事？

translations.literal: Why do you wish to do what Shun and Yu did?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you wish to do what Shun and Yu did?

sentences.zh: 此正是高德正教汝。

translations.literal: This is precisely what Gao Dezheng is teaching you."
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely what Gao Dezheng is teaching you."

sentences.zh: 」又說者以為昔周武王再駕盟津，然始革命。

translations.literal: Others also said that in former times King Wu of Zhou twice drove to Mengjin before he finally changed the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Others also said that in former times King Wu of Zhou twice drove to Mengjin before he finally changed the mandate.

sentences.zh: 於是乃旋晉陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he turned back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he turned back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 自是居常不悅。

translations.literal: From then on he was often displeased in daily life.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was often displeased in daily life.

sentences.zh: 徐之才、宋景業等每言卜筮雜占陰陽緯候，必宜以五月應天命。

translations.literal: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others repeatedly said that in divination, miscellaneous prognostication, yin-yang theory, and celestial portents, the fifth month was surely the time to answer Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others repeatedly said that in divination, miscellaneous prognostication, yin-yang theory, and celestial portents, the fifth month was surely the time to answer Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 德正亦敦勸不已，仍白文宣追魏收。

translations.literal: Dezheng also urged without ceasing and reported to Wenxuan to summon Wei Shou back.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng also urged without ceasing and reported to Wenxuan to summon Wei Shou back.

sentences.zh: 收至，令撰禪讓詔冊、九錫、建台及勸進文表。

translations.literal: When Shou arrived, he was ordered to draft the abdication edicts and proclamations, the Nine Bestowals, the establishment of the imperial platform, and the memorials urging accession.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou arrived, he was ordered to draft the abdication edicts and proclamations, the Nine Bestowals, the establishment of the imperial platform, and the memorials urging accession.

sentences.zh: 至五月初，文宣發晉陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the fifth month Wenxuan set out from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the fifth month Wenxuan set out from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 德正又錄在鄴諸事條進于文宣。

translations.literal: Dezheng also compiled a list of all affairs at Ye and forwarded it to Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng also compiled a list of all affairs at Ye and forwarded it to Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 文宣令陳山提馳驛齎事條並密書與楊愔。

translations.literal: Wenxuan ordered Chen Shanti to ride post-haste and deliver the list of affairs together with a secret letter to Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan ordered Chen Shanti to ride post-haste and deliver the list of affairs together with a secret letter to Yang Yin.

sentences.zh: 山提以五月至鄴，楊愔即召太常卿邢邵、七兵尚書崔甗、度支尚書陸操、太子詹事王昕、給事黃門侍郎陽休之、中書侍郎裴讓之等議撰儀注。

translations.literal: Shanti reached Ye in the fifth month; Yang Yin at once summoned Director of Ceremonial Xing Shao, Minister of the Seven Armies Cui Yan, Minister of Revenue Lu Cao, Steward of the Heir Apparent Wang Xin, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate Yang Xiuzhi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Rangzhi, and others to discuss and draft the ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Shanti reached Ye in the fifth month; Yang Yin at once summoned Director of Ceremonial Xing Shao, Minister of the Seven Armies Cui Yan, Minister of Revenue Lu Cao, Steward of the Heir Apparent Wang Xin, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate Yang Xiuzhi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Rangzhi, and others to discuss and draft the ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 六日，要魏太傅咸陽王坦、錄尚書事濟陰王暉業等總集，引入北宮，留於東齋，受禪後乃放還宅。

translations.literal: On the sixth day he required Wei Grand Tutor Prince Tan of Xianyang, Recorder of Affairs Prince Huiye of Jiyin, and others to assemble; they were brought into the Northern Palace, kept in the Eastern Study, and only after the abdication were released to their homes.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day he required Wei Grand Tutor Prince Tan of Xianyang, Recorder of Affairs Prince Huiye of Jiyin, and others to assemble; they were brought into the Northern Palace, kept in the Eastern Study, and only after the abdication were released to their homes.

sentences.zh: 文宣發至前亭，所乘馬忽倒，意甚惡之。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan set out and reached Qianting, the horse he was riding suddenly fell, and he took this as a very bad omen.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan set out and reached Qianting, the horse he was riding suddenly fell, and he took this as a very bad omen.

sentences.zh: 至平城都，便不復肯進。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital at Pingcheng, he would no longer go forward.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital at Pingcheng, he would no longer go forward.

sentences.zh: 德正與徐之才苦請曰：「山提先去，恐其漏泄，不果。

translations.literal: Dezheng and Xu Zhicai pleaded bitterly: "Shanti went ahead first; we fear the matter has leaked and will fail.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng and Xu Zhicai pleaded bitterly, "Shanti went ahead first; we fear the matter has leaked and will fail.

sentences.zh: 」即命司馬子如、杜弼馳驛續入，觀察物情。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Sima Ziru and Du Bi to ride post-haste after them and observe the mood of the people.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered Sima Ziru and Du Bi to ride post-haste after them and observe the mood of the people.

sentences.zh: 七日，子如等至鄴，眾人以事勢已決，無敢異言。

translations.literal: On the seventh day Ziru and the others reached Ye; the people, seeing that the matter was already decided, dared raise no dissent.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day Ziru and the others reached Ye; the people, seeing that the matter was already decided, dared raise no dissent.

sentences.zh: 九日，文宣至城南頓所。

translations.literal: On the ninth day Wenxuan reached the encampment south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day Wenxuan reached the encampment south of the city.

sentences.zh: 時既未行詔敕，諸公文書唯雲奉約束，德正及楊愔宣署而已。

translations.literal: At the time edicts and orders had not yet been issued; all official documents from the various offices spoke only of obeying restrictions, and Dezheng and Yang Yin handled announcements and signatures.
translations.idiomatic: At the time edicts and orders had not yet been issued; all official documents from the various offices spoke only of obeying restrictions, and Dezheng and Yang Yin handled announcements and signatures.

sentences.zh: 受禪日，堯難宗染赤雀以獻。

translations.literal: On the day of receiving the mandate, Yao Nanzong dyed a red sparrow and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of receiving the mandate, Yao Nanzong dyed a red sparrow and presented it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 帝尋知之，亦弗責也。

translations.literal: The emperor soon learned of it but did not reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon learned of it but did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 是日，即除德正為侍中，又領宗正卿。

translations.literal: That same day Dezheng was appointed Palace Attendant and also made Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Dezheng was appointed Palace Attendant and also made Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 尋遷吏部尚書，侍中如故，封藍田縣公。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, retaining his post as Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Lantian County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, retaining his post as Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed Duke of Lantian County.

sentences.zh: 天保七年，遷尚書右僕射，兼侍中，食勃海郡幹。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianbao he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Palace Attendant, with salary drawn from Bohai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianbao he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Palace Attendant, with salary drawn from Bohai commandery.

sentences.zh: 德正與尚書令楊愔，綱紀朝政，多有弘益。

translations.literal: Dezheng, together with Director of the Secretariat Yang Yin, regulated court governance and brought many broad benefits.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng, together with Director of the Secretariat Yang Yin, regulated court governance and brought many broad benefits.

sentences.zh: 文宣末年，縱酒酣醉。

translations.literal: In Wenxuan's later years he gave himself to wine and drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenxuan's later years he gave himself to wine and drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 德正屢進忠言，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Dezheng repeatedly offered loyal remonstrance; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng repeatedly offered loyal remonstrance; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 又謂左右云：「高德正恆以精神陵逼人。

translations.literal: He also told those around him: "Gao Dezheng always uses his spirit to overbear and press upon people.
translations.idiomatic: He also told those around him, "Gao Dezheng always uses his spirit to overbear and press upon people.

sentences.zh: 」德正甚憂懼，乃移疾，屏居佛寺，兼學坐禪，為退身之計。

translations.literal: Dezheng was deeply fearful; he thereupon pleaded illness, withdrew to live in a Buddhist temple, and also studied seated meditation as a plan to retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng was deeply fearful; he thereupon pleaded illness, withdrew to live in a Buddhist temple, and also studied seated meditation as a plan to retreat.

sentences.zh: 帝謂楊愔曰：「我大憂高德正，其疾何以？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yang Yin: "I am greatly worried about Gao Dezheng—what of his illness?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Yang Yin, "I am greatly worried about Gao Dezheng—what of his illness?

sentences.zh: 」愔知帝內忌之，由是答云：「陛下若用作冀州刺史，病即自差。

translations.literal: Yin knew the emperor inwardly resented him and therefore answered: "If Your Majesty appoints him Governor of Ji Province, the illness will cure itself.
translations.idiomatic: Yin knew the emperor inwardly resented him and therefore answered, "If Your Majesty appoints him Governor of Ji Province, the illness will cure itself.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，德正見除書而起。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed; when Dezheng saw the appointment order he rose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; when Dezheng saw the appointment order he rose.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謂曰：「聞爾病，我為爾針！

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and said: "I heard you were ill—I came to give you acupuncture!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered and said, "I heard you were ill—I came to give you acupuncture!

sentences.zh: 」親以刀子刺之，血流沾地。

translations.literal: He personally stabbed him with a knife, and blood flowed to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He personally stabbed him with a knife, and blood flowed to the ground.

sentences.zh: 又使曳下，斬去其趾。

translations.literal: He also had him dragged down and his toes cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He also had him dragged down and his toes cut off.

sentences.zh: 劉桃枝捉刀不敢下，帝起臨陛，切責桃枝，桃枝乃斬足之三指。

translations.literal: Liu Taozhi took up the knife but did not dare strike; the emperor rose and went to the steps, sharply rebuked Taozhi, and Taozhi then cut off three toes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taozhi took up the knife but did not dare strike; the emperor rose and went to the steps, sharply rebuked Taozhi, and Taozhi then cut off three toes.

sentences.zh: 帝怒不解，禁德正于門下省。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger did not subside, and Dezheng was confined in the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger did not subside, and Dezheng was confined in the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 其夜，開城門，以氈輿送還家。

translations.literal: That night the city gate was opened and he was sent home in a felt carriage.
translations.idiomatic: That night the city gate was opened and he was sent home in a felt carriage.

sentences.zh: 旦日，德正妻出寶物滿四床，欲以寄人。

translations.literal: At dawn Dezheng's wife brought out treasures filling four beds, intending to deposit them with others.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Dezheng's wife brought out treasures filling four beds, intending to deposit them with others.

sentences.zh: 帝奄至其宅，見而怒曰：「我府藏猶無此物。

translations.literal: The emperor suddenly arrived at the house, saw them, and angrily said: "Even my treasury does not have such things.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suddenly arrived at the house, saw them, and angrily said, "Even my treasury does not have such things.

sentences.zh: 」詰其所從得，皆諸元賂之也。

translations.literal: He interrogated where they had been obtained; all had been bribes from the Yuan clan."
translations.idiomatic: He interrogated where they had been obtained; all had been bribes from the Yuan clan."

sentences.zh: 遂曳出斬之，妻出拜謝，又斬之。

translations.literal: He had Dezheng dragged out and executed; the wife came out to bow and plead, and she too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He had Dezheng dragged out and executed; the wife came out to bow and plead, and she too was executed.

sentences.zh: 並其子司徒東閣祭酒伯堅亦見害。

translations.literal: Together with them his son Bojian, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion under the Minister of Works, was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Together with them his son Bojian, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion under the Minister of Works, was also killed.

sentences.zh: 後文宣謂群臣曰：「高德正常言，宜用漢除鮮卑，此即合死。

translations.literal: Later Wenxuan said to the assembled ministers: "Gao Dezheng often spoke of adopting Han customs and abolishing Xianbei ways—that alone deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenxuan said to the assembled ministers, "Gao Dezheng often spoke of adopting Han customs and abolishing Xianbei ways—that alone deserved death.

sentences.zh: 又教我誅諸元，我今殺之，為諸元報仇也。

translations.literal: He also urged me to execute the Yuan clan; now that I have killed him, I have avenged the Yuan clan."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged me to execute the Yuan clan; now that I have killed him, I have avenged the Yuan clan."

sentences.zh: 」帝後悔，贈太保、冀州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: "The emperor later regretted it and posthumously granted him Grand Tutor and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor later regretted it and posthumously granted him Grand Tutor and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 嫡孫王臣，襲爵藍田縣公，給事中、通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His eldest grandson's son Wang Chen inherited the title Duke of Lantian County and served as Palace Attendant and Regular Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest grandson's son Wang Chen inherited the title Duke of Lantian County and served as Palace Attendant and Regular Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德正次子仲武，京畿司馬、平原郡守。

translations.literal: Dezheng's second son Zhongwu served as Metropolitan Area Military Administrator and Administrator of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng's second son Zhongwu served as Metropolitan Area Military Administrator and Administrator of Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 顥弟雅，字興賢，有風度，位定州撫軍府長史。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Ya, styled Xingxian, had presence and bearing and served as Chief Administrator of the Pacification Army Headquarters in Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Ya, styled Xingxian, had presence and bearing and served as Chief Administrator of the Pacification Army Headquarters in Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 天平中，追贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Tianping era he was posthumously granted Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was posthumously granted Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子德範，早有令問，位任城太守，卒。

translations.literal: His son Defan was famed early for fine reputation and served as Administrator of Rencheng; he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Defan was famed from youth for fine reputation and served as Administrator of Rencheng; he died.

sentences.zh: 雅弟諒，字修賢，少好學，多識強記，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Ya's younger brother Liang, styled Xiuxian, loved learning from youth, was widely learned with a strong memory, and was famed for filial piety while in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's younger brother Liang, styled Xiuxian, loved learning from youth, was widely learned with a strong memory, and was famed for filial piety while in mourning.

sentences.zh: 太和末，京兆王愉開府辟召，孝文妙簡僚佐，諒與隴西李仲尚、趙郡李鳳起等同時應選。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era, when the Prince of Jingzhao Yu opened his office and recruited staff, Emperor Xiaowen carefully selected aides; Liang was chosen at the same time as Longxi's Li Zhongshang and Zhao commandery's Li Fengqi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taihe era, when the Prince of Jingzhao Yu opened his office and recruited staff, Emperor Xiaowen carefully selected aides; Liang was chosen alongside Longxi's Li Zhongshang and Zhao commandery's Li Fengqi.

sentences.zh: 正光中，加驍騎將軍，為徐州行台。

translations.literal: During the Zhengguang era he was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry and served at the Xuzhou Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era he was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry and served at the Xuzhou Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 至彭城，屬元法僧反，逼諒同之，不從見害。

translations.literal: When he reached Pengcheng, Yuan Faseng rebelled and tried to force Liang to join; Liang refused and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Pengcheng, Yuan Faseng rebelled and tried to force Liang to join; Liang refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈滄州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Governor of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又詔以諒臨危授命，復贈使持節、平北將軍、幽州刺史，優授一子出身，諡曰忠侯。

translations.literal: An edict also said that because Liang had entrusted his life at the hour of crisis, he was further posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Youzhou; one son was granted entry into official service with privilege, and his posthumous title was Marquis of Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also said that because Liang had entrusted his life at the hour of crisis, he was further posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Youzhou; one son was granted privileged entry into official service, and his posthumous title was Marquis of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 諒造《親表譜錄》四十餘卷，自五世以下，內外曲盡，覽者服其博記。

translations.literal: Liang compiled the Genealogical Records of Close and Distant Kin in more than forty juan; from the fifth generation onward, both inner and outer relations were exhaustively set forth, and readers admired his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: Liang compiled the Genealogical Records of Close and Distant Kin in more than forty juan; from the fifth generation onward, both inner and outer relations were exhaustively set forth, and readers admired his erudition.

sentences.zh: 祐從父弟翼，字次同，豪俠有風神。

translations.literal: You's younger cousin Yi, styled Citong, was bold and chivalrous with spirited bearing.
translations.idiomatic: You's younger cousin Yi, styled Citong, was bold and chivalrous with spirited bearing.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，葛榮作亂，朝廷以翼山東豪右，即家拜勃海太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiaochang era, when Ge Rong raised rebellion, the court, because Yi was a leading magnate east of the mountains, appointed him Administrator of Bohai at his home.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era, when Ge Rong raised rebellion, the court, because Yi was a leading magnate east of the mountains, appointed him Administrator of Bohai at his home.

sentences.zh: 翼率合境，徙居河、濟間。

translations.literal: Yi led the entire district to migrate and settle between the Yellow and Ji rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Yi led the entire district to migrate and settle between the Yellow and Ji rivers.

sentences.zh: 魏朝因置東冀州，以翼為刺史，封樂城縣侯。

translations.literal: The Wei court therefore established Eastern Jizhou, appointing Yi governor and enfeoffing him Marquis of Lecheng County.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court therefore established Eastern Jizhou, appointing Yi governor and enfeoffing him Marquis of Lecheng County.

sentences.zh: 俄除定州刺史，以賊亂不行。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and appointed Governor of Ding Province, but because of bandit chaos he could not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was removed and appointed Governor of Ding Province, but because of bandit chaos he could not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃兆弑莊帝，翼保境自守，卒。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao murdered Emperor Zhuang, Yi held his territory and maintained self-defense; he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao murdered Emperor Zhuang, Yi held his territory and maintained self-defense; he died.

sentences.zh: 中興初，贈使持節、侍中、太保、錄尚書、六州諸軍事、冀州刺史，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhongxing era he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, Minister Overseeing the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of the Six Provinces, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhongxing era he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, Minister Overseeing the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of the Six Provinces, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 子乾。

translations.literal: His son was Qian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qian.

sentences.zh: 乾字乾邕。

translations.literal: Qian was styled Qianyong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was styled Qianyong.

sentences.zh: 性明悟俊偉，有智略，美音容，進止都雅。

translations.literal: By nature he was bright, perceptive, handsome, and imposing, with strategic talent; his voice and appearance were fine, and in movement and deportment he was altogether elegant.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bright, perceptive, handsome, and imposing, with strategic talent; his voice and appearance were fine, and in movement and deportment he was altogether elegant.

sentences.zh: 少時輕俠，長而修改，輕財重義，多所交結。

translations.literal: In youth he was reckless and chivalrous; growing older he corrected himself, held wealth lightly and valued righteousness, and formed many friendships.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was reckless and chivalrous; growing older he corrected himself, held wealth lightly and valued righteousness, and formed many friendships.

sentences.zh: 起家拜員外散騎侍郎，稍遷員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He first entered service as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Gentleman and was gradually promoted to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Gentleman and was gradually promoted to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 魏孝莊之居籓也，乾潛相托附。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei held a princely fief, Qian secretly attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei held a princely fief, Qian secretly attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮入洛，乾東奔於翼。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Qian fled east to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Qian fled east to Yi.

sentences.zh: 乾兄弟本有從橫志，見榮殺害人士，謂天下遂亂，乃率河北流人於河、濟間，受葛榮官爵。

translations.literal: Qian and his brothers had originally harbored ambitions of independent action; seeing Rong kill cultivated men, they judged that the realm would soon fall into chaos, so they gathered refugees from north of the Yellow River between the Yellow and Ji rivers and accepted office and titles from Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and his brothers had originally harbored ambitions of independent action; seeing Rong kill cultivated men, they judged that the realm would soon fall into chaos, so they gathered refugees from north of the Yellow River between the Yellow and Ji rivers and accepted office and titles from Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 莊帝遣右僕射元羅巡撫三齊，乾兄弟相率出降。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang dispatched Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Luo to inspect and pacify the three Qi regions; Qian and his brothers led their followers out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang dispatched Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Luo to inspect and pacify the three Qi regions; Qian and his brothers led their followers out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以乾為給事黃門侍郎，兼武衛將軍。

translations.literal: The court appointed Qian Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, concurrently General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Qian Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, concurrently General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮以乾前罪，不應復居近要，莊帝聽乾解官歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong, because of Qian's earlier offense, held that he should not again hold a post near the center of power; Emperor Zhuang permitted Qian to resign office and return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, because of Qian's earlier offense, held that he should not again hold a post near the center of power; Emperor Zhuang permitted Qian to resign office and return to his home district.

sentences.zh: 於是招納驍勇，以射獵自娛。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited fierce warriors and amused himself with archery and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he recruited fierce warriors and amused himself with archery and hunting.

sentences.zh: 及榮死，乃馳赴洛陽。

translations.literal: When Rong died, he galloped to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, he galloped to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 莊帝見之大喜，以乾兼侍中，加撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫，鎮河北。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang was greatly pleased to see him and appointed Qian concurrent Palace Attendant, with additional titles General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord, to guard Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang was greatly pleased to see him and appointed Qian concurrent Palace Attendant, with additional titles General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord, to guard Hebei.

sentences.zh: 又以弟昂為通直散騎常侍、平北將軍。

translations.literal: He also made Qian's younger brother Ang Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Qian's younger brother Ang Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 令俱歸，招集鄉閭，為表裏形援。

translations.literal: He ordered them both to return home, gather their native districts, and provide inner and outer support.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them both to return home, gather their native districts, and provide inner and outer support.

sentences.zh: 帝親送於河橋上，舉酒指水曰：「卿兄弟冀部豪傑，能令士卒致死。

translations.literal: The emperor personally saw them off at the He Bridge, raised his cup, pointed to the water, and said: "You brothers are magnates of Ji province; you can make your soldiers die for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally saw them off at the He Bridge, raised his cup, pointed to the water, and said, "You brothers are magnates of Ji province; you can make your soldiers die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 京城儻有變，可為朕河上一揚塵。

translations.literal: If the capital should meet with upheaval, you may raise a cloud of dust for me on the north bank of the River."
translations.idiomatic: If the capital should meet with upheaval, you may raise a cloud of dust for me on the north bank of the River."

sentences.zh: 」乾垂涕受詔，昂援劍起舞，誓以死繼之。

translations.literal: Qian received the command with tears; Ang drew his sword and danced, vowing to follow him to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Qian received the command with tears; Ang drew his sword and danced, vowing to follow him to the death.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃氏既弑害，遣其監軍孫白雞率百餘騎至冀州。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan had murdered the emperor, they sent their military overseer Sun Baiji with more than a hundred horsemen to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu clan had murdered the emperor, they sent their military overseer Sun Baiji with more than a hundred horsemen to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 托言括馬，其實欲因乾兄弟送馬收之。

translations.literal: On the pretext of registering horses, they in fact intended to seize Qian and his brothers when they came to deliver the horses.
translations.idiomatic: On the pretext of registering horses, they in fact intended to seize Qian and his brothers when they came to deliver the horses.

sentences.zh: 乾既宿有報復之心，而白雞忽至，知欲見圖。

translations.literal: Qian had long harbored a desire for revenge, and when Baiji arrived suddenly he knew they meant to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had long harbored a desire for revenge, and when Baiji arrived suddenly he knew they meant to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 將先發，以告前河內太守封隆之。

translations.literal: Intending to strike first, he told the former Administrator of Henei Feng Longzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Intending to strike first, he told the former Administrator of Henei Feng Longzhi.

sentences.zh: 隆之父先為爾硃榮所殺，聞之喜曰：「國恥家怨，痛入骨髓，乘機而發，今正其時。

translations.literal: Longzhi's father had earlier been killed by Erzhu Rong; hearing this he said with joy: "The shame of the state and the grievance of the family cut to the marrow; to seize this moment and rise—now is exactly the time.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi's father had earlier been killed by Erzhu Rong; hearing this he said with joy, "The shame of the state and the grievance of the family cut to the marrow; to seize this moment and rise—now is exactly the time.

sentences.zh: 謹聞命矣。」

translations.literal: I respectfully await your command."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully await your command."

sentences.zh: 二月，乾與昂潛勒壯士，夜襲州城，執刺史元嶷，射白雞殺之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Qian and Ang secretly mustered stalwart men, attacked the provincial city by night, seized Governor Yuan Yi, shot and killed Baiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Qian and Ang secretly mustered stalwart men, attacked the provincial city by night, seized Governor Yuan Yi, shot and killed Baiji.

sentences.zh: 于葛榮殿為莊帝舉哀，素服，乾升壇誓眾，詞氣激揚，涕泗交集，將士莫不感憤。

translations.literal: At Ge Rong's hall they performed mourning rites for Emperor Zhuang in plain dress; Qian ascended the platform and swore before the host, his words impassioned and tears mingling, and none of the officers and soldiers was not moved to indignation.
translations.idiomatic: At Ge Rong's hall they performed mourning rites for Emperor Zhuang in plain dress; Qian ascended the platform and swore before the host, his words impassioned and tears mingling, and none of the officers and soldiers was not moved to indignation.

sentences.zh: 欲奉次同為王。

translations.literal: They wished to install Citong as king.
translations.idiomatic: They wished to install Citong as king.

sentences.zh: 次同曰：「和鄉里，我不及封皮。

translations.literal: Citong said: "In winning over the countryside, I am not the equal of Feng Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Citong said, "In winning over the countryside, I am not the equal of Feng Pi.

sentences.zh: 」乃推隆之為大都督，行州事。

translations.literal: They therefore pushed Longzhi to be Grand Commandant, acting in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore pushed Longzhi to be Grand Commandant, acting in provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 隆之欲逃，昂勃然作色，拔刀將斫隆之，隆之懼，乃受命。

translations.literal: When Longzhi wished to flee, Ang flushed with anger, drew his sword and was about to hack Longzhi down; Longzhi in fear accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: When Longzhi wished to flee, Ang flushed with anger, drew his sword and was about to hack Longzhi down; Longzhi in fear accepted the command.

sentences.zh: 北受幽州刺史劉靈助節度，俄而靈助被爾硃氏禽。

translations.literal: To the north they submitted to the command of Governor of Youzhou Liu Lingzhu; before long Lingzhu was captured by the Erzhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: To the north they submitted to the command of Governor of Youzhou Liu Lingzhu; before long Lingzhu was captured by the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 屬齊神武出山東，揚聲以討乾為辭，眾情惶懼。

translations.literal: At that time Qi Shenwu came out from east of the mountains, proclaiming as his purpose the suppression of Qian, and popular sentiment was panic-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qi Shenwu came out from east of the mountains, proclaiming as his purpose the suppression of Qian, and popular sentiment was panic-stricken.

sentences.zh: 乾謂之曰：「高晉州雄材蓋世，不居人下。

translations.literal: Qian said to them: "Gao of Jin Province is a hero whose talent covers the age and who will not remain beneath others.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said to them, "Gao of Jin Province is a hero whose talent covers the age and who will not remain beneath others.

sentences.zh: 且爾硃弑主肆虐，正是英雄效節之時，今者之來，必有深計。

translations.literal: Moreover the Erzhu murdered their lord and rampaged—this is exactly the time for heroes to devote themselves; that he comes now must mean he has a deep design.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Erzhu murdered their lord and rampaged—this is exactly the time for heroes to devote themselves; that he comes now must mean he has a deep design.

sentences.zh: 勿憂，吾將諸君見之。

translations.literal: Do not worry; I shall lead you to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Do not worry; I shall lead you to meet him.

sentences.zh: 」乃間行，與封隆之子子繪，俱迎于滏陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went by secret routes with Feng Longzhi's son Zihui to welcome him at Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he went by secret routes with Feng Longzhi's son Zihui to welcome him at Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 因說神武曰：「爾硃氏酷逆，痛結人神，凡厥生靈，莫不思奮。

translations.literal: He therefore urged Shenwu, saying: "The Erzhu clan are cruelly rebellious; their evil binds gods and men alike, and every living creature longs to rise against them.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore urged Shenwu, saying, "The Erzhu clan are cruelly rebellious; their evil binds gods and men alike, and every living creature longs to rise against them.

sentences.zh: 明公威德素著，天下傾心，若兵以忠立，則屈強之徒不足為明公敵矣。

translations.literal: Your Grace's prestige and virtue have long been manifest and the whole realm inclines to you; if you raise arms in the name of loyalty, then the stubbornly powerful will not be worthy opponents for Your Grace.
translations.idiomatic: Your Grace's prestige and virtue have long been manifest and the whole realm inclines to you; if you raise arms in the name of loyalty, then the stubbornly powerful will not be worthy opponents for Your Grace.

sentences.zh: 鄙州雖小，戶口不減十萬，穀秸之稅，足濟軍資。

translations.literal: My humble province is small, but its registered households are no fewer than one hundred thousand, and grain-and-straw taxes are enough to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: My humble province is small, but its registered households are no fewer than one hundred thousand, and grain-and-straw taxes are enough to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 願公熟詳其計。

translations.literal: I pray Your Grace will consider this plan carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Grace will consider this plan carefully.

sentences.zh: 」神武大笑曰：「吾事諧矣！

translations.literal: Shenwu laughed greatly and said: "My affair is settled!
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu laughed greatly and said, "My affair is settled!

sentences.zh: 」遂與乾同帳而寢，呼乾為叔父。

translations.literal: He then shared a tent with Qian to sleep and called Qian "Uncle."
translations.idiomatic: He then shared a tent with Qian to sleep and called Qian "Uncle."

sentences.zh: 乾旦日受命而去。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Qian received his orders and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day Qian received his orders and departed.

sentences.zh: 時神武雖內有遠圖，而外跡未見。

translations.literal: At the time Shenwu had far-reaching designs within but his outward tracks had not yet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shenwu had far-reaching designs within but his outward tracks had not yet appeared.

sentences.zh: 爾硃羽生為殷州刺史，神武密遣李元忠於封龍山舉兵逼其城，令乾率眾偽往救之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Yusheng was Governor of Yin Province; Shenwu secretly sent Li Yuanzhong to raise troops at Mount Fenglong and press the city, ordering Qian to lead troops in a feigned rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Yusheng was Governor of Yin Province; Shenwu secretly sent Li Yuanzhong to raise troops at Mount Fenglong and press the city, ordering Qian to lead troops in a feigned rescue.

sentences.zh: 乾遂輕騎入見羽生，偽為之計。

translations.literal: Qian therefore entered with a light escort to see Yusheng and feigned counsel for him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian therefore entered with a light escort to see Yusheng and feigned counsel for him.

sentences.zh: 羽生出勞軍，彭樂側從馬上禽斬之，遂平殷州。

translations.literal: When Yusheng came out to review the troops, Peng Le, at his side, seized and beheaded him from horseback; they then pacified Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yusheng came out to review the troops, Peng Le, at his side, seized and beheaded him from horseback; they then pacified Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 又共定策，推立中興主。

translations.literal: They also jointly settled the plan to install the Restoration Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They also jointly settled the plan to install the Restoration Emperor.

sentences.zh: 拜侍中、司空公。

translations.literal: Qian was appointed Palace Attendant and Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was appointed Palace Attendant and Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍國草創，乾父喪，不得終制。

translations.literal: At that time the state and army were newly founded; Qian's father had died and he could not complete the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the state and army were newly founded; Qian's father had died and he could not complete the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 及孝武立，天下初定，乾乃表請解職，行三年之禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was established and the realm was first settled, Qian memorialized requesting resignation to observe the three-year rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu was established and the realm was first settled, Qian memorialized requesting resignation to observe the three-year rites.

sentences.zh: 詔聽解侍中，司空如故，封長樂郡公。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to resign the post of Palace Attendant while retaining the Ministry of Works; he was enfeoffed Duke of Changle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted him to resign the post of Palace Attendant while retaining the Ministry of Works; he was enfeoffed Duke of Changle commandery.

sentences.zh: 乾雖求退，不謂便見從許，既去內侍，朝政空關，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Although Qian had sought withdrawal, he had not expected such ready consent; once removed from inner attendance, court affairs were left vacant and he was often discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Although Qian had sought withdrawal, he had not expected such ready consent; once removed from inner attendance, court affairs were left vacant and he was often discontent.

sentences.zh: 孝武將貳于神武，欲乘此撫之，于華林園宴罷，獨留乾，謂曰：「司空弈世忠良，今日復建殊效。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was about to turn against Shenwu and wished to use this occasion to win Qian over; after a banquet at Hualin Garden he kept Qian alone and said: "The Minister of Works' house has generation after generation served in loyalty; today he has again achieved extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was about to turn against Shenwu and wished to use this occasion to win Qian over; after a banquet at Hualin Garden he kept Qian alone and said, "The Minister of Works' house has generation after generation served in loyalty; today he has again achieved extraordinary merit.

sentences.zh: 相與雖則君臣，實義同兄弟，宜共立盟約。

translations.literal: Though in name we are sovereign and subject, in righteousness we are truly like brothers and ought to establish a sworn alliance together.
translations.idiomatic: Though in name we are sovereign and subject, in righteousness we are truly like brothers and ought to establish a sworn alliance together.

sentences.zh: 」勒逼之。

translations.literal: He pressed him to it.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed him to it.

sentences.zh: 乾曰：「臣以身許國，何敢有二？

translations.literal: Qian said: "I have devoted my person to the state—how would I dare be of two minds?
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "I have devoted my person to the state—how would I dare be of two minds?

sentences.zh: 」乾雖有此對，然非其本心，事出倉卒，又不謂孝武便有異志，遂不固辭，亦不啟神武。

translations.literal: Although Qian answered thus, it was not from his true heart; the matter arose in haste, and he did not think Emperor Xiaowu already harbored a different intent, so he did not firmly decline, nor did he inform Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Although Qian answered thus, it was not from his true heart; the matter arose in haste, and he did not think Emperor Xiaowu already harbored a different intent, so he did not firmly decline, nor did he inform Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 帝以乾為誠己。

translations.literal: The emperor believed Qian was sincere toward him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed Qian was sincere toward him.

sentences.zh: 時禁園養部曲稍至千人，驟令元士弼、王思政詣賀拔岳計，又以岳兄勝為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time he secretly kept retainers in the forbidden garden until they reached a thousand men; he suddenly ordered Yuan Shibi and Wang Sizheng to go consult with Helu Yue, and again made Yue's elder brother Sheng Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he secretly kept retainers in the forbidden garden until they reached a thousand men; he suddenly ordered Yuan Shibi and Wang Sizheng to go consult with Helu Yue, and again made Yue's elder brother Sheng Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾謂所親曰：「難將作矣，禍必及吾。

translations.literal: Qian said to those close to him: "Disaster is about to break out; calamity is sure to reach me.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said to those close to him, "Disaster is about to break out; calamity is sure to reach me.

sentences.zh: 」乃密以啟神武。

translations.literal: He then secretly reported this to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly reported this to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武召乾問之，乾因勸神武受禪。

translations.literal: Shenwu summoned Qian to question him; Qian thereupon urged Shenwu to accept the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu summoned Qian to question him; Qian thereupon urged Shenwu to accept the abdication.

sentences.zh: 神武以袖掩其口曰：「勿復言。

translations.literal: Shenwu covered Qian's mouth with his sleeve and said: "Speak no more of that.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu covered Qian's mouth with his sleeve and said, "Speak no more of that.

sentences.zh: 今啟叔復為侍中，門下之事，一以仰委。

translations.literal: From this day I report to Uncle that he is again Palace Attendant; all affairs of the Secretariat I entrust entirely to you.
translations.idiomatic: From this day I report to Uncle that he is again Palace Attendant; all affairs of the Secretariat I entrust entirely to you.

sentences.zh: 」及頻請而帝不答，乾懼變，啟神武，求為徐州。

translations.literal: When he repeatedly requested it but the emperor did not answer, Qian feared a turn in events, reported to Shenwu, and requested appointment to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he repeatedly requested it but the emperor did not answer, Qian feared a turn in events, reported to Shenwu, and requested appointment to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃以乾為開府儀同三司、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Qian was therefore appointed Honorary Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord with privileges equal to a Three Excellencies office and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was therefore appointed Honorary Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord with privileges equal to a Three Excellencies office and Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 將行，帝聞其與神武言，怒，使謂神武曰：「高乾與朕私盟，今復反覆。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the emperor heard of his words with Shenwu and in anger sent word to Shenwu, saying: "Gao Qian made a private alliance with me, yet now he turns again.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, the emperor heard of his words with Shenwu and in anger sent word to Shenwu, saying, "Gao Qian made a private alliance with me, yet now he turns again.

sentences.zh: 」神武聞其與帝盟，亦惡之，乃封其前後密啟以聞。

translations.literal: When Shenwu heard of his alliance with the emperor he also came to detest him, and sealed Qian's former and later secret reports and sent them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu heard of his alliance with the emperor he also came to detest him, and sealed Qian's former and later secret reports and sent them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝對神武使詰乾。

translations.literal: The emperor had Shenwu's envoy interrogate Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Shenwu's envoy interrogate Qian.

sentences.zh: 乾曰：「臣以身奉國，義盡忠貞。

translations.literal: Qian said: "I have devoted my person to serving the state and exhausted righteousness in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "I have devoted my person to serving the state and exhausted righteousness in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 陛下既有異圖，更言臣反覆。

translations.literal: Your Majesty already harbors a different design, yet you say I have turned again.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already harbors a different design, yet you say I have turned again.

sentences.zh: 以匹夫加諸，尚或難免，況人主推惡，何以逃命？

translations.literal: When ordinary men impose charges, one can scarcely escape; how much less when the sovereign harbors ill will—how could one preserve one's life?
translations.idiomatic: When ordinary men impose charges, one can scarcely escape; how much less when the sovereign harbors ill will—how could one preserve one's life?

sentences.zh: 所謂欲加之罪，其無辭乎！

translations.literal: Is this not the saying, 'When one wishes to impose a crime, is there ever a lack of pretext?'
translations.idiomatic: Is this not the saying, 'When one wishes to impose a crime, is there ever a lack of pretext?'

sentences.zh: 功大身危，自昔然也。

translations.literal: Great merit brings peril to the person—thus it has always been.
translations.idiomatic: Great merit brings peril to the person—thus it has always been.

sentences.zh: 若死而有知，差無負莊帝。

translations.literal: If in death there is awareness, I shall be somewhat less unfaithful to Emperor Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: If in death there is awareness, I shall be somewhat less unfaithful to Emperor Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 」詔遂賜死于門下省，年三十七。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon ordered him to die by poison in the Secretariat Department; he was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon ordered him to die by poison in the Secretariat Department; he was thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 臨死時，武衛將軍元整監刑，謂曰：「頗有書及家人乎？

translations.literal: At the hour of death, General of the Martial Guard Yuan Zheng oversaw the execution and asked: "Do you have any writings or messages for your family?
translations.idiomatic: At the hour of death, General of the Martial Guard Yuan Zheng oversaw the execution and asked, "Do you have any writings or messages for your family?

sentences.zh: 」乾曰：「吾諸弟分張，各在異處，今日之事，想無全者。

translations.literal: Qian said: "My younger brothers are scattered, each in a different place; given today's affair, I think none will survive whole.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "My younger brothers are scattered, each in a different place; given today's affair, I think none will survive whole.

sentences.zh: 兒子既小，未有所識，亦恐巢傾卵破，夫欲何言！

translations.literal: My sons are still young and understand nothing; I also fear the nest overturns and the eggs are broken—what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: My sons are still young and understand nothing; I fear too that when the nest falls the eggs will be crushed—what more can I say!

sentences.zh: 」後神武討斛斯椿等，謂高昂曰：「若早用司空策，豈有今日之舉？

translations.literal: Later, when Shenwu campaigned against Husi Chun and others, he said to Gao Ang: "If we had earlier adopted the Minister of Works' plan, would we have today's effort?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Shenwu campaigned against Husi Chun and others, he said to Gao Ang, "If we had taken the Minister of Works' counsel sooner, would we be facing this campaign now?

sentences.zh: 」天平初，贈太師、錄尚書事、冀州刺史，諡曰文昭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianping era he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wen Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wen Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以長子繼叔襲祖次同樂城縣侯，令第二子呂兒襲乾爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jishu inherited grandfather Cikou's title Marquis of Lecheng County; his second son Lü'er inherited Qian's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jishu inherited his grandfather Cikou's title as Marquis of Lecheng County, and his second son Lü'er inherited Qian's rank.

sentences.zh: 乾弟慎，字仲密，頗涉文史，與兄弟志尚不同，偏為父所愛。

translations.literal: Qian's younger brother Shen, styled Zhongmi, was fairly versed in literature and history; his aspirations differed from his brothers', and his father favored him in particular.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's younger brother Shen, styled Zhongmi, had a fair grounding in literature and history. His ambitions differed from his brothers', and his father doted on him.

sentences.zh: 歷位滄州刺史、東南道行台尚書、光州刺史，加驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Governor of Cangzhou, Secretary of the Southeast Route Mobile Headquarters, and Governor of Guangzhou, and was further given the ranks of Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Honorary Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Governor of Cangzhou, Secretary of the Southeast Route Mobile Headquarters, and Governor of Guangzhou, and was further promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with Honorary Three Excellencies privileges.

sentences.zh: 時天下初定，聽慎以本鄉部曲數千自隨。

translations.literal: As the realm was newly settled, Shen was permitted to bring with him several thousand men from his home district as personal retainers.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm was newly pacified, Shen was allowed to take several thousand men from his home district as his personal following.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴酷，又縱左右，吏人苦之。

translations.literal: His governance was harsh and cruel, and he indulged his attendants; officials and commoners suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with harsh severity and indulged his attendants, and officials and commoners alike groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 乾死，仲密棄州，將歸神武。

translations.literal: When Qian died, Zhongmi abandoned his province and prepared to return to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian died, Zhongmi abandoned his province and set out to rejoin Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 武帝敕青州斷其歸路，慎間行至晉陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu ordered Qing Province to cut off his route home; Shen slipped through by hidden paths and reached Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered Qing Province to block his way home, but Shen stole through by back routes and reached Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 神武以為大行台左丞，轉尚書，當官無所回避。

translations.literal: Shenwu appointed him Left Assistant Director of the Great Mobile Headquarters, then transferred him to Secretary; in office he shirked nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu made him Left Assistant Director of the Great Mobile Headquarters, then transferred him to the Secretariat, where he handled every matter without evasion.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中尉，選用御史，多其親戚鄉閭，不稱朝望，文襄奏令改選焉。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Censor-in-Chief; in selecting censors he appointed many relatives and men of his home district, falling short of court expectations, and Wenxiang memorialized ordering a fresh selection.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Censor-in-Chief, but in choosing censors he favored relatives and men of his home district, falling short of what the court expected; Wenxiang memorialized for a new selection.

sentences.zh: 慎前妻，吏部郎中崔暹妹，為慎棄。

translations.literal: Shen's former wife was the younger sister of Bureau of Personnel Langzhong Cui Xian; Shen had cast her aside.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's first wife was the younger sister of Cui Xian, a Langzhong in the Bureau of Personnel; Shen had abandoned her.

sentences.zh: 暹時為文襄委任，乃為暹高嫁其妹，禮夕，親臨之。

translations.literal: Xian was then in Wenxiang's trust; Shen therefore arranged a splendid marriage for Xian's sister, and on the wedding night he attended in person.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was then in Wenxiang's confidence, so Shen arranged a grand remarriage for Xian's sister and attended the wedding night in person.

sentences.zh: 慎後妻趙郡李徽伯女也，豔且慧，兼善書記，工騎乘。

translations.literal: Shen's later wife was a daughter of Zhao commandery's Li Huibo; she was beautiful and clever, skilled at correspondence, and adept at horsemanship.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's second wife was a daughter of Li Huibo of Zhao commandery—beautiful and clever, skilled at correspondence, and expert in riding.

sentences.zh: 慎之為滄州，甚重沙門顯公，夜常語，久不寢。

translations.literal: When Shen governed Cangzhou, he held the monk Xiangong in high esteem and often talked with him deep into the night without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Cangzhou, Shen held the monk Xiangong in high regard and often talked with him far into the night without sleeping.

sentences.zh: 李氏患之，構之於慎，遂被拉殺。

translations.literal: Lady Li resented this and framed Xiangong before Shen; the monk was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li resented this, slandered Xiangong to Shen, and the monk was seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 文襄聞其美，挑之，不從，衣盡破裂。

translations.literal: Wenxiang heard of her beauty and tried to seduce her; she refused, and her clothes were torn to shreds.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang heard of her beauty and tried to force himself on her; she refused, and her clothes were torn to rags.

sentences.zh: 李以告慎，慎由是積憾，且謂暹構己，遂罕所糾劾，多行縱舍。

translations.literal: Li told Shen; Shen therefore harbored deep resentment, and believing Xian had framed him, he rarely prosecuted offenders and often showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Li told Shen, who nursed a deep grievance; believing Xian had set him up, he rarely prosecuted wrongdoing and often let offenders go.

sentences.zh: 神武嫌責之，彌不自安。

translations.literal: Shenwu reproached him with displeasure, and Shen grew only more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu rebuked him in displeasure, and Shen grew ever more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 出為北豫州刺史，遂據武牢降西魏。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of North Yuzhou and thereupon seized Wulao and surrendered to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Governor of North Yuzhou, then seized Wulao and defected to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 慎先入關，周文率眾東出，敗於芒山，慎妻子盡見禽。

translations.literal: Shen had entered the Pass first; Zhou Wen led troops east and was defeated at Mount Mang; Shen's wife and children were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had entered the Pass ahead of the army; Zhou Wen led troops east and was defeated at Mount Mang, and Shen's wife and children were all taken captive.

sentences.zh: 神武以其家勳，啟慎一房配沒而已。

translations.literal: Shenwu, considering the family's merit, reported that only Shen's household should be confiscated and enslaved.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu, honoring the family's past service, reported that only Shen's own household should be confiscated and enslaved.

sentences.zh: 仲密妻逆口行中，文襄盛服見之，乃從焉。

translations.literal: Zhongmi's wife was walking with a cloth covering her mouth; Wenxiang received her in full ceremonial dress, and she yielded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmi's wife walked with a cloth over her mouth; Wenxiang received her in full ceremonial dress, and she submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 西魏以慎為侍中、司徒，遷太尉。

translations.literal: Western Wei appointed Shen Palace Attendant and Minister of Education; he was promoted to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei appointed Shen Palace Attendant and Minister of Education, then promoted him to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 慎弟昂。

translations.literal: Shen's younger brother Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's younger brother Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂字敖曹。

translations.literal: Ang, styled Ao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, styled Ao Cao.

sentences.zh: 其母張氏，始生一男二歲，令婢為湯，將浴之。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Zhang had borne a son who at age two she ordered a maid to heat water and bathe him.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zhang, had borne a son; when he was two she ordered a maid to heat water and bathe him.

sentences.zh: 婢置而去，養猿系解，以兒投鼎中，爓而死。

translations.literal: The maid set it down and left; a pet monkey's tether came loose, and it threw the child into the cauldron, where he boiled to death.
translations.idiomatic: The maid set the water down and left; a pet monkey's tether came loose, and it threw the child into the cauldron, where he was scalded to death.

sentences.zh: 張使積薪於村外，縛婢及猿焚殺之，揚其灰于漳水，然後哭之。

translations.literal: Zhang had firewood piled outside the village, bound the maid and monkey, and burned them to death; she scattered their ashes on the Zhang River, and only then wept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had firewood piled outside the village, bound the maid and the monkey, and burned them alive; she scattered their ashes on the Zhang River, and only then did she weep.

sentences.zh: 昂性似其母，幼時便有壯氣。

translations.literal: Ang's temperament resembled his mother's; even as a child he had a fierce spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Ang took after his mother in temperament; even as a boy he had a bold, fierce spirit.

sentences.zh: 及長，俶儻，膽力過人，龍犀豹頸，姿體雄異。

translations.literal: When grown he was bold and unrestrained, with courage and strength surpassing others; dragon brow, rhinoceros forehead, leopard neck—his bearing was heroically unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he was bold and free-spirited, with courage and strength beyond ordinary men—dragon brow, rhinoceros forehead, leopard neck; his frame was heroically striking.

sentences.zh: 其父為求嚴師，令加捶撻。

translations.literal: His father sought a strict tutor for him and ordered that beatings be applied.
translations.idiomatic: His father found him a strict tutor and ordered that the rod be used freely.

sentences.zh: 昂不遵師訓，專事馳騁，每言：「男兒當橫行天下，自取富貴，誰能端坐讀書，作老博士也？

translations.literal: Ang did not follow the tutor's instruction and devoted himself to galloping about; he often said: "A man ought to sweep across the realm and win wealth and honor for himself—who can sit upright reading books and become some decrepit scholar?
translations.idiomatic: Ang ignored his tutor and gave himself over to riding hard; he often said, "A man should ride roughshod across the world and seize fortune for himself—who wants to sit bolt upright over books and end a doddering doctor of letters?

sentences.zh: 」其父曰：「此兒不滅吾族，當大吾門。

translations.literal: His father said: "This boy will not destroy our clan; he will enlarge our house.
translations.idiomatic: His father said, "This boy will not destroy our clan—he will enlarge our house.

sentences.zh: 」以其昂藏敖曹，故以名字之。

translations.literal: Because he was lofty and bold like an Ao Cao, they gave him that style name.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was lofty-spirited and fierce as an Ao Cao, they gave him that style name.

sentences.zh: 少與兄乾數為劫掠，鄉閭畏之，無敢違忤。

translations.literal: In youth he often joined his elder brother Qian in plundering raids; the home district feared them and none dared defy them.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he often joined his elder brother Qian in raiding and plunder; the countryside feared them, and none dared stand against them.

sentences.zh: 兄乾求博陵崔聖念女為婚，崔氏不許。

translations.literal: Elder brother Qian sought the daughter of Boling's Cui Shengnian in marriage; the Cui family refused.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Qian sought the daughter of Cui Shengnian of Boling in marriage, but the Cui family refused.

sentences.zh: 昂與兄往劫之，置女村外，謂兄曰：「何不行禮？

translations.literal: Ang went with his brother to abduct her, leaving the girl outside the village, and said to his brother: "Why not perform the rites?
translations.idiomatic: Ang went with his brother to seize her, left the girl outside the village, and said to his brother, "Why not go through with the rites?

sentences.zh: 」於是野合而歸。

translations.literal: And so they consummated the union in the open country and returned.
translations.idiomatic: So they consummated the marriage in the open country and returned home.

sentences.zh: 乾及昂等並劫掠，父次同常系獄中，唯遇赦乃出。

translations.literal: Qian, Ang, and the others all plundered; their father Cikou was often imprisoned and only emerged when an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, Ang, and the rest all plundered; their father Cikou was often in prison and only got out when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 次同語人曰：「吾四子皆五眼，我死後豈有人與我一鍬土邪？

translations.literal: Cikou told people: "My four sons all have five eyes; after I die, will anyone give me so much as a shovelful of earth?
translations.idiomatic: Cikou told people, "My four sons are all five-eyed men—when I die, will anyone throw me so much as a shovelful of earth?

sentences.zh: 」及次同死，昂大起塚。

translations.literal: When Cikou died, Ang raised a great tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: When Cikou died, Ang built him a great tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 對之曰：「老公！

translations.literal: Facing it he said: "Old man!
translations.idiomatic: Facing the mound he said, "Old man!

sentences.zh: 子生平畏不得一鍬土，今被壓，竟知為人不？」

translations.literal: All your life you feared you would not get one shovel of earth; now you're crushed beneath it—do you finally know what it means to be a man?"
