translations.idiomatic: All your life you feared you would not get a single shovelful of earth—now you're buried under a mountain of it. Do you finally know what it means to be a man?"

sentences.zh: 昂以建義初，兄弟共舉兵，既而奉魏莊帝旨散眾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, the brothers jointly raised troops; afterward they obeyed Emperor Zhuang of Wei's edict and dispersed their forces.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era the brothers raised troops together, then obeyed Emperor Zhuang of Wei's order and disbanded their forces.

sentences.zh: 仍除通直散騎侍郎，封武城縣伯。

translations.literal: Ang was then appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was then appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng County.

sentences.zh: 與兄乾俱為爾硃榮所黜，免歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He and elder brother Qian were both dismissed by Erzhu Rong and sent home stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Qian were both dismissed by Erzhu Rong and sent home without office.

sentences.zh: 陰養壯士，又行抄掠。

translations.literal: Secretly he nurtured stalwart men and again carried out raids.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he gathered bold men and took to raiding again.

sentences.zh: 榮聞惡之，密令刺史元仲宗誘執昂，即送晉陽。

translations.literal: Rong heard and detested this; he secretly ordered Governor Yuan Zhongzong to lure and seize Ang, who was immediately sent to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong heard of it and took offense; he secretly ordered Governor Yuan Zhongzong to lure Ang in and seize him, then had him sent at once to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及入洛，將昂自隨，禁于駝牛署。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang he took Ang with him and confined him in the Camel-Ox Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered Luoyang he brought Ang with him and held him in the Camel-Ox Office.

sentences.zh: 既而榮死，莊帝即引見勞勉之。

translations.literal: Before long Rong died; Emperor Zhuang immediately received Ang in audience and comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Rong was dead; Emperor Zhuang summoned Ang at once, consoled him, and praised his courage.

sentences.zh: 時爾硃世隆還逼宮闕，帝親臨大夏門指麾處分。

translations.literal: At that time Erzhu Shilong had returned and was pressing the palace; the emperor personally went to the Great Summer Gate to direct dispositions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Erzhu Shilong had turned back and was pressing the palace; the emperor went in person to the Great Summer Gate to direct the defense.

sentences.zh: 昂既免縲絏，被甲橫戈，與其從子長命，推鋒徑進，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Ang, freed from bonds, donned armor and levelled his spear; with his nephew Changming he drove straight forward, routing all before them.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, freed from his bonds, armored himself and levelled his spear; with his nephew Changming he charged straight ahead and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 帝及觀者，莫不壯之，即除直閣將軍，賜帛千疋。

translations.literal: The emperor and onlookers all admired his valor; Ang was immediately appointed General of the Direct Gate and granted a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and every onlooker admired his prowess; Ang was immediately made General of the Direct Gate and given a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 昂以寇難尚繁，乃請還本鄉招集部曲，仍除通直散騎常侍，加北平將軍。

translations.literal: As banditry and warfare were still widespread, Ang requested return to his home district to gather retainers; he was further appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Regular Attendance and given the additional post of General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: With rebellion still rife, Ang asked to return to his home district to raise a following; he was further appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Regular Attendance and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 及聞莊帝見害，京師不守，遂與父兄據信都起兵。

translations.literal: When he heard that Emperor Zhuang had been murdered and the capital could not be held, he joined his father and brothers in raising troops at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Emperor Zhuang had been killed and the capital could not be held, he joined his father and brothers in raising troops at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 爾硃世隆從叔殷州刺史羽生，率五千人掩至龍尾阪。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong's cousin Yusheng, Governor of Yin Province, led five thousand men in a surprise attack to Longwei Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong's cousin Yusheng, Governor of Yin Province, led five thousand men in a surprise strike against Longwei Slope.

sentences.zh: 昂將十餘騎，不擐甲而馳之。

translations.literal: Ang with a dozen horsemen charged without donning armor.
translations.idiomatic: Ang took a dozen horsemen and charged without bothering to arm himself.

sentences.zh: 乾城守，繩下五百人追救，未及而昂已交兵，羽生敗走。

translations.literal: Qian defended the city and lowered five hundred men by rope in pursuit; before they arrived Ang had already joined battle and Yusheng fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Qian held the city and lowered five hundred men by rope to reinforce him, but before they arrived Ang was already fighting and Yusheng fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 昂馬槊絕世，左右無不一當百，時人比之項籍。

translations.literal: Ang's mounted spearwork was unmatched; those around him were each worth a hundred men; men of the time compared him to Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's skill with the mounted spear was unmatched; each man at his side fought as if worth a hundred, and his contemporaries compared him to Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 神武至信都，開門奉迎。

translations.literal: When Shenwu reached Xindu, they opened the gates to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu reached Xindu, they opened the gates and welcomed him in.

sentences.zh: 昂時在外略地，聞之，以乾為婦人，遺以布裙。

translations.literal: Ang was then away securing territory; hearing of this, he treated Qian as a woman and sent him a cloth skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was away securing territory; when he heard of it he mocked Qian as a woman and sent him a cloth skirt.

sentences.zh: 神武使世子澄以子孫禮見之，昂乃與俱來。

translations.literal: Shenwu had his heir Cheng greet Ang with the rites due a grandson; Ang then came together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu had his heir Cheng receive Ang with the courtesy due a grandson, and Ang then came in with him.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝立，除冀州刺史以終其身。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor was installed, Ang was appointed Governor of Jizhou for life.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor was enthroned, Ang was appointed Governor of Jizhou for life.

sentences.zh: 仍為大都督，率眾從神武破爾硃兆于廣阿。

translations.literal: He also served as Grand Commander and led troops with Shenwu to defeat Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Grand Commander and led troops with Shenwu to defeat Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a.

sentences.zh: 又討四胡于韓陵。

translations.literal: He also campaigned against the Four Hu at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought the Four Hu at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 昂自領鄉人部曲王桃湯、東方老等三千人，神武將割鮮卑兵千餘人共相參合。

translations.literal: Ang personally led three thousand home-district retainers—Wang Taotang, Dongfang Lao, and others; Shenwu intended to detach more than a thousand Xianbei troops to mix them in together.
translations.idiomatic: Ang personally led three thousand home-district retainers—Wang Taotang, Dongfang Lao, and the rest; Shenwu meant to detach more than a thousand Xianbei soldiers and fold them into the unit.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「敖曹所將部曲，練習已久，不煩更配。

translations.literal: Ang replied: "The retainers Ao Cao leads have been drilled for long; there is no need to reassign them.
translations.idiomatic: Ang replied, "The men Ao Cao commands have been drilled together for years—there is no need to mix in others.

sentences.zh: 」神武從之。

translations.literal: Shenwu consented.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu agreed.

sentences.zh: 及戰，神武軍小卻，兆等方乘之。

translations.literal: When battle was joined, Shenwu's army gave slight ground and Zhao's forces were pressing their advantage.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, Shenwu's line gave a little ground and Zhao's men pressed hard.

sentences.zh: 昂與蔡俊以千騎自栗園出，橫擊，兆軍大敗。

translations.literal: Ang and Cai Jun with a thousand horsemen sallied from Liyuan and struck across their line; Zhao's army was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and Cai Jun with a thousand horsemen burst from Liyuan and struck across the enemy line; Zhao's army was smashed.

sentences.zh: 是日，微昂等，神武幾殆。

translations.literal: That day, but for Ang and the others, Shenwu would nearly have perished.
translations.idiomatic: That day, but for Ang and his men, Shenwu would almost certainly have been killed.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，始之冀州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, Ang first went to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era, Ang took up his post in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中、開府，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional posts of Palace Attendant and Grand Master of the Domain; his enfeoffment was raised to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further made Palace Attendant and Grand Master of the Domain, and his title was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 及兄乾被殺，乃將十餘騎奔晉陽。

translations.literal: When elder brother Qian was executed, he fled with a dozen horsemen to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Qian was executed, he fled with a dozen horsemen to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 神武向洛陽，令昂為前驅。

translations.literal: Shenwu marched on Luoyang and made Ang vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu marched on Luoyang and put Ang in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 武帝入關中，昂率五百騎倍道兼行，至崤、陝，不及而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong; Ang led five hundred horsemen by forced day-and-night marches as far as Xiao and Shan, but failing to overtake him, returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong; Ang led five hundred horsemen by forced marches to Xiao and Shan, but could not overtake him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 尋行豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was acting Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as acting Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 天平初，除侍中、司空公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was appointed Palace Attendant and Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was appointed Palace Attendant and Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 昂以兄乾薨此位，固辭不拜，轉司徒公。

translations.literal: Ang, because elder brother Qian had died in that office, firmly declined to accept it and was transferred to Duke over Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, because his elder brother Qian had died holding that office, firmly refused it and was transferred to Duke over Masses instead.

sentences.zh: 好著小帽，世因稱司徒帽。

translations.literal: He liked to wear a small cap; the world therefore called it the Duke of Masses' cap.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to wear a small cap, and people thereafter called it the Duke of Masses' cap.

sentences.zh: 神武以昂為西南道大都督，徑趣商、洛。

translations.literal: Shenwu made Ang Grand Commander of the Southwest Route and sent him directly toward Shang and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu made Ang Grand Commander of the Southwest Route and sent him straight toward Shangzhou and Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 昂度河祭河伯曰：「河伯，水中之神；

translations.literal: Ang crossed the river and sacrificed to the River Lord, saying: "River Lord, god of the waters;
translations.idiomatic: Ang crossed the river and made offering to the River Lord, saying, "River Lord, god of the waters—

sentences.zh: 高敖曹，地上之虎。

translations.literal: Gao Ao Cao, tiger upon the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ao Cao, tiger upon the earth.

sentences.zh: 行經君所，故相決醉。

translations.literal: Passing your domain, we therefore share a parting cup."
translations.idiomatic: I pass through your domain, and so we share a farewell cup."

sentences.zh: 」時山道峻阻，巴寇守險，昂轉鬥而進，莫有當鋒。

translations.literal: At that time the mountain paths were steep and blocked; Ba raiders held the passes; Ang fought his way forward in successive battles and none could meet his charge.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain roads were steep and narrow, and Ba bandits held the passes; Ang fought his way forward in battle after battle, and none could stand against his charge.

sentences.zh: 遂克上洛，獲西魏洛州刺史泉ＧＣ並將數十人，欲入藍田關。

translations.literal: He thereupon captured Shangluo, seized Western Wei's Governor of Luozhou Quan Qi along with several dozen officers, and intended to enter Lantian Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Shangluo, captured Western Wei's Governor of Luozhou Quan Qi along with several dozen commanders, and meant to push through Lantian Pass.

sentences.zh: 會竇泰失利，神武召昂。

translations.literal: As Dou Tai met defeat, Shenwu recalled Ang.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai's force was defeated, Shenwu recalled Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂不忍棄眾，力戰全軍而還。

translations.literal: Ang could not bear to abandon his troops; he fought hard and brought the whole army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Ang could not bear to leave his men behind; he fought his way out and brought the whole army back intact.

sentences.zh: 時昂為流矢所中，創甚，顧左右曰：「吾死無恨，恨不見季式作刺史耳！

translations.literal: At that time Ang was struck by a stray arrow and badly wounded; he turned to those beside him and said: "If I die I shall have no regret—only that I shall not see Jishi made governor!
translations.idiomatic: Ang had been hit by a stray arrow and was badly wounded; he turned to those beside him and said, "If I die I have no regret—only that I will not live to see Jishi made governor!

sentences.zh: 」神武聞之，馳驛啟季式為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Shenwu sent urgent dispatch to appoint Jishi Governor of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu heard this, he sent urgent word appointing Jishi Governor of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昂還，復為軍司、大都督，統七十六都督，與行台侯景練兵于武牢。

translations.literal: When Ang returned he again served as Army Director and Grand Commander, commanding seventy-six area commanders; with Mobile Headquarters chief Hou Jing he drilled troops at Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: When Ang returned he again served as Army Director and Grand Commander over seventy-six area commanders, and with Hou Jing of the Mobile Headquarters he drilled troops at Wulao.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉劉貴時亦率眾在焉。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Liu Gui was also leading troops there at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Liu Gui was also encamped there with his troops.

sentences.zh: 昂與北豫州刺史鄭嚴祖握槊，貴召嚴祖，昂不時遣，枷其使。

translations.literal: Ang and Governor of North Yuzhou Zheng Yanzu were playing shuo; Gui summoned Yanzu, but Ang did not send him promptly and put his messenger in the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and Zheng Yanzu, Governor of North Yuzhou, were playing spear-shuo; Gui summoned Yanzu, but Ang did not send him at once and put Gui's messenger in the cangue.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「枷時易，脫時難。

translations.literal: The messenger said: "Putting on the cangue is easy; taking it off is hard."
translations.idiomatic: The messenger said, "It is easy to put on the cangue, but hard to take it off."

sentences.zh: 」昂使以刀就枷刎之，曰：「何難之有？

translations.literal: Ang had a blade brought to the cangue and cut the man's throat, saying: "What difficulty is there in that?"
translations.idiomatic: Ang had a blade brought to the cangue and cut the man's throat, saying, "Where is the difficulty in that?"

sentences.zh: 」貴不敢校。

translations.literal: Gui did not dare contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui did not dare answer back.

sentences.zh: 明日，貴與昂坐，外白河役夫多溺死。

translations.literal: The next day, as Gui and Ang were seated together, a report came from outside that many laborers conscripted for river work had drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, as Gui and Ang sat together, word came from outside that many conscripted river laborers had drowned.

sentences.zh: 貴曰：「頭錢價漢，隨之死。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Buy Han men at the price of a head-tax coin—they die along with it."
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "You buy Han men for the price of a head-tax coin—they die right along with it."

sentences.zh: 」昂怒，拔刀斫貴。

translations.literal: Ang in anger drew his blade and hacked at Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Ang flew into a rage, drew his blade, and hacked at Gui.

sentences.zh: 貴走出還營，昂便鳴鼓會兵攻之。

translations.literal: Gui fled out and returned to camp; Ang at once beat the drums, gathered troops, and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui fled back to his camp; Ang immediately beat the drums, mustered his troops, and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 侯景與冀州刺史万俟受洛解之乃止。

translations.literal: Hou Jing and Governor of Jizhou Moqi Shouluo mediated and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing and Moqi Shouluo, Governor of Jizhou, intervened and brought the clash to an end.

sentences.zh: 時鮮卑共輕中華朝士，唯懌昂。

translations.literal: At that time the Xianbei together looked down on Han court officials; only Ang they respected.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xianbei as a whole looked down on Han court officials; only Ang did they hold in esteem.

sentences.zh: 神武每申令三軍，常為鮮卑言；

translations.literal: Whenever Shenwu issued orders to the three armies, he usually spoke in Xianbei;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shenwu issued orders to the three armies, he usually spoke in Xianbei;

sentences.zh: 昂若在列時，則為華言。

translations.literal: when Ang was present in the ranks, he spoke in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: but when Ang was present in the ranks, he spoke in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 昂嘗詣相府，欲直入，門者不聽，昂怒，引弓射之。

translations.literal: Ang once went to the chancellor's residence intending to enter directly; the gatekeepers would not allow it, and Ang in anger drew his bow and shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: Ang once went to the chancellor's residence and tried to walk straight in; the gatekeepers barred him, and Ang in a fury drew his bow and shot at them.

sentences.zh: 神武知而不責。

translations.literal: Shenwu knew of it but did not reprove him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu knew of it but did not rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 性好為詩，言甚陋鄙，神武每容之。

translations.literal: By nature he loved composing poetry; his words were very crude and vulgar, yet Shenwu always indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved to write poetry, though his verses were coarse and vulgar; Shenwu always indulged him all the same.

sentences.zh: 元年，進封京兆郡公，與侯景等同攻獨孤信于金墉。

translations.literal: In the first year of the reign he was advanced to Duke of Jingzhao Commandery and, together with Hou Jing and others, jointly attacked Dugu Xin at Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the reign he was promoted to Duke of Jingzhao Commandery and, together with Hou Jing and others, attacked Dugu Xin at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 與周文帝戰，敗于芒陰，死之。

translations.literal: He fought Emperor Wen of Zhou, was defeated at Mangyin, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Emperor Wen of Zhou, was defeated at Mangyin, and died in the battle.

sentences.zh: 是役也，昂使奴京兆候西軍。

translations.literal: In this campaign Ang sent his slave Jingzhao to watch the Western army.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Ang sent his slave Jingzhao to scout the Western army.

sentences.zh: 京兆于傅婢強取昂佩刀以行，昂執殺之。

translations.literal: Jingzhao forcibly took Ang's belt sword from a maid and set out; Ang seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao snatched Ang's belt sword from a maid and set off with it; Ang seized him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 京兆曰：「三度救公大急，何忍以小事賜殺？

translations.literal: Jingzhao said: "Three times I saved you in great peril—how can you bear to have me put to death over a trifle?
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao said, "Three times I saved you in mortal peril—how can you bear to have me killed over a trifle?

sentences.zh: 」其夜，夢京兆以血塗己。

translations.literal: That night he dreamed that Jingzhao smeared blood on him.
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed that Jingzhao smeared him with blood.

sentences.zh: 寤而怒，使折其二脛。

translations.literal: Awakening, he grew angry and had both his shins broken.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he flew into a rage and had both of Jingzhao's shins broken.

sentences.zh: 時劉桃棒在勃海，亦夢京兆言訴得理，將公付賊。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Taobang was in Bohai and also dreamed that Jingzhao said his grievance had been heard and that he would deliver the lord to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Taobang was in Bohai and also dreamed that Jingzhao said his grievance had been upheld and that he would deliver his master to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 桃棒知昂必死，遽奔焉。

translations.literal: Taobang knew Ang would surely die and hurriedly rushed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Taobang knew Ang was doomed and hurried to join him.

sentences.zh: 昂心輕敵，建旗蓋以陵陣，西人盡銳攻之，一軍皆沒。

translations.literal: Ang in his heart underrated the enemy; he raised banners and canopies to storm the enemy line; the Westerners brought their full strength against him, and the whole army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Ang underestimated the enemy; he raised banners and canopies and charged the enemy line, but the Westerners brought their full strength against him and his whole army was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 昂輕騎東走河陽城，太守高永洛先與昂隙，閉門不受。

translations.literal: Ang fled east on light horse to Heyang City; the prefect Gao Yongluo had long been at odds with Ang and shut the gates, refusing him entry.
translations.idiomatic: Ang fled east on a light horse to Heyang City, but Prefect Gao Yongluo, who had long been at odds with him, shut the gates and refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 昂仰呼求繩，又不得，拔刀穿闔，未徹，而追兵至。

translations.literal: Ang looked up and cried for a rope but could not obtain one; he drew his blade to pierce the gate, but before he broke through the pursuers arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Ang looked up and cried for a rope but could get none; he drew his blade to hack through the gate, but before he broke through the pursuers were upon him.

sentences.zh: 伏於橋下。

translations.literal: He hid beneath a bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He hid beneath a bridge.

sentences.zh: 追者見其從奴持金帶，問昂所在，奴示之。

translations.literal: The pursuers saw his attendant slave holding a gold belt, asked where Ang was, and the slave pointed him out.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers saw his attendant holding a gold belt, asked where Ang was, and the slave pointed him out.

sentences.zh: 昂奮頭曰：「來，與爾開國公！

translations.literal: Ang thrust out his head and said: "Come—I'll make you a Duke Who Founds a State!
translations.idiomatic: Ang thrust out his head and cried, "Come here—I'll make you a Duke Who Founds a State!

sentences.zh: 」追者斬之以去。

translations.literal: The pursuers beheaded him and left.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers cut off his head and rode away.

sentences.zh: 先是，昂夢為此奴所殺，以告盧武，將殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier Ang had dreamed that this slave would kill him; he told Lu Wu and was about to kill the slave.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ang had dreamed that this slave would kill him; he told Lu Wu and was about to kill the man.

sentences.zh: 武諫乃止，果及難。

translations.literal: Wu remonstrated and he stopped; in the end the disaster came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Wu dissuaded him and he desisted; in the end disaster came to pass as foretold.

sentences.zh: 時年四十八。

translations.literal: He was then forty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 桃棒會喪于路。

translations.literal: Taobang met the funeral procession on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Taobang met the funeral procession on the road.

sentences.zh: 神武聞之，如喪肝膽，杖永洛二百。

translations.literal: When Shenwu heard of it he felt as though he had lost his liver and gall; he had Yongluo beaten two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu heard of it he was stricken as though he had lost his very heart; he had Yongluo beaten two hundred strokes with the rod.

sentences.zh: 西魏賞斬昂首者布絹萬段，歲歲稍與之，周亡猶未充。

translations.literal: Western Wei rewarded the man who beheaded Ang with ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, paying it out little by little year after year; even when Zhou fell the reward had not been fully paid.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei promised the man who beheaded Ang ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, paying it out in installments year after year; even when the Zhou dynasty fell the reward had still not been fully paid.

sentences.zh: 贈太師、大司馬、太尉公、錄尚書事、冀州刺史，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Grand Marshal, Duke of Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Zhong Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Grand Marshal, Duke of Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 西魏尋歸敖曹首，猶可識。

translations.literal: Western Wei soon returned Ao Cao's head; it could still be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei soon returned Ao Cao's head, and it was still recognizable.

sentences.zh: 先是，有鵲巢於庭中地上，家人怪之，及其首函至，置正當巢處。

translations.literal: Earlier a magpie had built its nest on the ground in the courtyard; the household thought it strange, and when the casket with his head arrived it was set down exactly where the nest had been.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a magpie had built its nest on the ground in the courtyard; the household found it strange, and when the casket bearing his head arrived it was placed exactly where the nest had been.

sentences.zh: 葬後，其妻張氏常見敖曹夜來旦去，有若生平。

translations.literal: After the burial his wife Lady Zhang often saw Ao Cao come at night and leave at dawn, just as in life.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial his wife, Lady Zhang, often saw Ao Cao arrive at night and leave at dawn, just as in life.

sentences.zh: 傍人莫見，唯犬隨而吠之，歲餘乃絕。

translations.literal: Those beside her saw nothing; only the dog followed and barked at him; after more than a year it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: No one else saw him; only the dog followed and barked at him. After more than a year the visitations ceased.

sentences.zh: 其故吏東方老為南兗州刺史，追慕其恩，為立祠廟。

translations.literal: His former subordinate Dongfang Lao, serving as Governor of South Yanzhou, cherishing his kindness, built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: His former subordinate Dongfang Lao, then Governor of South Yanzhou, cherishing his kindness, built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 靈像既成，頭上坼裂，改而更作，裂如初，見者咸稱神異。

translations.literal: Once the spirit image was completed, the head split open; it was remade, yet split again as before; all who saw it called it miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: Once the spirit image was completed, the head split open; it was remade, yet split again as before, and all who saw it declared it miraculous.

sentences.zh: 子突騎嗣，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Tuqi succeeded but died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuqi succeeded him but died young.

sentences.zh: 文襄復親簡昂諸子，以第三子道額嗣。

translations.literal: Wenxiang again personally selected among Ang's sons and had his third son Daoe succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang again personally chose among Ang's sons and had his third son, Daoe, succeed.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，追封昂永昌王，以道額襲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huangjian era Ang was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yongchang, and Daoe inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangjian era Ang was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yongchang, and Daoe inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武平末，開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuping era he held the rank of Honorary Three Excellencies with the Opening of a Government Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuping era he held the rank of Honorary Three Excellencies with the privilege of maintaining a full staff.

sentences.zh: 入周，為儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: After entering Zhou he became General of Honorary Equivalence.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou conquered Qi he became General of Honorary Equivalence.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于黃州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as Governor of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as Governor of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 昂弟季式，字子通，亦有膽氣。

translations.literal: Ang's younger brother Jishi, styled Zitong, likewise had courage and mettle.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's younger brother Jishi, styled Zitong, likewise had courage and fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，累遷尚食典禦，尋加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taichang era he was promoted in succession to Palace Provisioner and soon given the additional rank of Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era he rose in succession to Palace Provisioner and was soon further promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天平中，為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Tianping era he served as Governor of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he served as Governor of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 季式兄弟貴盛，並有勳于時，自領部曲千餘人，馬八百疋，衣甲器仗皆備，故能追督境內賊盜，多致克捷。

translations.literal: The Jishi brothers were noble and powerful and both had merit at the time; each led more than a thousand personal retainers, eight hundred horses, and was fully equipped with armor and weapons, and so could pursue and suppress bandits within their territories, often achieving victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Jishi brothers were powerful and honored, and both had won distinction in their day; each commanded more than a thousand personal retainers and eight hundred horses, with armor and weapons fully supplied, and so could hunt down bandits within their territories and often win decisive victories.

sentences.zh: 時濮陽人杜靈椿等，又陽平路叔文徒党各為亂，季式並討平之。

translations.literal: At that time Du Lingchun of Puyang and the factions of Lu Shuwen of Yangping and others each raised disturbances; Jishi suppressed and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Lingchun of Puyang and the factions of Lu Shuwen of Yangping and others each raised disturbances, and Jishi put them all down.

sentences.zh: 有客嘗謂季式曰：「濮陽、陽平乃是畿內，何忽遣私軍遠戰？

translations.literal: A guest once said to Jishi: "Puyang and Yangping lie within the capital region—why suddenly send private troops to fight far away?
translations.idiomatic: A guest once said to Jishi, "Puyang and Yangping lie within the capital region—why do you suddenly dispatch private troops to fight so far afield?

sentences.zh: 」季式曰：「我與國家同安危，豈有見賊不討之理？

translations.literal: Jishi said: "I share safety and peril with the state—how could there be any principle of seeing bandits and not attacking them?
translations.idiomatic: Jishi said, "I share the state's safety and peril—how could I see bandits and not attack them?

sentences.zh: 若以此獲罪，吾亦無恨。」

translations.literal: If I am punished for this, I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: If I am punished for this, I shall have no regret."

sentences.zh: 芒山之敗，所親部曲請季式奔梁。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Mang Mountain, his close personal retainers urged Jishi to flee to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Mang Mountain, his close retainers urged Jishi to flee to Liang.

sentences.zh: 季式曰：「吾兄弟受國厚恩，與高王共定天下，一旦傾危而亡之，不義。

translations.literal: Jishi said: "We brothers have received great favor from the state and, together with Prince Gao, settled the realm—once it is imperiled to abandon it and flee would be unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi said, "We brothers have received great favor from the state and, together with Prince Gao, helped settle the realm—to flee once it is imperiled would be unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 」是役也，兄昂歿焉。

translations.literal: In this campaign his elder brother Ang perished.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle his elder brother Ang was killed.

sentences.zh: 興和中，行晉州事。

translations.literal: During the Xinghe era he acted as governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era he served as acting governor of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 解州，仍鎮永安。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the prefecture he still garrisoned Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the post he continued to garrison Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 季式兄慎以武牢叛，遣信報季式。

translations.literal: Jishi's elder brother Shen rebelled at Wulao and sent word to inform Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi's elder brother Shen rebelled at Wulao and sent word to Jishi.

sentences.zh: 季式奔告神武，神武待之如初。

translations.literal: Jishi rushed to inform Shenwu; Shenwu treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi rushed to inform Shenwu, and Shenwu treated him exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 武定中，除侍中，尋加冀州大中正、都督。

translations.literal: During the Wuding era he was appointed Palace Attendant and soon given the additional posts of Chief Rectifier of Jizhou and Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he was appointed Palace Attendant and soon given the additional posts of Chief Rectifier of Jizhou and Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: For his successive merits he was given Honorary Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: For his successive achievements he was granted Honorary Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封乘氏縣子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chengsi County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chengsi County.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 仍為都督，隨司徒潘樂征江、淮間。

translations.literal: He again served as Area Commander and followed Minister of Education Pan Yue in campaigning between the Yangzi and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Area Commander and followed Minister of Education Pan Yue on campaign between the Yangzi and the Huai.

sentences.zh: 為私使樂人於邊境交易，還京，坐被禁止。

translations.literal: He privately sent musicians to trade at the border; on returning to the capital he was punished by confinement.
translations.idiomatic: He had sent musicians privately to trade at the border; on returning to the capital he was placed under detention for it.

sentences.zh: 尋赦之。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，發疽卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, summer, he died of a carbuncle.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he died of a carbuncle.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、開府儀同三司、冀州刺史，諡曰恭穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Honorary Three Excellencies with the Opening of a Government Office, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Gong Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Honorary Three Excellencies with the privilege of maintaining a full staff, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Reverent and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 季式豪率好酒，又恃舉家勳功，不拘檢節。

translations.literal: Jishi was bold and unrestrained and loved wine; he also relied on his family's collective merit and did not restrain himself by propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi was bold, free-spirited, and fond of wine; he also relied on his family's collective merit and paid little heed to propriety.

sentences.zh: 與光州刺史李元忠生平遊款。

translations.literal: He had been on intimate terms all his life with Li Yuanzhong, Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had been close friends all his life with Li Yuanzhong, Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在濟州夜飲，憶元忠，開城門，令左右乘驛馬持一壺酒往光州勸之。

translations.literal: While drinking at night in Ji Prefecture he thought of Yuanzhong, opened the city gate, and ordered his attendants to ride post horses carrying a jar of wine to Guang Prefecture to urge him to drink.
translations.idiomatic: One night while drinking in Ji Prefecture he thought of Yuanzhong, opened the city gates, and sent attendants on post horses with a jar of wine to Guang Prefecture to share a cup with him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知而容之。

translations.literal: The court knew of it and indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew of it and indulged him.

sentences.zh: 兄慎叛後，少時解職。

translations.literal: After his elder brother Shen rebelled, he was briefly removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After his elder brother Shen's rebellion he was briefly removed from office.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎司馬消難，左僕射子如之子，又是神武婿，勢盛當時。

translations.literal: Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Sima Xiaonan was the son of Left Vice Director of the Masters of Execution Ziru and also Shenwu's son-in-law; his power was great at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, was the son of Left Vice Director of the Masters of Execution Ziru and also Shenwu's son-in-law; his influence was immense at the time.

sentences.zh: 因退食暇，尋季式，酣歌留宿。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of leisure after the evening meal, he sought out Jishi, sang drunkenly, and stayed the night.
translations.idiomatic: One evening after the meal he sought out Jishi, drank and sang with abandon, and stayed the night.

sentences.zh: 旦日，重門並關，消難固請去。

translations.literal: At dawn every gate was shut; Xiaonan repeatedly begged to leave.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn every gate was barred shut; Xiaonan repeatedly begged to be let out.

sentences.zh: 季式曰：「君以地勢脅我邪？

translations.literal: Jishi said: "Are you trying to coerce me with your territorial position?
translations.idiomatic: Jishi said, "Are you trying to threaten me with your territorial power?

sentences.zh: 」消難拜謝請出，終不見許。

translations.literal: Xiaonan bowed in apology and asked to go out, but in the end permission was never granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan bowed in apology and begged to leave, but Jishi would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 酒至，不肯飲。

translations.literal: When wine was brought he refused to drink.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was brought he refused to drink.

sentences.zh: 季式索車輪括消難頸，又更索一車輪自括頸，引滿相勸。

translations.literal: Jishi fetched wagon wheel rims to encircle Xiaonan's neck, then fetched another rim and encircled his own neck, and with cups filled urged each other to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi fetched wagon wheel rims and looped one around Xiaonan's neck, then fetched another and looped it around his own, and with brimming cups urged each other to drink.

sentences.zh: 消難不得已，笑而從之。

translations.literal: Xiaonan had no choice and, laughing, complied.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan had no choice and, laughing, went along with it.

sentences.zh: 方俱脫車輪，更留一宿。

translations.literal: Just as they both removed the wheel rims, he kept him another night.
translations.idiomatic: Just as they both removed the wheel rims, Jishi kept him another night.

sentences.zh: 及消難出，方具言之。

translations.literal: Only when Xiaonan got out did he tell the whole story in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Xiaonan was released did he tell the whole story in detail.

sentences.zh: 文襄輔政，白魏帝，賜消難美酒數石，珍羞十輿，並令朝士與季式親狎者，就季式宅宴集。

translations.literal: While Wenxiang assisted in government he reported to the Wei emperor, bestowed on Xiaonan several shi of fine wine and ten carts of delicacies, and also ordered court officials who were on intimate terms with Jishi to gather for a banquet at Jishi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: While Wenxiang was regent he reported to the Wei emperor, bestowed on Xiaonan several shi of fine wine and ten cartloads of delicacies, and also ordered court officials who were close to Jishi to gather for a banquet at his residence.

sentences.zh: 其被優遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 自昂起兵，為羽翼者，有呼延族、劉貴珍、劉長秋、東方老、劉士榮、成五彪、韓願生、劉桃棒。

translations.literal: From the time Ang raised troops, those who served as his wings were Huyan Zu, Liu Guizhen, Liu Changqiu, Dongfang Lao, Liu Shirong, Cheng Wubiao, Han Yuansheng, and Liu Taobang.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Ang raised troops, those who served as his wings included Huyan Zu, Liu Guizhen, Liu Changqiu, Dongfang Lao, Liu Shirong, Cheng Wubiao, Han Yuansheng, and Liu Taobang.

sentences.zh: 隨其建義者，有李希光、劉叔宗、劉孟和等。

translations.literal: Those who followed his righteous uprising included Li Xiguang, Liu Shuzong, Liu Menghe, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Those who rallied to his righteous cause included Li Xiguang, Liu Shuzong, Liu Menghe, and others.

sentences.zh: 名顯可知者，列之後云。

translations.literal: Those whose names are clearly known are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose names are clearly known are listed below.

sentences.zh: 東方老，安德鬲人，與昂為部曲。

translations.literal: Dongfang Lao, a man of Ande in Ge County, was a retainer of Ang's.
translations.idiomatic: Dongfang Lao, a man of Ande in Ge County, had been a retainer in Ang's service.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，封陽平縣伯，位南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan received the abdication he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yangping County and held the post of Governor of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yangping County and appointed Governor of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 後與蕭軌等度江，沒。

translations.literal: Later he crossed the Yangzi with Xiao Gui and others and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Later he crossed the Yangzi with Xiao Gui and others and was killed.

sentences.zh: 李希光，勃海蓚人，初隨高乾起兵，後位儀同三司、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Xiguang, a man of Tiao in Bohai, at first followed Gao Gan in raising troops; later he held the ranks of Honorary Three Excellencies and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiguang, a native of Tiao in Bohai, had first followed Gao Gan in raising troops; later he rose to Honorary Three Excellencies and Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文宣責陳武帝廢蕭明，命儀同蕭軌率希光、東方老、裴英起、王敬寶步騎數萬，以天保七年三月度江，襲克石頭城。

translations.literal: Wenxuan reproached Emperor Wu of Chen for deposing Xiao Ming and ordered Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes Xiao Gui to lead Xiguang, Dongfang Lao, Pei Yingqi, and Wang Jingbao with several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry; in the third month of the seventh year of Tianbao they crossed the Yangzi and stormed and captured Shitou City.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan reproached Emperor Wu of Chen for deposing Xiao Ming and ordered Xiao Gui, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, to lead Xiguang, Dongfang Lao, Pei Yingqi, and Wang Jingbao with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry; in the third month of the seventh year of Tianbao they crossed the Yangzi and stormed Shitou City.

sentences.zh: 五將名位相侔，英起以侍中為軍司，蕭軌與希光並為都督。

translations.literal: The five generals were equal in name and rank; Yingqi served as Army Director in his capacity as Palace Attendant, and Xiao Gui and Xiguang were both Area Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The five generals were equal in rank and standing; Yingqi served as Army Director in his capacity as Palace Attendant, while Xiao Gui and Xiguang were both area commanders.

sentences.zh: 軍中抗禮，動必乖張。

translations.literal: In the army they refused to defer to one another, and every move was perverse and discordant.
translations.idiomatic: In the army they refused to defer to one another, and every move bred discord.

sentences.zh: 頓軍丹楊城下，遇霖雨五十餘日，故致敗。

translations.literal: They encamped below Danyang City, encountered more than fifty days of steady rain, and so met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They encamped below Danyang City, were battered by more than fifty days of steady rain, and so met defeat.

sentences.zh: 將卒俱死，軍士得還者十二三。

translations.literal: Generals and soldiers alike died; of the troops only one or two in ten returned.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men alike perished; only one or two soldiers in ten made it back.

sentences.zh: 劉叔宗名纂，樂陵平昌人，歸昂，位車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Liu Shuzong, personal name Zuan, a man of Pingchang in Leling, submitted to Ang and held the posts of General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shuzong, personal name Zuan, a native of Pingchang in Leling, submitted to Ang and rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 劉孟和名協，浮陽饒安人，聚眾附昂兄弟，位終大丞相司馬，坐事死。

translations.literal: Liu Menghe, personal name Xie, a man of Rao'an in Fuyang, gathered a force and attached himself to the Ang brothers; he ended as Marshal to the Grand Chancellor and died for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Menghe, personal name Xie, a native of Rao'an in Fuyang, gathered followers and attached himself to the Ang brothers; he eventually became Marshal to the Grand Chancellor and was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 其餘並不知所終云。

translations.literal: As for the rest, their final fates are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest, their final fates are unknown.

sentences.zh: 神武初起兵，范陽盧曹亦以勇力稱，為爾硃氏守，據薊。

translations.literal: When Shenwu first raised troops, Lu Cao of Fanyang was also famed for courage and strength; he served as a defender for the Erzhu clan and held Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu first raised troops, Lu Cao of Fanyang was also famed for courage and strength; he had served the Erzhu clan as a defender and held Ji.

sentences.zh: 神武厚禮召之，以昂相擬，曰：「宜來，與從叔為二曹。

translations.literal: Shenwu summoned him with generous courtesy, comparing him to Ang, and said: "You should come and be the two Caos with your junior uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu summoned him with generous courtesy, comparing him to Ang, and said, "You should come and stand as the two Caos with your junior uncle.

sentences.zh: 」曹慍曰：「將田舍兒比國士。

translations.literal: Cao in anger said: "You compare a farm boy to a champion of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Cao said angrily, "You compare a farm boy to a champion of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」遂率其徒自薊入海島。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his followers from Ji out to a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he led his followers from Ji out to a sea island.

sentences.zh: 得長人骨，以髑髏為馬皁；

translations.literal: He obtained the bones of a giant man and used the skull as a horse manger;
translations.idiomatic: He found the bones of a giant and used the skull as a horse manger;

sentences.zh: 脛長丈六尺，以為二槊。

translations.literal: the shins were one zhang and six chi long and were made into two spears.
translations.idiomatic: the shins, a full zhang and six chi long, he fashioned into two spears.

sentences.zh: 送其一于神武，諸將莫能用，唯彭樂強舉之。

translations.literal: He sent one to Shenwu; none of the generals could wield it—only Peng Yue could raise it by force.
translations.idiomatic: He sent one spear to Shenwu; none of the generals could wield it—only Peng Yue could lift it by main force.

sentences.zh: 未幾，曹遇疾，恫聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Before long Cao fell ill; his groans could be heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cao fell ill, and his groans could be heard outside.

sentences.zh: 巫言海神為崇，遂卒。

translations.literal: A shaman said the Sea God was afflicting him, and he thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman said the Sea God was tormenting him, and he died.

sentences.zh: 其徒五百人皆服斬衰，葬畢潛散。

translations.literal: His five hundred followers all wore the hemp mourning of the closest degree; after the burial they secretly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: His five hundred followers all wore the deepest mourning hemp; after the burial they quietly dispersed.

sentences.zh: 曹身長九尺，鬢面甚雄，臂毛逆如豬鬣，力能拔樹。

translations.literal: Cao was nine chi tall; his beard and face were very formidable; the hair on his arms grew against the grain like boar bristles; his strength could uproot trees.
translations.idiomatic: Cao stood nine chi tall; his beard and face were formidable; the hair on his arms grew against the grain like boar bristles, and his strength was enough to uproot trees.

sentences.zh: 性弘毅方重，常從客雅服，北州敬仰之。

translations.literal: By nature he was magnanimous, resolute, and dignified; he often wore elegant attire as a guest would, and the northern provinces revered him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was magnanimous, resolute, and dignified; he often dressed with elegant restraint, and the northern provinces revered him.

sentences.zh: 嘗臥疾，猶申足以舉二人。

translations.literal: Once when he lay ill he could still extend a foot and lift two men.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he lay ill he could still stretch out a leg and lift two men.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕寇范陽，曹登城射之，矢出三百步，投弓於外，群虜莫能彎，乃去之。

translations.literal: When the Rouran raided Fanyang, Cao mounted the wall and shot at them; his arrows flew three hundred paces; he cast his bow outside the wall, and none of the barbarians could draw it, whereupon they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided Fanyang, Cao mounted the wall and shot at them; his arrows carried three hundred paces; he cast his bow outside the wall, and none of the raiders could draw it, whereupon they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時有沙門曇贊，號為神力，唯曹與之角焉。

translations.literal: At that time there was a monk named Tanzan, famed for divine strength; only Cao could match him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a monk named Tanzan, famed for divine strength; only Cao could match him.

sentences.zh: 曇贊聞叫聲則勝。

translations.literal: When Tanzan heard shouting he would win.
translations.idiomatic: When Tanzan heard shouting he would win.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高允踐危禍之機，抗雷電之氣，處死夷然，忘身濟難，卒悟明主，保己全名。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Gao Yun trod the brink of peril and disaster, withstood the force of thunder and lightning, faced death with calm, forgot himself to rescue others from difficulty, and in the end won the understanding of a wise ruler and preserved himself with his reputation intact.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Gao Yun stood at the brink of peril and disaster, withstood the force of thunder and lightning, faced death with calm composure, forgot himself to rescue others from difficulty, and in the end won a wise ruler's understanding and preserved both his life and his good name.

sentences.zh: 自非體鄰知命，鑒昭窮達，亦何能若此。

translations.literal: Had he not been one whose inner nature partook of knowing fate and whose discernment illuminated rise and fall, how could he have done thus?
translations.idiomatic: Had his inner nature not partaken of knowing fate, and had his discernment not illuminated rise and fall, how could he have done thus?

sentences.zh: 宜光寵四世，終享百齡。

translations.literal: It was fitting that honor should shine upon four generations and that he should enjoy a lifespan of a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: It was fitting that honor should shine upon four generations and that he should live to a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 有魏以來，斯人而已。

translations.literal: Since the Wei dynasty, this man alone.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei, there has been no one like him.

sentences.zh: 僧裕藝用有聞，聿修之義。

translations.literal: Sengyu was known for his arts and abilities and for upholding the principle of continual cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyu was known for his arts and abilities and upheld the principle of continual self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 世禮貪而無道，能無及乎？

translations.literal: Shili was greedy and without the Way—how could he not come to ruin?
translations.idiomatic: Shili was greedy and without the Way—how could he not come to ruin?

sentences.zh: 子集學業優道，知名前世，儒俊之風，門舊不殞。

translations.literal: Ziji's learning excelled in the Way; he was famed among forebears; the manner of Confucian worthies—the family's old standing did not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Ziji's learning excelled in the Way; he was famed among forebears; the manner of Confucian worthies endured, and the family's old standing did not perish.

sentences.zh: 德正受終之際，契協亂臣，雖鐘淫虐，而名亦茂矣！

translations.literal: At the time of receiving the abdication Dezheng joined with rebellious ministers; though he met with wanton cruelty, his fame was still great!
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the abdication Dezheng joined with rebellious ministers; though he met with wanton cruelty, his fame was still great!

sentences.zh: 乾邕兄弟，不階尺土之資，奮臂河朔，自致勤王之舉，神武因之，以成霸業。

translations.literal: The Qian-Ou brothers, without inheriting so much as a foot of land, raised their arms in Heshuo, brought about the righteous campaign to rescue the ruler, and Shenwu relied on them to achieve his hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: The Qian-Ou brothers, without inheriting so much as a foot of land, raised their arms in Heshuo, brought about the righteous campaign to rescue the ruler, and Shenwu relied on them to achieve his hegemony.

sentences.zh: 但以非潁川元從，異豐沛故人，腹心之寄，有所未允。

translations.literal: But because they were not original followers from Yingchuan, unlike the old companions from Fengpei, entrusting them with innermost counsels was not wholly approved.
translations.idiomatic: But because they were not original followers from Yingchuan, unlike the old companions from Fengpei, entrusting them with one's innermost counsels was never wholly approved.

sentences.zh: 露其啟疏，假手天誅，枉濫之極，莫或過此。

translations.literal: Exposing their memorials, borrowing Heaven's punishment—the height of injustice, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Exposing their memorials and borrowing Heaven's punishment to destroy them—nothing surpasses this in injustice.

sentences.zh: 昂之膽力，氣冠萬夫，韓陵之下，風飛電擊。

translations.literal: Ang's courage and strength crowned ten thousand men; below Hanling he swept like wind and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's courage and strength topped ten thousand men; below Hanling he swept like wind and lightning.

sentences.zh: 然則齊氏元功，一門而已。

translations.literal: Thus the paramount merit of the Qi house rested in one clan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the paramount merit of the Qi house rested in one clan alone.

sentences.zh: 其餘托而義唱，亦足稱云。

translations.literal: The rest who rallied to his righteous standard also merit mention.
translations.idiomatic: The rest who rallied to his righteous standard also merit mention.
